sec02-card-sec02-F01.front: Which roadway signs, signals, and pavement markings must you obey, and who can override them?
sec02-card-sec02-F01.expected_back: You must obey every official sign, signal and pavement marking, except when a police officer or road worker directs traffic differently.

sec02-card-sec02-F02.front: How can you recognize what family a road sign belongs to at a glance even when it uses symbols instead of words?
sec02-card-sec02-F02.expected_back: Signs often use pictures or symbols instead of words, and each sign family has its own color and shape so you can identify it at a glance.

sec02-card-sec02-F03.front: What color are prohibitive regulatory signs, and what two jobs do they perform?
sec02-card-sec02-F03.expected_back: Prohibitive regulatory signs are red; they forbid certain actions and help control traffic moving through intersections.

sec02-card-sec02-R02.front: What rule does an octagon, a triangle, and a square red sign each communicate by shape alone?
sec02-card-sec02-R02.memory_hook: Octagon stops, triangle yields, square blocks
sec02-card-sec02-R02.expected_back: The octagon means stop, the triangle means yield and the square red sign means Do Not Enter, so the shape alone tells you which rule applies.

sec02-card-sec02-F04.front: What steps must you complete at an eight-sided stop sign before pulling into the intersection?
sec02-card-sec02-F04.expected_back: At an eight-sided stop sign, stop completely, yield to other vehicles, and wait for anyone in a marked or unmarked crosswalk; then enter when it is safe.

sec02-card-sec02-F05.front: What actions does a triangular yield sign require as you approach intersecting traffic?
sec02-card-sec02-F05.memory_hook: Slow down, yield, stop if needed
sec02-card-sec02-F05.expected_back: A triangular yield sign means slow down and give the right of way, stopping just as you would at a stop sign if that is needed.

sec02-card-sec02-R01.front: How does the stopping requirement at a stop sign differ from the requirement at a yield sign?
sec02-card-sec02-R01.memory_hook: Stop every time, yield stops conditionally
sec02-card-sec02-R01.expected_back: A stop sign always requires a full stop, while a yield sign requires slowing and giving way, with a stop only when traffic or pedestrians make it necessary.

sec02-card-sec02-F06.front: What command does a square Do Not Enter sign give, and what does seeing one usually mean?
sec02-card-sec02-F06.memory_hook: Do Not Enter means wrong way
sec02-card-sec02-F06.expected_back: A square Do Not Enter sign tells you not to enter that road or freeway, and seeing it usually means you are heading the wrong way.

sec02-card-sec02-F07.front: What does a red circle with a diagonal slash across a turn arrow tell you?
sec02-card-sec02-F07.expected_back: A red circle with a slash across a turn symbol, as on No Left Turn, No Right Turn and No U Turn signs, means you may not make the turn shown.

sec02-card-sec02-F08.front: What do non-red regulatory signs look like, and where are they placed along the road?
sec02-card-sec02-F08.expected_back: Other regulatory signs are rectangles with black words or symbols on white; they tell you what to do and stand at or near the place the rule applies.

sec02-card-sec02-F09.front: What does a speed limit sign tell you, and how can electronic versions behave?
sec02-card-sec02-F09.memory_hook: Top miles per hour, may adjust
sec02-card-sec02-F09.expected_back: A speed limit sign gives the maximum speed in miles per hour, and electronic versions may change with current conditions.

sec02-card-sec02-F10.front: Which way may vehicles travel on a street marked as a one-way road?
sec02-card-sec02-F10.expected_back: On a one-way road, traffic may travel only in the direction the arrow points.

sec02-card-sec02-F11.front: What does a Right Turn Permitted Without Stopping sign allow, and what must all other drivers still do?
sec02-card-sec02-F11.expected_back: A Right Turn Permitted Without Stopping sign, sometimes under a stop sign, lets right-turning traffic go without stopping while all other traffic must stop and yield.

sec02-card-sec02-F17.front: What do a Do Not Pass sign and a No Turn on Red sign each forbid?
sec02-card-sec02-F17.memory_hook: Hold your lane, wait for green
sec02-card-sec02-F17.expected_back: A Do Not Pass sign means passing is not allowed, and a No Turn on Red sign means you must wait for the green signal before turning.

sec02-card-sec02-R05.front: How does the rule on a Do Not Pass sign differ from the rule on a No Turn on Red sign?
sec02-card-sec02-R05.memory_hook: One bans overtaking, one waits green
sec02-card-sec02-R05.expected_back: A Do Not Pass sign forbids passing, while a No Turn on Red sign forbids turning until the light turns green.

sec02-card-sec02-F19.front: What must you do on a green circular light when a Left Turn Yield on Green sign is posted?
sec02-card-sec02-F19.expected_back: A Left Turn Yield on Green sign means that on a green circular light you must yield to oncoming traffic and pedestrians until the turn is safe.

sec02-card-sec02-F20.front: Where and when must you stop at a Stop Here for Pedestrians sign?
sec02-card-sec02-F20.expected_back: A Stop Here for Pedestrians sign near a crosswalk means you stop at the stop line whenever someone is in that crosswalk.

sec02-card-sec02-F15.front: What road feature does a Keep Right sign warn about, and which side must you take?
sec02-card-sec02-F15.expected_back: A Keep Right sign warns that an island, median or obstruction splits the road ahead, so you stay to its right.

sec02-card-sec02-F12.front: What do lane-use control signs tell drivers approaching an intersection?
sec02-card-sec02-F12.memory_hook: Signs assign mandatory or optional turns
sec02-card-sec02-F12.expected_back: Lane-use control signs show which lanes must turn or may turn at an intersection.

sec02-card-sec02-F16.front: Which drivers share the middle lane marked by a Center Lane Turn Only sign?
sec02-card-sec02-F16.expected_back: A Center Lane Turn Only sign means the middle lane is shared by left-turning drivers coming from both directions.

sec02-card-sec02-F18.front: Which vehicles qualify for a high occupancy vehicle lane, and what pavement symbol may mark it?
sec02-card-sec02-F18.expected_back: A high occupancy vehicle lane is reserved for vehicles carrying at least the number of people on the sign, such as two or more, and may show a painted white diamond.

sec02-card-sec02-R06.front: How does a Center Lane Turn Only lane differ from a high occupancy vehicle lane?
sec02-card-sec02-R06.memory_hook: Shared left turns versus rider count
sec02-card-sec02-R06.expected_back: A Center Lane Turn Only lane is shared by left-turning drivers from both directions, unlike a high occupancy vehicle lane, which is reserved by the number of people in the vehicle.

sec02-card-sec02-F13.front: At a Right Lane Transit Only sign, who is allowed to continue straight through the intersection from that lane?
sec02-card-sec02-F13.memory_hook: Only transit and listed bikes continue
sec02-card-sec02-F13.expected_back: At a Right Lane Transit Only sign, only transit vehicles, and bicycles when the sign shows them, may continue straight through the intersection from that lane.

sec02-card-sec02-F14.front: When a Right Turns Permitted sign accompanies a transit lane, what may you use that lane for and how must you merge?
sec02-card-sec02-F14.expected_back: A Right Turns Permitted sign lets you use a transit lane briefly to reach a driveway, the next intersection or legal curb parking; yield to buses and bikes in it and merge in behind them.

sec02-card-sec02-R04.front: How does a Right Lane Transit Only sign differ from a Right Turns Permitted sign for ordinary cars?
sec02-card-sec02-R04.memory_hook: No straight travel, brief turns allowed
sec02-card-sec02-R04.expected_back: A Right Lane Transit Only sign bars ordinary cars from going straight from that lane, while a Right Turns Permitted sign lets them enter it briefly to turn or park.

sec02-card-sec02-F21.front: What do yellow warning signs alert you to, and what is your duty when a hazard has no warning sign?
sec02-card-sec02-F21.expected_back: Yellow warning signs flag possible hazards or changed conditions ahead, yet you must react to conditions whether or not a sign warns you.

sec02-card-sec02-F24.front: What does a Curve sign, a Sharp Turn sign, and a Chevron sign each indicate about the road?
sec02-card-sec02-F24.expected_back: A Curve sign warns of a curve ahead, a Sharp Turn sign of a sharp turn ahead, and a Chevron sign marks a sharp curve or change of direction right at the sign.

sec02-card-sec02-R07.front: Which curve signs warn before the bend, and which sign marks the direction change right at the spot?
sec02-card-sec02-R07.expected_back: A Curve sign and a Sharp Turn sign warn of what lies ahead, while a Chevron sign marks the sharp curve or direction change at the sign itself.

sec02-card-sec02-F25.front: How does a Winding Road sign differ from a Reversing Curves sign?
sec02-card-sec02-F25.expected_back: A Winding Road sign warns of a series of turns or curves, while a Reversing Curves sign warns the road bends right and then left.

sec02-card-sec02-R10.front: How many bends does a Winding Road sign warn of compared with a Reversing Curves sign?
sec02-card-sec02-R10.expected_back: A Winding Road sign means several turns or curves, while a Reversing Curves sign means one curve right followed by one curve left.

sec02-card-sec02-F26.front: How does a Crossroad warning sign differ from a Side Road warning sign?
sec02-card-sec02-F26.expected_back: A Crossroad sign warns of a four-way intersection where cross traffic may enter; a Side Road sign warns of a T intersection with traffic joining from left or right.

sec02-card-sec02-F27.front: What does a Merge sign warn of, and how is an Add Lane sign different?
sec02-card-sec02-F27.memory_hook: Merge shares lane, add lane separates
sec02-card-sec02-F27.expected_back: A Merge sign warns that traffic is joining from the side shown, while an Add Lane sign means two roadways join and no merge is needed.

sec02-card-sec02-R08.front: Why does an Add Lane sign not require merging the way a Merge sign does?
sec02-card-sec02-R08.expected_back: A Merge sign means traffic will join your road from the side shown, while an Add Lane sign means the roads join with a new lane so nobody has to merge.

sec02-card-sec02-F28.front: What must drivers in the ending lane do when they see a Lane Reduction sign?
sec02-card-sec02-F28.expected_back: A Lane Reduction sign means the marked lane ends soon and drivers in it must merge into the through lane.

sec02-card-sec02-F29.front: What roadway change does a Two-Way Traffic Ahead sign warn you to expect?
sec02-card-sec02-F29.expected_back: A Two-Way Traffic Ahead sign means your one-way road becomes a two-way road and you will meet oncoming traffic.

sec02-card-sec02-R09.front: How does a Lane Reduction sign differ from a Two-Way Traffic Ahead sign?
sec02-card-sec02-R09.memory_hook: Dropped lane merges, two-way brings oncoming
sec02-card-sec02-R09.expected_back: A Lane Reduction sign means your lane is ending and you must merge, which differs from a Two-Way Traffic Ahead sign, where a one-way road starts carrying oncoming traffic.

sec02-card-sec02-F30.front: What do Divided Highway Begins and Divided Highway Ends signs mark, and which side do you keep to?
sec02-card-sec02-F30.memory_hook: Median starts or ends, keep right
sec02-card-sec02-F30.expected_back: Divided Highway Begins or Ends signs mark the start or end of a divided highway, where you keep to the right.

sec02-card-sec02-F22.front: What does a flashing yellow beacon on a pedestrian crossing sign tell approaching drivers?
sec02-card-sec02-F22.expected_back: A pedestrian crossing sign may have a flashing yellow beacon, meaning someone is crossing now, has just crossed or is about to cross.

sec02-card-sec02-F23.front: What do a Multiuse Path Crossing sign and an In-Street Pedestrian Crossing sign each require or warn of?
sec02-card-sec02-F23.memory_hook: Trail users ahead, stop for walkers
sec02-card-sec02-F23.expected_back: A Multiuse Path Crossing sign marks where cyclists and walkers often cross; an In-Street Pedestrian Crossing sign means stop when someone is in the crosswalk.

sec02-card-sec02-F31.front: What does a Stop Ahead warning sign mean, and how should you respond?
sec02-card-sec02-F31.expected_back: A Stop Ahead sign warns of a stop sign ahead, so slow down and get ready to stop.

sec02-card-sec02-F32.front: What should you prepare for when you pass a Signal Ahead sign or a Reduced Speed Limit Ahead sign?
sec02-card-sec02-F32.memory_hook: Ready for signal or lower limit
sec02-card-sec02-F32.expected_back: A Signal Ahead sign means slow down and be prepared to stop for a traffic light, and a Reduced Speed Limit Ahead sign means prepare to slow to a lower limit.

sec02-card-sec02-F36.front: What information does an Advisory Speed sign give, and how can it appear?
sec02-card-sec02-F36.memory_hook: Recommended safe ramp or curve speed
sec02-card-sec02-F36.expected_back: An Advisory Speed sign gives the safe speed for a freeway ramp or curve, may be paired with other signs, and may be electronic and change with conditions.

sec02-card-sec02-R03.front: How does a Reduced Speed Limit Ahead sign differ from an Advisory Speed sign?
sec02-card-sec02-R03.memory_hook: Upcoming legal cap versus curve advice
sec02-card-sec02-R03.expected_back: A Reduced Speed Limit Ahead sign warns that a lower legal limit is coming, while an Advisory Speed sign only recommends a safe speed for a ramp or curve.

sec02-card-sec02-F33.front: What do a Roundabout Ahead sign and a Railroad Advance sign each announce?
sec02-card-sec02-F33.expected_back: A Roundabout Ahead sign announces a roundabout intersection, and a Railroad Advance sign warns of a railroad crossing where you may need to stop.

sec02-card-sec02-F34.front: What does a Low Clearance sign tell you if you are driving a tall vehicle or carrying a high load?
sec02-card-sec02-F34.expected_back: A Low Clearance sign means the overpass ahead is low, so do not continue if your vehicle is too tall to fit beneath it.

sec02-card-sec02-F35.front: What roadway condition does a Hill warning sign alert you to?
sec02-card-sec02-F35.expected_back: A Hill sign warns of a steep grade ahead.

sec02-card-sec02-F37.front: What hazards do a Slippery When Wet sign and a Deer sign warn drivers about?
sec02-card-sec02-F37.expected_back: A Slippery When Wet sign means the pavement becomes unusually slick in rain, and a Deer sign means deer often cross there, so slow down if you see deer or other wildlife.

sec02-card-sec02-F38.front: What two facts do route signs tell you about the road you are traveling?
sec02-card-sec02-F38.expected_back: Route signs tell you which road you are on and whether it is an interstate, a U.S. route or a state highway.

sec02-card-sec02-F39.front: What information do green guide signs give, and how does the exit number help?
sec02-card-sec02-F39.memory_hook: Green guides destinations, numbers pick exits
sec02-card-sec02-F39.expected_back: Green guide or information signs give exit details and point the way to roads and cities, and the exit number helps you choose the right exit.

sec02-card-sec02-F40.front: What makes a highway stretch a safety corridor, what should you turn on there, and what may top the sign?
sec02-card-sec02-F40.expected_back: Safety corridors are designated highway stretches with more fatal and serious injury crashes than the statewide average; turn your lights on there, and their signs may carry diamond-shaped flags.

sec02-card-sec02-F41.front: What kinds of destinations do brown roadside signs point toward?
sec02-card-sec02-F41.memory_hook: Brown points to parks and history
sec02-card-sec02-F41.expected_back: Brown signs point to historic and cultural places as well as scenic areas, picnic grounds and parks.

sec02-card-sec02-R11.front: How do green guide signs and brown signs differ in the destinations they point to?
sec02-card-sec02-R11.memory_hook: Green guides cities, brown guides parks
sec02-card-sec02-R11.expected_back: Green signs guide you to exits, roads and cities, while brown signs point to historic, cultural and recreation sites.

sec02-card-sec02-F42.front: Which traveler needs and facilities are listed on blue motorist service signs?
sec02-card-sec02-F42.memory_hook: Blue marks traveler services and hospitals
sec02-card-sec02-F42.expected_back: Blue motorist service signs show gas, food, lodging, rest areas, electric vehicle charging, accessible facilities or parking, and the way to a hospital.

sec02-card-sec02-R12.front: Which sign family does a blue hospital directional sign belong to, and what else shares that family?
sec02-card-sec02-R12.memory_hook: Hospital belongs with blue motorist services
sec02-card-sec02-R12.expected_back: A blue sign pointing to a hospital is a motorist service sign, the same family that shows fuel, food, lodging, rest areas, charging and accessible parking.

sec02-card-sec02-F43.front: How must you handle a completely dark traffic signal versus a malfunctioning signal that flashes yellow or red?
sec02-card-sec02-F43.memory_hook: Dark means all-way stop, obey flashes
sec02-card-sec02-F43.expected_back: A dark signal, as in a power outage, means stop as if every approach had a stop sign; a broken signal that flashes yellow or red is obeyed by its flashing meaning.

sec02-card-sec02-F44.front: What does a steady circular red traffic light require you to do?
sec02-card-sec02-F44.expected_back: A steady circular red light means stop and stay stopped until the signal changes.

sec02-card-sec02-F46.front: Which sign rule applies equally to a flashing red light and a dark traffic signal?
sec02-card-sec02-F46.expected_back: A flashing red light or a dark signal is treated exactly like a stop sign.

sec02-card-sec02-R13.front: How does your duty at a steady red light differ from your duty at a flashing red light?
sec02-card-sec02-R13.memory_hook: Steady waits, flashing goes when clear
sec02-card-sec02-R13.expected_back: A steady red light means stop and stay stopped until it changes, while a flashing red light is treated like a stop sign.

sec02-card-sec02-F45.front: After coming to a full stop at a red light with no ban posted, which turns are legal in Oregon?
sec02-card-sec02-F45.expected_back: After a complete stop on red, unless a sign or officer forbids it, you may turn right onto a two-way road, or turn right or left onto a one-way road in its direction of travel.

sec02-card-sec02-R14.front: How does the roadway requirement for turning left on red differ from turning right on red?
sec02-card-sec02-R14.expected_back: Turning right on red onto a two-way road is allowed after a full stop, but a left turn on red is allowed only onto a one-way road going in the direction of the turn.

sec02-card-sec02-F47.front: What does a steady red arrow require in Oregon, and which turns are still permitted on it?
sec02-card-sec02-F47.memory_hook: Stop first, same red turns allowed
sec02-card-sec02-F47.expected_back: A steady red arrow means stop and stay stopped until it changes, but the same turns allowed on a steady red light are allowed on a red arrow.

sec02-card-sec02-F48.front: What does a steady circular yellow light warn of, and how should you respond?
sec02-card-sec02-F48.expected_back: A steady circular yellow light warns that red is coming, so stop before the intersection, or if you cannot stop safely, continue carefully through it.

sec02-card-sec02-R15.front: How does the stopping rule for a steady yellow light differ from a steady red light?
sec02-card-sec02-R15.memory_hook: Yellow stops safely, red holds fast
sec02-card-sec02-R15.expected_back: A steady yellow light tells you to stop before the intersection if you safely can, unlike a steady red light, which requires you to stop and stay stopped.

sec02-card-sec02-F49.front: How should you drive through an intersection with a flashing circular yellow light?
sec02-card-sec02-F49.expected_back: A flashing yellow light means slow down and go ahead with caution.

sec02-card-sec02-F50.front: What does a steady yellow arrow warn you is ending, and what action should you take?
sec02-card-sec02-F50.expected_back: A steady yellow arrow warns that the arrow is about to turn red, so stop before entering or, if stopping is unsafe, go carefully through.

sec02-card-sec02-F51.front: When may you turn on a flashing yellow arrow, and what signal does oncoming traffic have?
sec02-card-sec02-F51.expected_back: A flashing yellow arrow allows the turn shown only after you yield to pedestrians and to oncoming traffic, which has a steady green light.

sec02-card-sec02-R16.front: How does a steady yellow arrow differ from a flashing yellow arrow?
sec02-card-sec02-R16.expected_back: A steady yellow arrow warns that the protected movement is ending, while a flashing yellow arrow allows the turn only after yielding to pedestrians and oncoming traffic.

sec02-card-sec02-F52.front: Which movements does a steady circular green light permit, and who must left and right turners yield to?
sec02-card-sec02-F52.expected_back: A steady green light allows straight, left and right moves unless a sign forbids one; left turns yield to pedestrians and oncoming traffic, right turns yield to pedestrians.

sec02-card-sec02-F53.front: What priority does a steady green arrow give you for the direction it points?
sec02-card-sec02-F53.memory_hook: Green arrow grants right of way
sec02-card-sec02-F53.expected_back: A steady green arrow gives you the right of way to make the movement the arrow shows.

sec02-card-sec02-R17.front: For a left turn, how does a steady green arrow differ from a circular green light?
sec02-card-sec02-R17.memory_hook: Green arrow protects, green ball yields
sec02-card-sec02-R17.expected_back: A green arrow gives you the right of way for the movement shown, while a circular green light permits the movement but a left turn must still yield to pedestrians and oncoming traffic.

sec03-card-sec03-F01.front: What five situations allow you to drive somewhere other than the right side of the road?
sec03-card-sec03-F01.expected_back: Keep right except when passing a same-direction vehicle, going left of center around an obstruction, on a one-way road, using the center passing lane of a three-lane road, or when traffic personnel direct you.

sec03-card-sec03-F02.front: How much roadway space must each driver leave for oncoming traffic on a two-way street with no center line?
sec03-card-sec03-F02.expected_back: On a two-way road with no center line, each driver must leave at least half the road to oncoming traffic.

sec03-card-sec03-F04.front: What does yielding actually require you to do for another vehicle or pedestrian?
sec03-card-sec03-F04.expected_back: To yield means to slow or stop so another vehicle or a pedestrian can continue safely.

sec03-card-sec03-F03.front: What right-of-way rule applies any time your vehicle crosses left of the center line?
sec03-card-sec03-F03.expected_back: Whenever you drive left of the center line, for any reason, you must yield to oncoming traffic.

sec03-card-sec03-F05.front: What must you do when pulling out of an alley, driveway, or parking lot that has no signs or signals?
sec03-card-sec03-F05.expected_back: Leaving an alley, driveway or parking lot without signs or signals, stop before the road and yield to approaching vehicles and pedestrians.

sec03-card-sec03-F06.front: When should you change lanes, and how often should you do it?
sec03-card-sec03-F06.expected_back: Change lanes only when safe, and avoid frequent lane changes.

sec03-card-sec03-F19.front: Where must you position your vehicle when driving slower than normal traffic, and what should you do if a line builds behind you?
sec03-card-sec03-F19.expected_back: If slower than normal traffic, use the right lane or hug the right edge unless preparing to turn left, and pull off at the first safe spot to let a line of traffic pass.

sec03-card-sec03-R06.front: What single maneuver allows a slower driver to leave the right lane or right edge?
sec03-card-sec03-R06.expected_back: A slow driver keeps to the right lane or right edge, except when getting ready to make a left turn.

sec03-card-sec03-F35.front: What color lines mark a painted crosswalk, and what is your duty when a pedestrian is in it?
sec03-card-sec03-F35.expected_back: A marked crosswalk is shown with white lines, and you must stop when a pedestrian is in it.

sec03-card-sec03-F36.front: How do a pavement stop line and a pavement yield line look and work?
sec03-card-sec03-F36.expected_back: A stop line is a solid white line across your lane where you must stop, and a yield line is a row of triangles pointing at you where you must yield.

sec03-card-sec03-R13.front: What separates your legal duty at a solid stop line from your duty at a row of pointing yield triangles?
sec03-card-sec03-R13.expected_back: A stop line marks where you must stop, while a yield line of triangles pointing at you marks where you must yield.

sec03-card-sec03-F07.front: How do Oregon's statutory maximum speed limits interact with the basic rule and unposted roads?
sec03-card-sec03-F07.expected_back: Oregon's maximum limits apply on top of the basic rule, mark the top safe speed in ideal conditions, and hold whether or not posted unless another speed is posted.

sec03-card-sec03-F08.front: What is Oregon's statutory speed limit in alleys and narrow residential areas?
sec03-card-sec03-F08.expected_back: The statutory limit is fifteen miles per hour in alleys and narrow residential areas.

sec03-card-sec03-F09.front: What statutory speed limit applies in Oregon business districts and school speed zones?
sec03-card-sec03-F09.expected_back: The statutory limit is twenty miles per hour in any business district and in a school speed zone.

sec03-card-sec03-F10.front: What statutory speed limit governs residential districts, public parks, and ocean shores open to vehicles?
sec03-card-sec03-F10.expected_back: The statutory limit is twenty-five miles per hour in residential districts, public parks and on ocean shores where vehicles are allowed.

sec03-card-sec03-F11.front: What default statutory speed applies to roads fitting no other category, and how are Oregon interstate limits set?
sec03-card-sec03-F11.expected_back: Roads fitting no other category are fifty-five miles per hour unless posted otherwise, and interstate limits vary.

sec03-card-sec03-R01.front: How does street width change the statutory speed limit between narrow residential areas and ordinary residential districts?
sec03-card-sec03-R01.expected_back: Alleys and narrow residential areas carry the lowest statutory limit of fifteen miles per hour, while ordinary residential districts carry twenty-five miles per hour, so the narrowness of the street changes the limit.

sec03-card-sec03-R02.front: Which other district shares the twenty-mile-per-hour statutory cap with school speed zones instead of twenty-five?
sec03-card-sec03-R02.expected_back: A school speed zone shares the twenty miles per hour statutory limit with business districts, not the twenty-five miles per hour limit that applies in residential districts and parks.

sec03-card-sec03-R03.front: How does the fifty-five miles per hour catch-all statutory limit compare with interstate highway limits?
sec03-card-sec03-R03.expected_back: The fifty-five miles per hour statutory limit covers roads that fit no other category, while interstate highways have limits that vary rather than one fixed statutory figure.

sec03-card-sec03-F12.front: What inputs do Oregon's digital speed signs monitor to lower displayed speeds when conditions worsen?
sec03-card-sec03-F12.expected_back: Some Oregon speed signs are digital and use road, weather, traffic and visibility sensors to lower the speed when needed, sometimes showing why.

sec03-card-sec03-F13.front: What do yellow variable advisory speed signs do, and how can police still enforce them?
sec03-card-sec03-F13.expected_back: Yellow variable advisory speed signs recommend a speed and switch on only when needed; they are not limits, but police may enforce them through the basic rule.

sec03-card-sec03-F14.front: How is a black-and-white variable speed limit sign treated under Oregon law?
sec03-card-sec03-F14.expected_back: Black-and-white variable speed limit signs change the actual limit with conditions and are enforced like any speed limit sign.

sec03-card-sec03-F15.front: What two safety buffers do lower variable speeds create in poor visibility or challenging terrain?
sec03-card-sec03-F15.expected_back: Lower variable speeds add reaction time when fog, rain or snow cut visibility, and add stopping room on sharp curves, steep hills and construction zones.

sec03-card-sec03-F16.front: What driving speed does Oregon's basic rule require, and when and where does it apply?
sec03-card-sec03-F16.expected_back: The basic rule requires a speed that is reasonable and cautious for existing conditions, on every road at all times.

sec03-card-sec03-F17.front: Which factors must you weigh under the basic rule, and does it ever let you drive above the speed limit?
sec03-card-sec03-F17.expected_back: Obeying the basic rule means weighing traffic, pedestrians, cyclists, road surface and width, intersection hazards, weather and visibility; it never permits exceeding the limit.

sec03-card-sec03-F18.front: Can you violate Oregon's basic rule even while driving slower than the posted speed limit?
sec03-card-sec03-F18.expected_back: A speed unsafe for conditions breaks the basic rule even when it is below the posted limit.

sec03-card-sec03-F20.front: Where is racing illegal in Oregon, and what actions count as racing?
sec03-card-sec03-F20.expected_back: Racing is illegal on any road and includes any acceleration or speed contest or a speed record attempt.

sec03-card-sec03-F21.front: According to the federal chart, what is a pedestrian's risk of death when struck at twenty-three, forty-two, and fifty-eight miles per hour?
sec03-card-sec03-F21.expected_back: A federal chart shows a pedestrian hit at twenty-three miles per hour has a ten percent risk of death, rising to fifty percent at forty-two miles per hour and ninety percent at fifty-eight miles per hour

sec03-card-sec03-R04.front: How does a yellow variable advisory sign differ from a black-and-white variable speed limit sign?
sec03-card-sec03-R04.expected_back: A yellow variable advisory speed sign only recommends a speed, while a black-and-white variable speed limit sign sets an enforceable limit that police treat like any other.

sec03-card-sec03-R05.front: How do the posted speed limit and Oregon's basic rule work together?
sec03-card-sec03-R05.expected_back: The posted limit caps your speed in all conditions, while the basic rule can require going slower than that cap; neither one ever allows exceeding the limit.

sec03-card-sec03-F22.front: What standards do Oregon pavement lines follow, and who can authorize you to disregard them?
sec03-card-sec03-F22.expected_back: Oregon pavement markings follow national standards and must be obeyed unless a police officer or road worker redirects you.

sec03-card-sec03-F23.front: What does yellow pavement paint separate, and what does a solid yellow line mark on one-way roads and ramps?
sec03-card-sec03-F23.expected_back: Yellow lines separate opposing traffic and also edge the left side of one-way roads, ramps, shared left-turn lanes and painted medians; a solid yellow line is the left boundary of one-way roads and ramps.

sec03-card-sec03-F24.front: What does a single broken yellow center line tell drivers on a two-way road?
sec03-card-sec03-F24.expected_back: A broken yellow center line marks a two-way road where drivers in both directions may pass.

sec03-card-sec03-F25.front: When a solid yellow line runs beside a broken yellow line, when may you cross to pass?
sec03-card-sec03-F25.expected_back: With a solid and a broken yellow line together, you may pass when the broken line is on your side but not when the solid line is.

sec03-card-sec03-F26.front: What does a double solid yellow center line ban, and what crossing maneuver does it still allow?
sec03-card-sec03-F26.expected_back: Double solid yellow lines ban passing both ways, but you may turn left across them into or out of a roadway once oncoming traffic clears.

sec03-card-sec03-F27.front: How must you enter and use a shared two-way left-turn lane, and what is illegal inside it?
sec03-card-sec03-F27.expected_back: Where a two-way left-turn lane exists, turn left only from it; driving along it is illegal, so enter just before the turn and wait there until clear.

sec03-card-sec03-F28.front: How may you interact with a narrow painted median bordered by double solid yellow lines?
sec03-card-sec03-F28.expected_back: A painted median edged by double solid yellow lines may be crossed to turn left after oncoming traffic clears, but it is not a turn lane and may not be driven in.

sec03-card-sec03-F29.front: What do yellow diagonal stripes inside a painted median warn of, and what two actions are illegal there?
sec03-card-sec03-F29.memory_hook: Hazard zone, no driving or turning
sec03-card-sec03-F29.expected_back: Yellow diagonal stripes in a painted median warn of fixed objects or no-vehicle areas, and driving in or turning across them is illegal.

sec03-card-sec03-R07.front: How do a broken yellow center line and a double solid yellow line differ for passing and turning?
sec03-card-sec03-R07.expected_back: A broken yellow center line lets both directions pass, while a double solid yellow line bars passing for both directions but still allows a left turn across it once clear.

sec03-card-sec03-R08.front: In a combined solid-and-broken yellow center stripe, which line governs your lane?
sec03-card-sec03-R08.expected_back: In a solid-plus-broken yellow pair, only the line nearest your lane counts: broken on your side means you may pass, solid on your side means you may not.

sec03-card-sec03-R09.front: How does a two-way left-turn lane differ from a painted median edged with double solid yellow lines?
sec03-card-sec03-R09.memory_hook: Wait in pocket, only cross median
sec03-card-sec03-R09.expected_back: A two-way left-turn lane is meant for waiting to turn left, while a painted median with double yellow lines may only be crossed to turn and never used as a turn lane.

sec03-card-sec03-R10.front: What fundamental traffic-direction difference separates yellow pavement lines from white pavement lines?
sec03-card-sec03-R10.expected_back: Yellow markings separate traffic going opposite ways, while white markings separate lanes going the same way and mark the right edge.

sec03-card-sec03-F30.front: What roadway features do white markings create, and how does a solid white fog line help?
sec03-card-sec03-F30.expected_back: White markings divide same-direction lanes, mark the right edge, and form crosswalks, stop lines, symbols and words; a solid white edge or fog line helps you stay on the road.

sec03-card-sec03-F31.front: Where is a wide solid white line used, and what is the rule on crossing it?
sec03-card-sec03-F31.expected_back: A wide solid white line channels traffic into lanes such as turn lanes and separates bike lanes; crossing it is allowed but discouraged.

sec03-card-sec03-F32.front: What does a broken white line divide, and when may you cross it?
sec03-card-sec03-F32.expected_back: A broken white line separates same-direction lanes and may be crossed with caution.

sec03-card-sec03-F33.front: What does a dotted white line indicate before an exit, at a freeway entrance, and inside an intersection?
sec03-card-sec03-F33.memory_hook: Exit drops, ramp merges, intersection guides
sec03-card-sec03-F33.expected_back: A dotted white line may be crossed with caution; before an exit or intersection it means your lane leaves the route, at a freeway entrance it means merge, and in an intersection it guides your lane.

sec03-card-sec03-F34.front: What does a double solid white line between same-direction lanes forbid?
sec03-card-sec03-F34.expected_back: A double solid white line means no lane changes and usually comes with a sign banning lane changes for a set distance.

sec03-card-sec03-F37.front: Which lines, symbols, signs, or pavement color identify a bicycle lane?
sec03-card-sec03-F37.expected_back: A bike lane has a wide white line plus a bicycle symbol or bike lane sign and may be painted green.

sec03-card-sec03-F38.front: What hazards or restrictions do painted white chevrons on the roadway warn about?
sec03-card-sec03-F38.expected_back: White pavement chevrons may warn of fixed objects ahead or areas closed to vehicles.

sec03-card-sec03-F39.front: What does red pavement paint reserve, and why can you not rely on red paint alone to spot transit lanes?
sec03-card-sec03-F39.expected_back: Red markings show where only transit such as buses, light rail or bikes may travel continuously, but not every transit-only lane is red, so watch signs and markings.

sec03-card-sec03-F40.front: What legends may appear on a solid red transit lane, and what do striped red lines allow cars to do?
sec03-card-sec03-F40.memory_hook: Solid blocks cars, stripes allow turns
sec03-card-sec03-F40.expected_back: A solid red lane is transit only and may read BUS ONLY, BUS BIKE ONLY or LRT, while striped red lines show where cars may cross in to turn, park or reach a driveway.

sec03-card-sec03-R11.front: How does permission to cross compare across wide solid, broken or dotted, and double solid white lines?
sec03-card-sec03-R11.expected_back: A wide solid white line may be crossed but crossing is discouraged, a broken or dotted white line may be crossed with caution, and a double solid white line may not be crossed to change lanes.

sec03-card-sec03-R12.front: How does a dotted white line before a freeway exit differ from a dotted white line at an on-ramp?
sec03-card-sec03-R12.expected_back: A dotted white line ahead of an exit means your lane will leave the route, while a dotted white line at a freeway on-ramp means you must merge into freeway traffic.

sec03-card-sec03-R14.front: How does a solid red lane differ from striped red markings for someone driving a passenger car?
sec03-card-sec03-R14.memory_hook: Solid stays closed, stripes open turns
sec03-card-sec03-R14.expected_back: A solid red lane is closed to cars, while striped red lines mark the places where a car may enter the transit lane to turn, park or reach a driveway.

sec03-card-sec03-F41.front: What sides make up your space cushion, and how does driving faster change hazard time and stopping distance?
sec03-card-sec03-F41.expected_back: A space cushion is room ahead, beside and behind you; the faster you go, the less time you have to spot hazards and react, and the longer it takes to stop.

sec03-card-sec03-F42.front: What is a safe following gap in seconds, and what does Oregon recommend above thirty miles per hour?
sec03-card-sec03-F42.memory_hook: Two to four, four plus faster
sec03-card-sec03-F42.expected_back: A safe following distance is two to four seconds, and above thirty miles per hour it should be four seconds or more.

sec03-card-sec03-F43.front: How do you measure your following distance in seconds, and what if your count finishes under two seconds?
sec03-card-sec03-F43.expected_back: To check your gap, count seconds from when the car ahead passes a fixed mark until you reach it; under two seconds means back off and recount.

sec03-card-sec03-F44.front: What visual check tells you that you stopped far enough behind the vehicle ahead?
sec03-card-sec03-F44.expected_back: Stopped behind a vehicle, stay back far enough to see its rear tires meet the road, and rebuild a safe gap once traffic moves.

sec03-card-sec03-F45.front: Which weather, visibility, vehicle, and passing conditions call for extra following distance?
sec03-card-sec03-F45.memory_hook: Add seconds for rain, size, loads
sec03-card-sec03-F45.expected_back: Add following distance on wet roads, when someone behind wants to pass, behind bikes or motorcycles, behind large vehicles that cannot see you, when loaded or towing, and in poor visibility.

sec03-card-sec03-F46.front: What three additional situations involving hills, driver experience, and road crews call for extra following room?
sec03-card-sec03-F46.expected_back: Also add following distance when stopped on a hill, where the car ahead may roll back, while learning to drive, and near or in work zones.

sec03-card-sec03-F53.front: Which four factors shape stopping distance, and how does speed affect it even on dry clear days?
sec03-card-sec03-F53.expected_back: Stopping distance depends on road and weather, vehicle weight, reaction time and braking, and it grows with speed even in ideal conditions.

sec03-card-sec03-F54.front: Traveling sixty miles per hour, how does total hazard-to-stop distance compare against a football field?
sec03-card-sec03-F54.expected_back: At sixty miles per hour, the distance from spotting a hazard to a full stop is longer than a football field.

sec03-card-sec03-R15.front: How does Oregon's general following-distance range shift once your speed climbs above thirty miles per hour?
sec03-card-sec03-R15.expected_back: The general safe following distance is two to four seconds, but at speeds above thirty miles per hour the guidance rises to four seconds or more.

sec03-card-sec03-R16.front: Why and how do you increase your following gap when a driver behind you wants to pass?
sec03-card-sec03-R16.expected_back: When a driver behind you wants to pass, you add following distance by slowing so there is room in front of you for them to complete the pass.

sec03-card-sec03-F47.front: How should you position your vehicle on multilane and two-way streets to protect your side space?
sec03-card-sec03-F47.expected_back: For side space, avoid riding beside other vehicles on multilane streets, and keep away from oncoming traffic, usually by staying in the center of your lane.

sec03-card-sec03-F48.front: How can you help merging freeway traffic or a driver signaling to change lanes?
sec03-card-sec03-F48.expected_back: Make room for vehicles entering a freeway by moving over if the lane is clear, and help signaling drivers by easing your speed slightly.

sec03-card-sec03-F49.front: Why should you leave extra room inside your lane when passing a line of parked cars?
sec03-card-sec03-F49.expected_back: Give parked cars extra room within your lane, since a door may open or a person may step out.

sec03-card-sec03-F50.front: How do you keep a following driver back, and what is your first move if tailgated on a multi-lane road?
sec03-card-sec03-F50.memory_hook: Steady speed, tap brakes, move right
sec03-card-sec03-F50.expected_back: Keep the driver behind you back with a steady speed and an early brake tap that lights your brake lights; if tailgated, move right when there is a right lane.

sec03-card-sec03-F51.front: If a tailgater stays glued to your bumper and no right lane exists, what should you do and never do?
sec03-card-sec03-F51.expected_back: If a tailgater stays and you cannot move over, slow gradually to invite a pass, and never brake hard to punish tailgating, since you could be rear-ended.

sec03-card-sec03-F52.front: Because mirrors miss blind zones, how should you position your body and scan while backing up?
sec03-card-sec03-F52.expected_back: Before backing, look both ways; mirrors miss areas, so turn your head and body right, look out the rear window, glance to each side and back slowly.

sec03-card-sec03-R17.front: Which response to a tailgater is recommended, and which response is never acceptable?
sec03-card-sec03-R17.memory_hook: Gradual slowdown yes, hard brake never
sec03-card-sec03-R17.expected_back: With a tailgater behind you, easing off gradually is the advice, while braking hard to scare them off is never acceptable because it risks a rear-end crash.

sec03-card-sec03-R18.front: Why are mirrors alone not enough when backing up, and what must you do instead?
sec03-card-sec03-R18.expected_back: Mirrors alone are not enough for backing; the manual calls for turning your head and body to look out the rear window and glancing to each side.

sec04-card-sec04-F01.front: How far ahead should you scan for trouble spots, and what driving benefit does that give you?
sec04-card-sec04-F01.expected_back: Scan for trouble spots as far ahead as you can see, so you rarely need a last-minute move.

sec04-card-sec04-F02.front: What areas does proper scanning cover, and what four kinds of roadway clues does it help you catch?
sec04-card-sec04-F02.expected_back: Scanning means taking in the whole scene, roadsides included, so you notice pedestrians, hazards, vehicles that may cut into your path and signs routing you elsewhere.

sec04-card-sec04-F03.front: What three visual clues warn that a driver ahead may be about to slow down or stop?
sec04-card-sec04-F03.expected_back: Signs that a driver ahead may slow or stop include a cyclist or pedestrian on the road ahead, brake lights coming on and blinking turn signals.

sec04-card-sec04-F04.front: When should you slow down for a curve, and what posted clue helps guide your speed?
sec04-card-sec04-F04.expected_back: Slow down before entering a curve, using any speed posted under the curve sign as your guide.

sec04-card-sec04-F05.front: Where should your eyes and vehicle stay inside a curve, and what hidden users must you anticipate?
sec04-card-sec04-F05.expected_back: In a curve, look through it to your path, check where oncoming vehicles are in their lane, keep right of the center line in the middle of your lane, and expect hidden cyclists, pedestrians or slow vehicles.

sec04-card-sec04-F06.front: How should you adjust your speed as your vehicle straightens out leaving a curve?
sec04-card-sec04-F06.expected_back: Speed up gradually as you leave a curve.

sec04-card-sec04-R01.front: What is the proper order for slowing down and speeding up when driving through a curve?
sec04-card-sec04-R01.expected_back: Entering a curve you slow down first, while leaving a curve you build speed back up gradually, never the reverse.

sec04-card-sec04-F07.front: What is a vehicle blind spot, and how should you drive around other vehicles' blind spots?
sec04-card-sec04-F07.expected_back: A blind spot is the area around a vehicle the driver cannot see from the seat even using mirrors, so avoid staying in another driver's blind spot.

sec04-card-sec04-F08.front: What three steps must you complete before moving into an adjacent lane?
sec04-card-sec04-F08.expected_back: Before changing lanes, signal, check your side and rearview mirrors for traffic coming from behind, and glance over the shoulder on the side you are moving toward.

sec04-card-sec04-R02.front: Why are mirrors alone insufficient before changing lanes, and which shoulder must you check?
sec04-card-sec04-R02.memory_hook: Mirrors miss blind spots, check target
sec04-card-sec04-R02.expected_back: Mirrors alone do not clear a lane change, because the blind spot cannot be seen from the seat even with mirrors, so the shoulder glance goes toward the side you are moving to.

sec04-card-sec04-F09.front: Before overtaking on a two-lane road, why must you avoid tailgating, especially behind trucks, and what must you know about your car?
sec04-card-sec04-F09.expected_back: Passing is routine but dangerous, so keep a good view ahead by not tailgating, especially trucks and trailers, and know how fast your vehicle can accelerate.

sec04-card-sec04-F10.front: What crash risk comes from cutting back too early versus returning too late after passing, and what if you have doubts?
sec04-card-sec04-F10.expected_back: Pass only with enough room: cutting back too early risks sideswiping the passed vehicle, returning too late risks a head-on crash, and when unsure you stay in your lane.

sec04-card-sec04-R03.front: How does the collision hazard of cutting in too soon after a pass differ from staying out too long?
sec04-card-sec04-R03.memory_hook: Early clips side, late hits oncoming
sec04-card-sec04-R03.expected_back: Cutting back in too soon after a pass risks sideswiping the vehicle you passed, while staying out too long risks a head-on crash with oncoming traffic.

sec04-card-sec04-F11.front: On a two-lane road, which side do you pass on, and where must your pass start and finish?
sec04-card-sec04-F11.expected_back: On a two-lane road you pass only on the left, starting no sooner than the beginning of a passing zone and finishing before any no-passing zone.

sec04-card-sec04-R04.front: How do passing-zone and no-passing-zone markings restrict both the start and the end of a pass?
sec04-card-sec04-R04.expected_back: A pass must begin no earlier than the start of the passing zone and be finished before the no-passing zone, so both ends of the pass are fixed by the zone.

sec04-card-sec04-F12.front: Are you allowed to exceed the posted speed limit briefly to pass a slower vehicle?
sec04-card-sec04-F12.expected_back: You may not exceed the speed limit to pass, because going over the limit is illegal at all times.

sec04-card-sec04-F13.front: Walk through the steps of a safe pass from checking ahead to pulling back into your lane?
sec04-card-sec04-F13.expected_back: To pass, confirm a clear path, check mirrors and glance over your shoulder toward the new lane, signal, speed up and finish quickly, then signal and return once the passed vehicle shows in your rearview mirror.

sec04-card-sec04-R05.front: What mirror visual confirms you have enough room to signal and return to the right lane after passing?
sec04-card-sec04-R05.expected_back: After a pass you signal and move back into your lane once the vehicle you passed is visible in your rearview mirror.

sec04-card-sec04-F14.front: What roadway guides tell you where passing is allowed, and what visibility rule overrides everything?
sec04-card-sec04-F14.expected_back: Signs and pavement markings show where passing is allowed, and you must never pass where your view of oncoming traffic is limited.

sec04-card-sec04-F15.front: What two passing actions are illegal in or approaching a no-passing zone?
sec04-card-sec04-F15.memory_hook: Never cross inside or run over
sec04-card-sec04-F15.expected_back: Do not cross the center line to pass inside a no-passing zone, and do not start a pass you cannot finish before reaching one.

sec04-card-sec04-F16.front: When do hills or curves make passing illegal?
sec04-card-sec04-F16.expected_back: Do not pass when a hill or curve blocks your view of oncoming traffic.

sec04-card-sec04-F17.front: At or approaching which two types of crossings is passing strictly forbidden?
sec04-card-sec04-F17.expected_back: Do not pass when approaching, at or inside an intersection or a railroad crossing.

sec04-card-sec04-F18.front: What is the rule if a vehicle ahead stops at a crosswalk for a pedestrian?
sec04-card-sec04-F18.expected_back: Do not pass a vehicle that has stopped at a crosswalk to let a pedestrian cross.

sec04-card-sec04-R07.front: Which three crossing situations all share a strict ban on passing?
sec04-card-sec04-R07.expected_back: Passing is banned when the vehicle ahead has stopped at a crosswalk for a pedestrian, just as it is banned near intersections and railroad crossings.

sec04-card-sec04-F19.front: What two situations allow crossing the center line inside a no-passing zone?
sec04-card-sec04-F19.expected_back: In a no-passing zone you may cross the center line only when the right side of the road is blocked or when you are turning left.

sec04-card-sec04-R06.front: Inside a no-passing zone, which center-line crossings remain legal and which crossing is never legal?
sec04-card-sec04-R06.memory_hook: Left turns or blocks, never passing
sec04-card-sec04-R06.expected_back: In a no-passing zone, crossing the center line is still allowed to turn left or when the right side of the road is blocked, but never to pass.

sec04-card-sec04-F20.front: Under what conditions may you pass on the right of a vehicle that is turning or signaling left?
sec04-card-sec04-F20.memory_hook: Clear pavement only, skip bike lane
sec04-card-sec04-F20.expected_back: You may pass on the right when the vehicle ahead is turning or signaling left, if there is room without leaving the pavement or using a bike lane and the road ahead of it is clear.

sec04-card-sec04-F21.front: When may you pass on the right on a roadway with two or more lanes moving in your direction?
sec04-card-sec04-F21.expected_back: You may also pass on the right on a road with two or more lanes in your direction when the vehicle you pass is in the left lane.

sec04-card-sec04-R08.front: How do Oregon's two legal situations for passing on the right differ?
sec04-card-sec04-R08.expected_back: Passing a left-turning vehicle on the right is allowed only on pavement and outside the bike lane, whereas passing on the right on a multi-lane road needs the slower vehicle to be in the left lane.

sec04-card-sec04-F22.front: Why does passing on the right demand extra caution, and what speed rule still applies?
sec04-card-sec04-F22.expected_back: Take extra care when passing on the right, since other drivers do not expect it, and never speed past the limit to do it.

sec04-card-sec04-F23.front: What three things should you do when another driver is passing your vehicle?
sec04-card-sec04-F23.expected_back: When someone passes you, stay to the right, watch oncoming traffic and adjust your speed so the passer can get back into the right lane quickly.

sec04-card-sec04-F24.front: Why must you never wave or flash vehicle lights to tell a following driver when to pass?
sec04-card-sec04-F24.expected_back: Never wave or use lights to tell other drivers when to pass; the law forbids flashing any of your signals for that purpose.

sec04-card-sec04-R09.front: When being passed, how may you cooperate legally, and what signal action is forbidden?
sec04-card-sec04-R09.expected_back: When you are being passed, you help by keeping right and adjusting speed, but you must not wave the driver on or flash your signals to tell them when to go.

sec04-card-sec04-F25.front: Which design features allow traffic on multi-lane freeways to move faster and smoother?
sec04-card-sec04-F25.memory_hook: Controlled access, zero lights or rails
sec04-card-sec04-F25.expected_back: Freeways have several lanes each way and higher speeds, and traffic flows better because access is controlled, sharp curves are few and there are no railroad crossings or traffic signals.

sec04-card-sec04-F26.front: Why is holding a steady freeway speed smarter than weaving from lane to lane?
sec04-card-sec04-F26.memory_hook: Steady cuts risk, weaving wastes effort
sec04-card-sec04-F26.expected_back: Holding a steady speed on a freeway reduces lane changes, while weaving through traffic raises crash risk and rarely saves time.

sec04-card-sec04-F27.front: How should you balance freeway traffic flow with the speed limit, and which lane belongs to slower vehicles?
sec04-card-sec04-F27.memory_hook: Keep pace under limit, slow right
sec04-card-sec04-F27.expected_back: Keep pace with traffic but do not exceed the posted speed to match the flow, and if you drive slower than the flow, use the right lane.

sec04-card-sec04-R12.front: Does keeping pace with fast freeway traffic ever make driving over the posted speed limit legal?
sec04-card-sec04-R12.expected_back: Keeping pace with freeway traffic is encouraged, but the posted speed still caps you, and a driver below the flow belongs in the right lane.

sec04-card-sec04-F28.front: How should mainline freeway drivers respond when vehicles are entering from an on-ramp?
sec04-card-sec04-F28.expected_back: Watch for vehicles entering the freeway and adjust your speed so they can merge smoothly.

sec04-card-sec04-F29.front: How do you warn drivers behind you when you spot freeway traffic slowing up ahead?
sec04-card-sec04-F29.memory_hook: Tap brake pedal lightly several times
sec04-card-sec04-F29.expected_back: If you see freeway traffic slowing ahead, tap your brake pedal lightly several times to warn the drivers behind you.

sec04-card-sec04-R11.front: What specific brake-pedal technique signals a freeway slowdown to trailing drivers?
sec04-card-sec04-R11.expected_back: Several light taps on the brake pedal are how you warn drivers behind you that freeway traffic ahead is slowing.

sec04-card-sec04-F30.front: How does entering a freeway on an on-ramp differ from pulling onto most busy surface streets?
sec04-card-sec04-F30.expected_back: Unlike entering most busy roads, you enter a freeway by using the on-ramp to speed up and merge with fast traffic.

sec04-card-sec04-R10.front: Instead of slowing or stopping like at surface intersections, what do you do on a freeway on-ramp?
sec04-card-sec04-R10.expected_back: Entering a freeway is the reverse of entering most busy roads: instead of slowing or stopping, you speed up on the ramp and merge.

sec04-card-sec04-F31.front: Who yields during a freeway merge, what checks must you make, and why must you keep moving?
sec04-card-sec04-F31.memory_hook: Yield, check, match speed, keep moving
sec04-card-sec04-F31.expected_back: When merging onto a freeway, yield to traffic already on it, check mirrors and blind spots, match its speed and keep moving, since drivers behind expect you to accelerate.

sec04-card-sec04-F32.front: What immediate steps must you take if DO NOT ENTER or WRONG WAY signs tell you that you entered a ramp backward?
sec04-card-sec04-F32.expected_back: If a DO NOT ENTER or WRONG WAY sign shows you are entering a freeway the wrong way, pull to the side of the ramp at once, stop, turn on hazard lights, and carefully turn around or back off the ramp.

sec04-card-sec04-F33.front: How do ramp meters operate on single-lane and multi-lane freeway entrances when switched on?
sec04-card-sec04-F33.expected_back: Ramp meters look like traffic signals and run only at certain times; on multi-lane ramps each lane has one, only one vehicle goes per green, and you speed up to merge when yours turns green.

sec04-card-sec04-F34.front: What should you do when you approach a freeway ramp meter that is completely dark?
sec04-card-sec04-F34.expected_back: A dark ramp meter is not in use, so do not stop at it.

sec04-card-sec04-R13.front: How does your action at a green ramp meter compare with a dark ramp meter?
sec04-card-sec04-R13.memory_hook: Green releases one, dark skips stop
sec04-card-sec04-R13.expected_back: A ramp meter that shows green lets one vehicle go, while a dark ramp meter is off and requires no stop at all.

sec04-card-sec04-F35.front: When leaving a freeway, when do you signal and where do you begin slowing down?
sec04-card-sec04-F35.expected_back: To leave a freeway, signal well ahead, keep your speed until you are off the freeway, then slow to the posted advisory speed on the exit ramp.

sec04-card-sec04-R14.front: Why must you hold speed until leaving freeway travel lanes rather than braking before the exit ramp?
sec04-card-sec04-R14.expected_back: Leaving a freeway, you hold your speed until you are off the freeway and slow down only on the exit ramp, not in the travel lanes.

sec04-card-sec04-F36.front: What must you do if you miss your freeway exit, and why is using the shoulder or reversing banned?
sec04-card-sec04-F36.memory_hook: Take next exit, never back up
sec04-card-sec04-F36.expected_back: Most exits are numbered; if you miss yours, continue to the next one, because you must never stop or back up on a freeway and the shoulder is for emergencies only.

sec04-card-sec04-R15.front: After passing your intended freeway exit, which choice is lawful and which two moves are strictly forbidden?
sec04-card-sec04-R15.memory_hook: Continue ahead, never stop or reverse
sec04-card-sec04-R15.expected_back: A missed exit means driving on to the next one, while stopping or backing up on the freeway is never allowed and the shoulder is for emergencies only.

sec04-card-sec04-F37.front: If your vehicle breaks down on a freeway, where should you pull over, what lights go on, and where should you wait?
sec04-card-sec04-F37.memory_hook: Right shoulder, hazards, away from traffic
sec04-card-sec04-F37.expected_back: With vehicle trouble on a freeway, move to the right shoulder or an emergency stopping area, turn on hazard lights, and if possible stay in or near the vehicle on the side away from traffic, since walking there is dangerous.

sec04-card-sec04-F38.front: How do large vehicles and towed trailers differ from ordinary cars in size, acceleration, braking, and turning?
sec04-card-sec04-F38.memory_hook: Bigger dimensions, slower stops, wide turns
sec04-card-sec04-F38.expected_back: Large vehicles and vehicles towing trailers are longer, higher and wider, take longer to speed up and stop, and need more room to turn.

sec04-card-sec04-F39.front: What lane and turnout habits apply when driving a camper, motor home, or trailer that slows following traffic?
sec04-card-sec04-F39.memory_hook: Keep right, use first safe turnout
sec04-card-sec04-F39.expected_back: Driving a pickup with a camper, a motor home or a trailer, check your speed and the traffic behind often, pull off at the first safe turnout when traffic stacks up, and use the right lane on multi-lane roads.

sec04-card-sec04-F40.front: Is riding inside a towed trailer legal in Oregon, and what three trailer types are exceptions?
sec04-card-sec04-F40.expected_back: Letting passengers ride in a trailer is illegal, with three exceptions: a commercial bus trailer, a trailer that is independently steered, and a trailer towed by a fifth-wheel device.

sec04-card-sec04-F41.front: What three safety features must a fifth-wheel trailer have before passengers may ride inside it?
sec04-card-sec04-F41.memory_hook: Safety glazing, driver signal, two-way exit
sec04-card-sec04-F41.expected_back: A fifth-wheel trailer carrying passengers needs safety glazing in its windows and windowed doors, a sound or visual signal to reach the driver, and a clear exit that opens from inside and outside.

sec04-card-sec04-R16.front: How does Oregon's passenger rule for an equipped fifth-wheel trailer differ from an ordinary bumper-pull trailer?
sec04-card-sec04-R16.expected_back: A fifth-wheel trailer may carry passengers only when it has safety glazing, a way to signal the driver and an exit that opens from both sides, while trailers outside the listed exceptions may not carry passengers at all.

sec04-card-sec04-F42.front: How many boats, utility trailers, or vehicles may a passenger or recreational vehicle tow at once in Oregon?
sec04-card-sec04-F42.expected_back: Oregon law allows a passenger or recreational vehicle to tow at most one boat, utility trailer or other vehicle, so a second trailer or towed vehicle is not allowed.

sec04-card-sec04-R17.front: May a passenger car or recreational vehicle add a second towed unit behind its first trailer in Oregon?
sec04-card-sec04-R17.expected_back: One boat, utility trailer or other vehicle may be towed behind a passenger or recreational vehicle, but adding a second towed unit is not allowed.

sec05-card-sec05-F01.front: Which four maneuvers require a signal, and which directions must you check first?
sec05-card-sec05-F01.expected_back: A signal is required before you turn, change lanes, leave a roundabout or pull away from a curb, and before any of these moves you check ahead, behind and to the side that it is safe.

sec05-card-sec05-F02.front: How far ahead must your turn signal click on when you are already moving in traffic?
sec05-card-sec05-F02.expected_back: When you are moving in traffic, your turn signal must go on at least one hundred feet before the turn or lane change.

sec05-card-sec05-F03.front: How long should you run your turn signal before pulling out from a curb into traffic?
sec05-card-sec05-F03.expected_back: Pulling away from a curb into traffic, keep your signal on long enough that drivers know you are coming into the lane.

sec05-card-sec05-R02.front: How does signaling while moving in traffic differ from signaling when pulling away from a curb?
sec05-card-sec05-R02.expected_back: The one hundred-foot signal rule applies when you are already moving in traffic, while leaving a curb you signal long enough to warn traffic rather than for a set distance.

sec05-card-sec05-F04.front: Under what visibility conditions are hand-and-arm signals legal, and what must you use after dark?
sec05-card-sec05-F04.expected_back: Hand-and-arm signals may be used only in daylight when you can clearly see people and vehicles one thousand feet away; at night or in poor visibility you must use your signal lights.

sec05-card-sec05-F05.front: In what kind of vehicle must you avoid using hand-and-arm signals?
sec05-card-sec05-F05.expected_back: Do not use hand-and-arm signals while driving a wide or long vehicle.

sec05-card-sec05-F06.front: Which three driver actions have official hand-and-arm signals in the Oregon manual?
sec05-card-sec05-F06.expected_back: The manual shows three hand-and-arm signals: one for a right turn, one for a left turn and one for stopping or slowing down.

sec05-card-sec05-R01.front: How does the legal window for electric signal lights compare with hand-and-arm signals?
sec05-card-sec05-R01.expected_back: Signal lights work at any time, but hand-and-arm signals are limited to daylight with a clear view of one thousand feet, so darkness or poor visibility means lights only.

sec05-card-sec05-F07.front: Why is trusting another vehicle's flashing turn signal by itself a dangerous mistake?
sec05-card-sec05-F07.expected_back: Never rely only on another driver's turn signal, because that driver may turn the other way or turn without signaling at all.

sec05-card-sec05-F08.front: Do Oregon's turning rules stop at street intersections, or where else do they apply?
sec05-card-sec05-F08.expected_back: Turning rules apply wherever you turn, including driveways and alleys, not just at intersections.

sec05-card-sec05-F09.front: When should you scan behind and beside your car for a turn, and how should you steer through it?
sec05-card-sec05-F09.expected_back: Check for traffic behind and beside you well before you turn, then make the turn smoothly at a lower speed.

sec05-card-sec05-F22.front: Which lane do you start a turn from, which lane do you finish in, and what two habits must you avoid?
sec05-card-sec05-F22.expected_back: The general turning rule is to go from the nearest lane in your direction of travel into the nearest lane in the direction you want to go, without swinging wide or changing lanes during the turn.

sec05-card-sec05-F23.front: Which two specific lane mistakes does the manual illustrate as improper turns?
sec05-card-sec05-F23.expected_back: The manual pictures two turning errors: turning into the wrong lane and turning from the wrong lane.

sec05-card-sec05-F10.front: How must you handle a painted bicycle lane when preparing for and making a turn?
sec05-card-sec05-F10.expected_back: You may cross a bicycle lane to make a turn, but you must not pull into the bike lane to get ready for the turn.

sec05-card-sec05-R03.front: Which action in a bike lane is legal during a turn, and which pre-turn move is illegal?
sec05-card-sec05-R03.expected_back: Crossing a bike lane during a turn is allowed, but merging into the bike lane ahead of the turn is not.

sec05-card-sec05-F11.front: Why must you check both mirrors and glance over your shoulder before turning?
sec05-card-sec05-F11.expected_back: Before turning, check mirrors and look over your shoulder for bicyclists in your blind spot, since riders can come up beside you while you prepare to turn.

sec05-card-sec05-F12.front: Which cyclists and pedestrians take priority over your turning vehicle?
sec05-card-sec05-F12.expected_back: When turning you must yield to bicyclists in a bike lane or on a sidewalk, and you check the crosswalk and stop for pedestrians.

sec05-card-sec05-F13.front: What is the right move when you reach an intersection in the wrong lane for your intended turn?
sec05-card-sec05-F13.expected_back: If you arrive at an intersection in the wrong lane for your turn, go on to the next intersection, because circling the block is safer than a last-second lane or direction change.

sec05-card-sec05-F14.front: Where do you position your car for a right turn, and what four-step visual scan comes right before entering?
sec05-card-sec05-F14.expected_back: For a right turn, move as close as you can to the right curb or road edge, and just before entering the intersection look left, ahead, right and left again.

sec05-card-sec05-F15.front: Which lane do you use to turn left from a two-way street, and who gets the right of way?
sec05-card-sec05-F15.expected_back: For a left turn on a two-way road, approach in the lane just right of the center line, and Oregon law requires you to yield to oncoming traffic until the turn is safe.

sec05-card-sec05-R04.front: How does your starting position on a two-way street change between a right turn and a left turn?
sec05-card-sec05-R04.expected_back: A right turn starts as close as possible to the right curb or road edge, while a left turn on a two-way road starts in the lane just right of the center line.

sec05-card-sec05-R05.front: What exact four-part head check applies right before both right turns and left turns?
sec05-card-sec05-R05.expected_back: Before a right turn and before a left turn the same head check applies: left, ahead, right, then left again.

sec05-card-sec05-F16.front: Relative to the center point and the new street's center line, where do you turn and finish a left turn?
sec05-card-sec05-F16.expected_back: Make a left turn just before the imaginary center point of the intersection and finish just to the right of the center line of the new street.

sec05-card-sec05-F17.front: Is turning left on red onto a two-way road ever legal, and what rule governs dedicated left-turn lanes?
sec05-card-sec05-F17.expected_back: Turning left onto a two-way road against a red light is illegal, and where a left turn lane is provided you must turn from that lane.

sec05-card-sec05-F21.front: When can two or more lanes turn the same direction together, and how must drivers steer through?
sec05-card-sec05-F21.expected_back: Two or more lanes may turn the same way at once only where lane use signs or pavement markings allow it, and each driver follows the markings and stays in their own lane through the turn.

sec05-card-sec05-F18.front: Which lanes do you use to turn left from one one-way street onto another, and what is the red-light rule?
sec05-card-sec05-F18.expected_back: Turning left from a one-way road onto another one-way road, approach in the lane nearest the left curb and turn into the nearest left lane; this turn is allowed on red after you stop and yield to traffic and pedestrians.

sec05-card-sec05-F19.front: How do you position and handle a red light when turning from a two-way street onto a one-way street?
sec05-card-sec05-F19.expected_back: Turning from a two-way road onto a one-way road, approach in the lane nearest the side you are turning toward and turn into the nearest lane; this turn is also allowed on red after stopping and yielding.

sec05-card-sec05-F20.front: Going left off a one-way street onto a two-way street, which lanes apply and is red legal?
sec05-card-sec05-F20.expected_back: Turning left from a one-way road onto a two-way road, approach in the lane nearest the left curb and turn into the lane just right of the center line; this turn may not be made on a red light.

sec05-card-sec05-R06.front: Leaving a one-way street to turn left, what determines whether you can go on a red light?
sec05-card-sec05-R06.expected_back: A left turn from one one-way road onto another is allowed on red after a stop and yield, but a left turn from a one-way road onto a two-way road is never allowed on red.

sec05-card-sec05-R07.front: Why does turning from a two-way street onto a one-way street have the opposite red-light rule from turning left onto a two-way street?
sec05-card-sec05-R07.expected_back: Turning from a two-way road onto a one-way road may be made against a red light after stopping and yielding, the opposite of a left turn onto a two-way road on red.

sec05-card-sec05-R08.front: When turning left off a one-way street, what stays identical and what changes based on the cross street?
sec05-card-sec05-R08.expected_back: Leaving a one-way road to turn left, you start from the lane nearest the left curb whether the new road is one-way or two-way; only the lane you end in changes.

sec05-card-sec05-F24.front: When is a U-turn legal at an intersection controlled by a traffic light in Oregon?
sec05-card-sec05-F24.expected_back: U-turns are banned at intersections controlled by a traffic signal unless a sign allows the turn.

sec05-card-sec05-F25.front: Are U-turns allowed between intersections on city streets?
sec05-card-sec05-F25.expected_back: U-turns are banned between intersections in a city.

sec05-card-sec05-R10.front: Which urban U-turn ban can be lifted by a posted sign, and which one has no sign exception?
sec05-card-sec05-R10.expected_back: A U-turn at a signal-controlled intersection is banned unless a sign allows it, whereas a U-turn between intersections in a city is banned outright.

sec05-card-sec05-F26.front: Inside city limits, how far away must approaching drivers from both directions be able to see your car for a U-turn?
sec05-card-sec05-F26.expected_back: Inside city limits, a U-turn is banned anywhere traffic coming from either direction cannot see your vehicle within five hundred feet.

sec05-card-sec05-F27.front: Outside city limits, what clear sight distance in both directions is required to make a U-turn?
sec05-card-sec05-F27.expected_back: Outside city limits, a U-turn is banned anywhere traffic coming from either direction cannot see your vehicle within one thousand feet.

sec05-card-sec05-R09.front: How does the required sight distance for a U-turn change once you drive past city limits?
sec05-card-sec05-R09.expected_back: The U-turn visibility distance is five hundred feet inside city limits but one thousand feet outside city limits.

sec05-card-sec05-F28.front: Which two other locations strictly outlaw U-turns regardless of sight distance?
sec05-card-sec05-F28.expected_back: U-turns are banned at or on a railroad crossing and anywhere official signs or markings prohibit them.

sec05-card-sec05-F29.front: What dangerous assumption does a defensive driver refuse to make about stop signs and red lights?
sec05-card-sec05-F29.expected_back: A defensive driver never assumes that a stop sign or traffic signal will make approaching traffic stop.

sec05-card-sec05-F30.front: Where must your front bumper stop at a stop sign, steady red light, or flashing red signal?
sec05-card-sec05-F30.expected_back: At a stop sign, a steady red signal or a flashing red signal, stop before the marked stop line or crosswalk, or if neither is marked, before the unmarked crossing area.

sec05-card-sec05-F31.front: Even when your signal or sign allows a turn, which two groups still hold priority over you?
sec05-card-sec05-F31.expected_back: Always yield to vulnerable road users such as pedestrians and bicyclists, and to traffic already in the intersection, when making an allowed turn.

sec05-card-sec05-F32.front: What should you do after stopping properly if hedges, buildings, or parked cars still block your side view?
sec05-card-sec05-F32.expected_back: If you cannot see traffic coming from the left and right after stopping, pull forward slightly and scan before going on.

sec05-card-sec05-F33.front: What space check must pass before you roll into an intersection on a green light?
sec05-card-sec05-F33.expected_back: Even with a green light, do not enter an intersection unless your vehicle has room on the far side.

sec05-card-sec05-R13.front: Why does a green signal alone fail to guarantee you should enter an intersection?
sec05-card-sec05-R13.expected_back: A green light lets you go only if there is space for your vehicle beyond the intersection; a green light does not mean the way through is clear.

sec05-card-sec05-F34.front: How do drivers decide order at a four-way stop, and what breaks a tie when arrival order is unclear?
sec05-card-sec05-F34.expected_back: At a four-way stop, courtesy lets the driver who stopped first go first, and when in doubt you yield to the driver on your right, never assuming others will yield to you.

sec05-card-sec05-F35.front: When two opposite approaches have stop signs and cross traffic does not, who yields between straight and left-turning cars?
sec05-card-sec05-F35.expected_back: Where two-way stop signs face each other, a driver turning left yields to approaching or oncoming traffic going straight.

sec05-card-sec05-R11.front: How does priority shift between a four-way stop and an intersection where only facing approaches have stop signs?
sec05-card-sec05-R11.expected_back: At a four-way stop the first driver to stop goes first by courtesy, while at a two-way stop with facing signs the driver turning left yields to oncoming straight traffic.

sec05-card-sec05-F36.front: At an intersection with zero signs or signals, which way do you look first and who gets the right of way?
sec05-card-sec05-F36.expected_back: At an intersection with no signs or signals, look left first to see that cross traffic is yielding, then ahead and right, and yield to any vehicle already in the intersection or coming from your right.

sec05-card-sec05-F37.front: Who holds the right of way when your street ends at an uncontrolled T-intersection?
sec05-card-sec05-F37.expected_back: When your road dead-ends into an uncontrolled T intersection, drivers on the through road have the right of way and you must yield to them.

sec05-card-sec05-R12.front: How does the uncontrolled right-of-way rule change when one road ends at a T instead of crossing straight through?
sec05-card-sec05-R12.expected_back: At an uncontrolled intersection you yield to vehicles already in it or coming from the right, while at an uncontrolled T intersection the driver on the ending road yields to through traffic.

sec05-card-sec05-F38.front: What defines roundabouts, rotaries, and traffic circles, and which direction does traffic travel around the island?
sec05-card-sec05-F38.expected_back: Roundabouts, rotaries and traffic circles are circular intersections with a center island, and traffic always moves counterclockwise around it.

sec05-card-sec05-F39.front: What does a yellow warning sign displaying arrows arranged in a circle mean?
sec05-card-sec05-F39.expected_back: A warning sign showing arrows in a circle tells you a circular intersection is ahead.

sec05-card-sec05-F40.front: Which four actions prepare you safely as you roll toward a roundabout entry?
sec05-card-sec05-F40.expected_back: Approaching a roundabout, slow down, read the signs to find your exit, watch for bicyclists who may merge or use the sidewalk, and stop for pedestrians in the crosswalk in your lane.

sec05-card-sec05-F41.front: Who must you yield to when entering a roundabout, and how should you merge in?
sec05-card-sec05-F41.expected_back: To enter a roundabout you yield to traffic already inside and to traffic exiting, wait for a gap, merge, and stay ready to stop.

sec05-card-sec05-F42.front: How must you drive behind a bicyclist who has merged into the roundabout lane?
