sec05-card-sec05-F42.expected_back: Inside a roundabout, circle until your exit, give a bicyclist who has merged into traffic the full lane, and never pass a bicyclist within the roundabout.

sec05-card-sec05-R15.front: What two path choices do bicyclists have at a roundabout, and what protection applies if they join traffic?
sec05-card-sec05-R15.expected_back: A bicyclist approaching a roundabout may either merge with traffic or use the sidewalk, and one who merges gets the full travel lane with no passing inside.

sec05-card-sec05-F43.front: Which signal and hazard check are required every time you exit a roundabout?
sec05-card-sec05-F43.expected_back: To leave a roundabout, use your right turn signal and watch for pedestrians in the crosswalk, ready to stop.

sec05-card-sec05-R14.front: How do your responsibilities at a roundabout entry compare with your responsibilities at the exit?
sec05-card-sec05-R14.expected_back: Entering a roundabout you yield to circulating and exiting traffic, while leaving it you give a right turn signal and watch the crosswalk.

sec05-card-sec05-F44.front: When do you select your lane for a multi-lane roundabout, and what must you avoid once inside?
sec05-card-sec05-F44.expected_back: In a multi-lane roundabout, read exit and lane use signs and markings before entering, pick the lane for your exit, keep that lane until you leave and avoid lane changes inside.

sec05-card-sec05-R17.front: Why is changing lanes inside a multi-lane roundabout the wrong way to reach your exit?
sec05-card-sec05-R17.expected_back: In a multi-lane roundabout you choose the lane for your exit before entering and hold it, rather than changing lanes once inside.

sec05-card-sec05-F45.front: What lane space can large trucks use in a roundabout, and what is illegal around them?
sec05-card-sec05-F45.expected_back: Trucks may straddle both lanes of a roundabout, and passing or driving beside a truck inside a roundabout is illegal.

sec05-card-sec05-F46.front: What must you do if an emergency vehicle approaches before you have entered a roundabout?
sec05-card-sec05-F46.expected_back: When emergency vehicles are approaching, do not enter the roundabout; pull to the right and let other vehicles clear the intersection.

sec05-card-sec05-F47.front: What is the rule if sirens approach while you are already driving inside a roundabout?
sec05-card-sec05-F47.expected_back: Never stop inside a roundabout for an emergency vehicle; keep going, exit, and then pull onto the right shoulder to let it pass.

sec05-card-sec05-R16.front: How does yielding to an emergency vehicle change once your car is already inside a roundabout?
sec05-card-sec05-R16.expected_back: For an emergency vehicle outside a roundabout you stay out and pull right, but once inside you keep moving, exit and then pull over; stopping in the circle is never correct.

sec06-card-sec06-F01.front: Which people on public ways, crosswalks, or highway shoulders count as vulnerable road users in Oregon?
sec06-card-sec06-F01.expected_back: Vulnerable road users include pedestrians, bicyclists, motorcyclists, highway workers and anyone using a skateboard, scooter or similar device in a public way, a crosswalk or on a highway shoulder.

sec06-card-sec06-F02.front: What two real-world factors make vulnerable road users especially at risk around cars?
sec06-card-sec06-F02.expected_back: These road users are called vulnerable because they can be hard to see and often have no protection from injury in a crash.

sec06-card-sec06-F03.front: Beyond people on foot, who else counts as a pedestrian under the Oregon manual?
sec06-card-sec06-F03.expected_back: In the manual the word pedestrian covers people walking and people rolling on skateboards, scooters, wheelchairs and similar devices.

sec06-card-sec06-F04.front: Does a crosswalk need painted stripes before you are required to stop for a pedestrian?
sec06-card-sec06-F04.expected_back: You must stop for a pedestrian crossing the road at any crosswalk, whether it is marked or unmarked.

sec06-card-sec06-F05.front: What exact movement triggers a pedestrian's legal crossing right of way in Oregon?
sec06-card-sec06-F05.expected_back: A pedestrian is legally crossing as soon as any part of the person, or something they use such as a cane, wheelchair or bicycle, moves onto the road.

sec06-card-sec06-F06.front: When a pedestrian is in a crosswalk, which specific lanes require you to stop and remain stopped?
sec06-card-sec06-F06.expected_back: Stop and stay stopped for a crosswalk pedestrian who is in your lane, in the lane beside yours (a bike lane counts), or in the lane you are turning into.

sec06-card-sec06-F09.front: Why is passing another car stopped at a crosswalk illegal?
sec06-card-sec06-F09.expected_back: It is illegal to pass a vehicle that is stopped at a crosswalk, since its driver may be waiting for someone to cross.

sec06-card-sec06-F10.front: Do you have to stop for a pedestrian crossing on the far side of a raised safety island?
sec06-card-sec06-F10.expected_back: You do not have to stop for a pedestrian who is in a crosswalk on the far side of a safety island.

sec06-card-sec06-R21.front: How does your duty to stop compare between a pedestrian in the adjacent lane and one beyond a safety island?
sec06-card-sec06-R21.expected_back: A pedestrian in the lane next to yours requires you to stop and stay stopped, while a pedestrian on the other side of a safety island does not.

sec06-card-sec06-F07.front: At an intersection with a traffic light, how much clearance past your target lane must a pedestrian have before you turn?
sec06-card-sec06-F07.expected_back: When turning at an intersection with a traffic signal, the pedestrian must be at least six feet from the lane you are turning into before you start the turn.

sec06-card-sec06-F08.front: When turning at an intersection with no traffic signal, how far must a pedestrian clear before you start turning?
sec06-card-sec06-F08.expected_back: When turning at an intersection without a traffic signal, the pedestrian must have cleared the lane you are turning into and the next lane too before you start the turn.

sec06-card-sec06-R20.front: How does pedestrian clearance for a turn change when an intersection has no traffic signal?
sec06-card-sec06-R20.expected_back: At a signalized intersection you may start your turn once the pedestrian is six feet or more from your target lane, but without a signal you wait until the pedestrian has cleared that lane plus the next one.

sec06-card-sec06-F11.front: Where do unmarked crosswalks exist, and how do you picture their boundaries?
sec06-card-sec06-F11.expected_back: Every intersection has a crosswalk even with no painted lines; to find an unmarked one, picture the corner sidewalk or shoulder carried across the road.

sec06-card-sec06-F12.front: What is the minimum width of an unmarked crosswalk, and does a street need sidewalks to have one?
sec06-card-sec06-F12.expected_back: An unmarked crosswalk is at least six feet wide, and it exists even where there is no sidewalk or shoulder.

sec06-card-sec06-F13.front: What does a flashing yellow beacon at a mid-block crosswalk alert drivers to expect?
sec06-card-sec06-F13.expected_back: A mid-block crosswalk may have a flashing yellow light that warns a pedestrian is crossing or about to cross.

sec06-card-sec06-F14.front: Why must your front and rear bumpers stay completely off a crosswalk when stopped?
sec06-card-sec06-F14.expected_back: Never stop with any part of your vehicle over the crosswalk, because a blocked crosswalk forces pedestrians around your car into danger.

sec06-card-sec06-F15.front: Where must you stop and who gets priority when crossing a sidewalk at an alley, driveway, or lot?
sec06-card-sec06-F15.expected_back: When you cross a sidewalk to enter or leave a parking lot, alley or driveway, stop before the sidewalk and yield to pedestrians and bicyclists.

sec06-card-sec06-F17.front: What does a yellow five-sided road sign tell you is ahead?
sec06-card-sec06-F17.expected_back: A yellow five-sided sign marks where a school zone begins and warns of school crossings, so look for children and be ready to stop.

sec06-card-sec06-F18.front: What reduced speed limit applies in an Oregon school speed zone, and what marks its start and end?
sec06-card-sec06-F18.expected_back: A school speed zone carries a reduced limit of twenty miles per hour, beginning at the SCHOOL SPEED LIMIT twenty sign and ending at the END SCHOOL ZONE sign or another posted speed sign.

sec06-card-sec06-F19.front: What does a flashing yellow light mounted on a school speed sign tell you?
sec06-card-sec06-F19.expected_back: When the yellow light on a school speed sign is flashing, children are arriving at or leaving school and the reduced limit applies.

sec06-card-sec06-F20.front: Which hours and days trigger a school-hours speed sign, and what if you cannot tell whether school is open?
sec06-card-sec06-F20.expected_back: A school-hours speed sign applies from seven a.m. to five p.m. on days school is in session, and if you are unsure whether it is a school day, slow to twenty miles per hour

sec06-card-sec06-F21.front: On which days and hours does a when-children-are-present school speed sign take effect?
sec06-card-sec06-F21.expected_back: A school speed sign for when children are present applies on any day and at any hour that children are present.

sec06-card-sec06-F22.front: Which three specific crosswalk scenes legally count as children being present in Oregon?
sec06-card-sec06-F22.expected_back: Children are present when they are waiting at a crosswalk, are in or walking through a crosswalk, or a traffic patrol member is there to help them cross.

sec06-card-sec06-R22.front: How does a school-hours speed sign differ from a children-present speed sign?
sec06-card-sec06-R22.expected_back: The school-hours sign covers set daytime hours on school days only, while the children-present sign applies on any day at any hour children are present.

sec06-card-sec06-F23.front: How long must you remain stopped for a pedestrian with a white cane or guide dog, even if your light turns green?
sec06-card-sec06-F23.expected_back: Yield to a pedestrian with limited vision, or one who is blind or deaf and blind using a white cane or guide dog: stop if the person is crossing or about to, and stay stopped until they have crossed the whole road, even on a green light.

sec06-card-sec06-F24.front: What two precautions protect children near parks, parked cars, and residential driveways?
sec06-card-sec06-F24.expected_back: In neighborhoods and near parks, keep away from parked cars that hide your view and take great care backing out of a driveway, since children may be playing behind your vehicle.

sec06-card-sec06-F25.front: When children enter a crosswalk or a school crossing guard signals, when can you move again?
sec06-card-sec06-F25.expected_back: Stop and yield when children step into a crosswalk or a school crossing guard signals you, and stay stopped until the children are out of the crosswalk.

sec06-card-sec06-F26.front: Why are bicyclists easier to overlook than full-size motor vehicles?
sec06-card-sec06-F26.expected_back: Bicyclists are harder to see than other vehicles and can be hidden in your blind spot.

sec06-card-sec06-F27.front: What street-surface hazards can force a bicyclist to brake or swerve toward your lane?
sec06-card-sec06-F27.expected_back: Potholes, glass, litter, storm grates, railroad tracks and car doors opening can make a bicyclist slow or swerve into your path, so leave riders plenty of room.

sec06-card-sec06-F28.front: Are driving or parking in a bike lane ever allowed, and when may your tires cross one?
sec06-card-sec06-F28.expected_back: Never drive or park in a bike lane; crossing one is allowed to turn or to get into or out of an alley, driveway or private road.

sec06-card-sec06-F29.front: How do right-of-way rules treat bicyclists in bike lanes, on sidewalks, and at intersections?
sec06-card-sec06-F29.expected_back: Before turning across a bike lane or sidewalk you must yield to bicyclists using it, and at intersections you yield to bicyclists just as you would to other vehicles.

sec06-card-sec06-F30.front: Above thirty-five miles per hour, how much lateral room must you leave to pass a bicyclist in your lane?
sec06-card-sec06-F30.expected_back: At speeds above thirty-five miles per hour, you may pass a bicyclist in your lane only if you leave enough distance that you would not hit the rider if they fell.

sec06-card-sec06-F31.front: What should you do when traffic or sightlines prevent you from passing a bicyclist safely?
sec06-card-sec06-F31.expected_back: Ordinary passing rules apply to bicyclists too, and if you cannot pass safely you slow down and stay behind the rider until you can.

sec06-card-sec06-F32.front: Which assistive or electric devices legally share bike lanes and paths, and how do you yield to them?
sec06-card-sec06-F32.expected_back: Motorized wheelchairs, scooters and personal assistive mobility devices may use bike lanes and paths, and you yield to their operators as you would to a bicyclist.

sec06-card-sec06-F33.front: What does a green bike box at a signalized intersection look like, and where must cars stop?
sec06-card-sec06-F33.expected_back: A bike box is usually a green painted box marked with a white bicycle symbol; at a signal you stop behind it, never inside it, and bicyclists move into the box ahead of you.

sec06-card-sec06-F34.front: How does a bike box change right-on-red rules and right turns on green?
sec06-card-sec06-F34.expected_back: Where there is a bike box, right turns on a red light are not allowed, and when turning right on green you signal and yield to bicyclists on your right.

sec06-card-sec06-F35.front: What road marking pairs two chevrons over a bicycle icon, and what does it mean?
sec06-card-sec06-F35.expected_back: A sharrow, two chevrons painted above a bicycle symbol, shows a shared lane where bicyclists may be riding in the road.

sec06-card-sec06-F36.front: Why do drivers misread approaching motorcycles and mopeds at intersections?
sec06-card-sec06-F36.expected_back: Motorcycles and mopeds are harder to see than other vehicles, and it is hard to judge how far away a rider is or how fast they are going.

sec06-card-sec06-F37.front: How should you handle an oncoming motorcyclist when waiting to turn across traffic?
sec06-card-sec06-F37.expected_back: You must yield to an oncoming motorcyclist just as you would to any vehicle, and the safest choice is to wait until the rider passes before you turn.

sec06-card-sec06-F38.front: How should your following distance behind a motorcycle compare with following a passenger car?
sec06-card-sec06-F38.expected_back: Leave more following distance behind a motorcycle than you would behind a car.

sec06-card-sec06-F39.front: Why must you verify a motorcycle is genuinely slowing before turning across its flashing signal?
sec06-card-sec06-F39.expected_back: Some motorcycle turn signals do not cancel by themselves, so before turning in front of an oncoming rider with a signal on, make sure the rider is really slowing to turn.

sec06-card-sec06-F40.front: Is lane sharing alongside a motorcycle or moped legal, and how much space do you give when passing?
sec06-card-sec06-F40.expected_back: Sharing a lane with a motorcycle or moped is against the law, and when you pass one you must leave the rider a full lane.

sec06-card-sec06-F41.front: What wind and pavement conditions force motorcyclists to adjust speed or lane position suddenly?
sec06-card-sec06-F41.expected_back: Strong wind and surfaces such as gravel, debris, pavement seams, grooved pavement and manhole covers can make riders change speed or direction, so increase your following distance.

sec06-card-sec06-R23.front: Which two space rules protect motorcyclists when you follow behind them and when you overtake them?
sec06-card-sec06-R23.expected_back: Following a motorcycle calls for more distance than following a car, and passing a motorcycle calls for giving the rider a full lane.

sec06-card-sec06-F42.front: How do large trucks, buses, RVs, and towed trailers compare with small cars in acceleration and stopping distance?
sec06-card-sec06-F42.expected_back: Large vehicles such as recreational vehicles, trucks, buses and vehicles towing trailers accelerate slowly, need more room, and need about three times the stopping distance of a smaller vehicle at the same speed.

sec06-card-sec06-F43.front: How can you tell whether the driver of a large truck or bus can see your car beside it?
sec06-card-sec06-F43.expected_back: Large vehicles have bigger blind spots on both sides, and if you cannot see the driver in the large vehicle's side mirror, that driver cannot see you.

sec06-card-sec06-F44.front: What two hazards make stopping close behind a large truck or bus dangerous?
sec06-card-sec06-F44.expected_back: A large vehicle has a deep blind spot right behind it, and you should not stop too close behind one because it may roll back slightly when it starts.

sec06-card-sec06-R24.front: How do you recognize when your car sits inside a large vehicle's rear or side blind spots?
sec06-card-sec06-R24.expected_back: Behind a large vehicle you are in its deep rear blind spot, and beside it you are in a side blind spot unless you can see its driver in the side mirror.

sec06-card-sec06-F45.front: How should you pace a pass beside a large vehicle, and when is it safe to merge back over?
sec06-card-sec06-F45.expected_back: Passing a large vehicle takes longer, so finish quickly, do not ride alongside it, and wait until its entire front appears in your rearview mirror before moving back in.

sec06-card-sec06-F46.front: How do you maintain visibility around tire spray thrown up by a large vehicle on wet pavement?
sec06-card-sec06-F46.expected_back: On a wet road, spray from a large vehicle can badly reduce your vision, so stay as far from it as you can while keeping to your lane.

sec06-card-sec06-F47.front: Why must you keep out of the curbside gap beside a turning bus or big truck?
sec06-card-sec06-F47.expected_back: Never cut in between a turning large vehicle and the curb or shoulder, because it may swing wide and use more than one lane, and do not crowd the intersection while it turns.

sec06-card-sec06-R01.front: What rule applies whenever a large truck is preparing to back up or reversing into a dock?
sec06-card-sec06-R01.expected_back: A large vehicle backing up may need to block the street, and you must never cross behind one that is getting ready to back or is already backing.

sec06-card-sec06-R02.front: What do smoking wheels or high downhill speed on a large truck warn of, and how should you react?
sec06-card-sec06-R02.expected_back: Large vehicles lose speed climbing hills and must go slowly downhill to stay in control; smoking wheels or a high speed may mean brake failure, so leave extra space and do not pass.

sec06-card-sec06-R03.front: What is the role of a specially marked pilot vehicle on Oregon highways?
sec06-card-sec06-R03.expected_back: Pilot vehicles are specially marked cars that lead or follow a vehicle hauling an especially large load.

sec06-card-sec06-R04.front: How should you adjust position and speed when meeting, following, or passing a pilot vehicle?
sec06-card-sec06-R04.expected_back: Meeting an oncoming pilot vehicle, slow down and move as far right as you can while staying in your lane; following one, lengthen your following distance; and pass a pilot vehicle or its load only with caution.

sec06-card-sec06-R05.front: Where are warning lamps mounted on a school bus, and what swings out when red lights flash?
sec06-card-sec06-R05.expected_back: School buses carry flashing amber and red lights high on the front and rear, and some have a stop arm that swings out near the driver's window when the red lights start flashing.

sec06-card-sec06-R06.front: What do flashing amber lights at the top of a school bus warn drivers to prepare for?
sec06-card-sec06-R06.expected_back: Flashing amber lights on a school bus warn that it is about to stop on the road to load or unload children, so get ready to stop.

sec06-card-sec06-R07.front: What is your exact legal duty when a school bus switches on flashing red lights?
sec06-card-sec06-R07.expected_back: When a school bus flashes red lights, stop before you reach the bus and stay stopped until the driver switches the red lights off.

sec06-card-sec06-R08.front: When does oncoming traffic not have to stop for a school bus flashing red lights?
sec06-card-sec06-R08.expected_back: On a divided highway whose two roadways are split by an unpaved median strip or a barrier, you stop for a school bus only if you are on the bus's side of the road.

sec06-card-sec06-R09.front: Does a painted median or center turn lane excuse oncoming drivers from stopping for a school bus?
sec06-card-sec06-R09.expected_back: A painted median strip or a turn lane does not make two separate roads, so traffic in all lanes must stop for the flashing school bus.

sec06-card-sec06-R10.front: Which other buses may flash amber and red warning lights, and how must you respond?
sec06-card-sec06-R10.expected_back: Buses serving places of worship and buses carrying workers may use flashing amber and red lights, and you treat those lights exactly as you would on a school bus.

sec06-card-sec06-R11.front: When are drivers behind a public transit bus legally required to yield and let it back into the lane?
sec06-card-sec06-R11.expected_back: When a transit bus driver signals to pull back into traffic and the electric yield sign on the back of the bus is flashing, vehicles coming from behind must yield.

sec06-card-sec06-R12.front: What colors make up a slow-moving vehicle emblem, and what vehicles display it on highways?
sec06-card-sec06-R12.expected_back: Slow moving vehicles such as farm equipment must show the slow moving vehicle emblem on public highways, a fluorescent orange center with a reflective red border, so be ready to slow or change position.

sec06-card-sec06-R13.front: At what rear overhang length must cargo carry a red warning flag, and how big must that flag be?
sec06-card-sec06-R13.expected_back: A load sticking out four feet or more past the rear of a vehicle must carry a red flag at least twelve inches square at its end.

sec06-card-sec06-R14.front: What replaces the red cloth flag on a long rear load at night or in poor visibility?
sec06-card-sec06-R14.expected_back: When visibility is limited, the red flag on a rear overhanging load is replaced by a red light that can be seen from five hundred feet to the rear and sides.

sec06-card-sec06-R15.front: How far may cargo extend beyond the left fenders, right fenders, and front bumper of a passenger car?
sec06-card-sec06-R15.expected_back: A passenger vehicle may carry no load past the left fenders, no more than six inches past the right fenders, and no more than four feet past the front of the vehicle.

sec06-card-sec06-R16.front: How do intersection rules apply to vehicles inside a funeral procession versus outside traffic?
sec06-card-sec06-R16.expected_back: Vehicles in a funeral procession may enter intersections without stopping and need not obey traffic control devices, and other drivers must yield to the procession.

sec06-card-sec06-R17.front: Is an outside driver allowed to join or cut between cars in a funeral procession?
sec06-card-sec06-R17.expected_back: If you are not part of a funeral procession, joining it or driving between its vehicles is against the law.

sec06-card-sec06-R18.front: On a multi-lane road, what are your two options when approaching any stopped vehicle with flashing lights?
sec06-card-sec06-R18.expected_back: On a road with two or more lanes in your direction, when you approach any stopped motor vehicle showing flashing lights you must change lanes so you are not beside it; the manual also lists slowing to at least five miles per hour under the posted limit, and you give the vehicle as much room as is safe.

sec06-card-sec06-R19.front: How should you drive near an emergency scene, and when can your tires cross a fire hose?
sec06-card-sec06-R19.expected_back: Near an emergency scene, slow down and be ready to stop, and do not drive over fire hoses unless officials at the scene tell you to.

sec09-card-sec09-F01.front: What two continuous awareness habits form the foundation of safe, responsible driving in Oregon?
sec09-card-sec09-F01.expected_back: Safe, responsible driving rests on staying aware of everything around you at all times and watching for situations that could turn dangerous.

sec09-card-sec09-F02.front: Which six vehicle, road, environment, and personal factors must a defensive driver continually adjust for?
sec09-card-sec09-F02.memory_hook: Car, road, weather, traffic, light, self
sec09-card-sec09-F02.expected_back: Defensive driving means adjusting for vehicle trouble, the road surface, bad weather, heavy traffic, poor lighting and your own physical, mental and emotional state.

sec09-card-sec09-F03.front: Which directions must remain clear from the driver's seat, and what everyday items can shrink that view?
sec09-card-sec09-F03.expected_back: You must be able to see to the front, sides and rear, so never load or equip the vehicle in a way that blocks your view, and remember that window stickers or objects can cut into it.

sec09-card-sec09-F04.front: Alongside tracking nearby traffic, what backup option does a defensive driver keep ready at all times?
sec09-card-sec09-F04.expected_back: A defensive driver keeps track of the surroundings and of possible escape routes at all times.

sec09-card-sec09-F05.front: Who must buckle up under Oregon's safety-belt law?
sec09-card-sec09-F05.expected_back: Oregon requires safety belts for every driver and every passenger in all available seating positions.

sec09-card-sec09-F06.front: How tight should a safety belt sit, and where must the shoulder strap never be tucked?
sec09-card-sec09-F06.expected_back: Wear the belt with no slack in the lap or shoulder part, and never put the shoulder strap under your arm or behind your back.

sec09-card-sec09-F07.front: Until what age or height—plus fit check—must a child use an approved safety seat or booster?
sec09-card-sec09-F07.expected_back: A child must ride in an approved child safety seat until reaching eight years of age or a height of at least four feet nine inches, and the adult lap and shoulder belt must fit the child correctly.

sec09-card-sec09-F08.front: Until what birthday must infants ride in a rear-facing child seat in Oregon?
sec09-card-sec09-F08.expected_back: Infants must ride facing the rear until they are two years old.

sec09-card-sec09-F09.front: What two everyday breakdowns between drivers account for a huge share of collisions?
sec09-card-sec09-F09.expected_back: Collisions often happen because one driver fails to see another vehicle or a driver does something others do not expect.

sec09-card-sec09-F10.front: Which five built-in lights or sounds broadcast your intentions and warnings to surrounding drivers?
sec09-card-sec09-F10.expected_back: You tell other drivers what you plan to do by signaling before changing direction or lanes, showing brake lights, using headlights, using the horn as a reasonable warning and using hazard lights when needed.

sec09-card-sec09-F11.front: What three emergency maneuvers can avoid an imminent crash or soften its impact?
sec09-card-sec09-F11.expected_back: The three ways to avoid a collision or soften its impact are stopping quickly, turning quickly and speeding up.

sec09-card-sec09-F12.front: What road space makes emergency braking work, and where do you learn your car's specific brake type?
sec09-card-sec09-F12.expected_back: Stopping quickly works when you have enough distance to stop, and your owner's manual explains how to use your vehicle's brakes properly.

sec09-card-sec09-F13.front: When stopping distance runs out ahead, why is steering toward a pre-spotted escape route your best play?
sec09-card-sec09-F13.expected_back: Most vehicles can turn away faster than they can stop, so if you cannot stop in time, steer away from the collision toward an escape route you spotted by scanning.

sec09-card-sec09-F14.front: In what crash-angle scenario can pressing the gas pedal save you?
sec09-card-sec09-F14.expected_back: Speeding up can be the best escape when a vehicle is about to strike you from behind or from the side and the road ahead is open enough to get clear.

sec09-card-sec09-R20.front: How do you choose between steering away and speeding up during a split-second emergency?
sec09-card-sec09-R20.expected_back: Turning away is usually the quickest escape because most vehicles turn faster than they stop, while speeding up is the choice when the threat comes from the side or behind.

sec09-card-sec09-F15.front: If your right tires drop off the pavement edge, what two reactions must you avoid while slowing?
sec09-card-sec09-F15.expected_back: If your wheels leave the road, do not panic or brake hard; slow down until you can return to the road safely.

sec09-card-sec09-F16.front: How should your hands hold and aim the vehicle immediately after wheels drop onto a shoulder?
sec09-card-sec09-F16.expected_back: After running off the road, hold the steering wheel firmly and keep the vehicle going straight.

sec09-card-sec09-F17.front: Why must you use only minimal steering angle when climbing back over a pavement edge?
sec09-card-sec09-F17.expected_back: Steer back onto the road with only as much front wheel turn as needed, because a sharp turn can carry you across the road into oncoming traffic.

sec09-card-sec09-F18.front: What three immediate steps respond to an oncoming car drifting across the centerline into your lane?
sec09-card-sec09-F18.expected_back: If an oncoming vehicle drifts into your lane, move as far right as you can, slow down and warn the driver with your horn or lights.

sec09-card-sec09-F19.front: Why must you never swerve left into the opposing lane to dodge an oncoming drifter?
sec09-card-sec09-F19.expected_back: Never swerve into the opposing lane to dodge a drifting vehicle, since its driver may jerk back into that lane; heading for the shoulder or ditch is usually safer than a head-on crash.

sec09-card-sec09-F20.front: How should you respond to yellow animal-crossing signs or wildlife standing near the shoulder?
sec09-card-sec09-F20.expected_back: Watch for animal crossing signs and be ready to brake or slow down when passing an animal.

sec09-card-sec09-F21.front: What three legal duties trigger if your vehicle strikes and injures a domestic animal in Oregon?
sec09-card-sec09-F21.expected_back: If you hit and injure a domestic animal, stop, make a reasonable effort to check its injuries, and report it right away to the owner, or to local law enforcement if the owner cannot be found.

sec09-card-sec09-F22.front: What does a horseback rider's raised hand mean, and what must you do unless stopping causes a crash?
sec09-card-sec09-F22.expected_back: Stop for a horseback rider or someone leading an animal who raises a hand, or when the animal is clearly frightened, unless stopping would cause a collision; a raised hand signals a frightened animal.

sec09-card-sec09-F23.front: What cabin or exhaust noises must you avoid while passing horses or livestock along a road?
sec09-card-sec09-F23.expected_back: Do not honk or make other loud, sudden noises near a horse or other animal on the road.

sec09-card-sec09-R21.front: How does your horn rule flip completely between an oncoming drifting car and a frightened horse?
sec09-card-sec09-R21.expected_back: For a vehicle drifting toward you, you move right and warn it, while for a frightened animal you stop and stay quiet rather than honking.

sec09-card-sec09-F24.front: Which two fundamental changes belong whenever visibility drops or roads turn wet, snowy, or icy?
sec09-card-sec09-F24.expected_back: Reduced visibility or a wet, snowy or icy road makes driving hazardous and calls for lower speeds and longer following distances.

sec09-card-sec09-F25.front: During what daily clock span does Oregon law require headlights to burn?
sec09-card-sec09-F25.expected_back: Headlights help others see you at any hour, and they must be on from sunset to sunrise.

sec09-card-sec09-F26.front: During daytime weather, below what forward visibility footage must Oregon drivers switch headlights on?
sec09-card-sec09-F26.expected_back: Headlights must also be on whenever conditions make it hard to see people or vehicles one thousand feet ahead.

sec09-card-sec09-F27.front: Within how many feet of an oncoming vehicle must you switch high beams down to low?
sec09-card-sec09-F27.expected_back: When using high beams you must dim them once an oncoming vehicle is within five hundred feet.

sec09-card-sec09-F28.front: Within how many feet behind another vehicle must Oregon drivers dim high beams?
sec09-card-sec09-F28.expected_back: Dim your high beams when you are following another vehicle within three hundred fifty feet, since glare in its mirror can blind the driver.

sec09-card-sec09-R17.front: Compare Oregon's oncoming high-beam dimming distance against its following dimming distance?
sec09-card-sec09-R17.expected_back: High beams must be dimmed at five hundred feet for an oncoming vehicle but at three hundred fifty feet when you are following a vehicle.

sec09-card-sec09-R18.front: How do one thousand feet, five hundred feet, and three hundred fifty feet split Oregon's headlight laws?
sec09-card-sec09-R18.expected_back: The one thousand-foot visibility test decides when headlights must be on beyond the sunset-to-sunrise rule, while the five hundred-foot and three hundred fifty-foot distances decide when high beams must be dimmed.

sec09-card-sec09-F29.front: What must happen to auxiliary lights like fog lamps whenever law requires dimming your high beams?
sec09-card-sec09-F29.expected_back: Whenever you are required to dim your headlights, auxiliary lights such as fog lights must also be off.

sec09-card-sec09-F30.front: Is cruising at night or in bad weather using parking lights alone legal in Oregon?
sec09-card-sec09-F30.expected_back: Driving at night or in bad weather with only your parking lights on is illegal.

sec09-card-sec09-F31.front: When do parking lights perform their actual legal job on a roadway or shoulder?
sec09-card-sec09-F31.expected_back: A vehicle stopped or parked on a road or its shoulder in limited visibility must show its parking lights.

sec09-card-sec09-F32.front: Why is your reaction margin naturally tighter after dark than in daylight?
sec09-card-sec09-F32.expected_back: At night you react later because you can see only as far as your headlights reach, so adjust how you drive.

sec09-card-sec09-F33.front: Where should you aim your eyes to avoid getting blinded by oncoming headlights at night?
sec09-card-sec09-F33.expected_back: To cut glare from oncoming headlights, look a little to the right of them and follow the road edge or fog line.

sec09-card-sec09-F34.front: What two maintenance checks keep your exterior lighting effective year-round?
sec09-card-sec09-F34.expected_back: Check often that your headlights, taillights and turn signals work and that their lenses are clean.

sec09-card-sec09-F35.front: What hidden danger makes two-lane passing at dawn or dusk extra risky?
sec09-card-sec09-F35.expected_back: Take care passing at dawn or dusk, because an oncoming vehicle may have no headlights on and you may not see it in time.

sec09-card-sec09-F36.front: Which two vulnerable road-user groups demand extra nighttime alertness because dark clothing hides them?
sec09-card-sec09-F36.expected_back: Stay alert at night for bicyclists and pedestrians, who are harder to see in the dark.

sec09-card-sec09-F37.front: Which headlight setting belongs in fog, dust, or smoke—and why does the brighter setting fail?
sec09-card-sec09-F37.expected_back: In fog, dust, smoke or any low-visibility area, use low beam headlights, because high beams reflect back as glare and make it harder to see.

sec09-card-sec09-R19.front: Why do high beams worsen visibility in thick fog despite producing stronger light?
sec09-card-sec09-R19.expected_back: In fog, dust or smoke you use low beams, not high beams, even though high beams seem brighter, because their light bounces back as glare.

sec09-card-sec09-F38.front: When thick fog or storms force you off the road, where do you park and what lights go on?
sec09-card-sec09-F38.expected_back: As visibility drops, slow down, watch for slow or stopped vehicles and obstacles, and be ready to pull over; if you leave the road, pull as far right as you can and turn on your hazard lights.

sec09-card-sec09-F39.front: How should rain change both the timing and foot pressure of your braking?
sec09-card-sec09-F39.expected_back: Rain cuts how far you can see and lengthens braking distance, so on wet roads brake earlier and more gently than usual.

sec09-card-sec09-F40.front: Why can a light summer rain shower make dry asphalt unexpectedly slick?
sec09-card-sec09-F40.expected_back: Even a summer shower can make roads slippery when the rain mixes with oil and dirt on the pavement.

sec09-card-sec09-F41.front: What three settings—for headlights, cruise control, and interior glass—belong whenever wipers run in rain?
sec09-card-sec09-F41.expected_back: Turn on your headlights whenever your windshield wipers are running, skip cruise control on wet roads, and keep the windows free of moisture.

sec09-card-sec09-F42.front: What happens to your tires and vehicle controls during hydroplaning?
sec09-card-sec09-F42.expected_back: Hydroplaning is when tires skim or float on a wet surface and you can partly or fully lose the ability to steer and stop, so slow down when roads are wet.

sec09-card-sec09-F43.front: How do you restore stopping bite right after splashing through deep water soaks your brakes?
sec09-card-sec09-F43.expected_back: If the brakes get wet after driving through water, drive slowly and press the brakes gently until they respond, doing this as soon as you can.

sec09-card-sec09-F44.front: What two serious failures make driving through flooded roadways too dangerous to risk?
sec09-card-sec09-F44.expected_back: Do not drive through flooded areas, because high water can make you lose control or stall the engine.

sec09-card-sec09-F45.front: What speed, gap, window, and cruise-control rules govern driving on snow and ice?
sec09-card-sec09-F45.expected_back: Snow and ice hide the road ahead and lengthen braking distance, so drive slower, leave more space, clear snow, ice and fog off the windows, and leave cruise control off.

sec09-card-sec09-R01.front: When should you skip driving altogether during severe winter weather?
sec09-card-sec09-R01.expected_back: Follow weather forecasts and warnings, and stay off the road when police or highway officials say driving is very hazardous.

sec09-card-sec09-R02.front: Why must you press the accelerator gently when pulling out on snow or ice?
sec09-card-sec09-R02.expected_back: On snow or ice, press the gas pedal gently, because too much power can spin the tires or slide the vehicle.

sec09-card-sec09-R03.front: How should you work the brake pedal on snowy or icy pavement to avoid skidding?
sec09-card-sec09-R03.expected_back: On snow or ice, press and release the brakes gently, since slamming them will likely send the vehicle into a skid.

sec09-card-sec09-R04.front: How can you safely gauge road slickness right after starting out on snow or ice?
sec09-card-sec09-R04.expected_back: When you start out on snow or ice, get the feel of the road away from traffic and test the brakes lightly so you know how they will respond.

sec09-card-sec09-R05.front: How should you carry speed through turns when snow or ice coats the pavement?
sec09-card-sec09-R05.expected_back: Take turns on snow or ice at a reduced, steady speed to avoid skidding.

sec09-card-sec09-R06.front: Which two roadway locations freeze into ice patches while open sunlit stretches remain wet?
sec09-card-sec09-R06.expected_back: Bridges and shaded spots freeze first and can be icy while the rest of the road is clear.

sec09-card-sec09-R07.front: How much throttle belongs while climbing a snow-covered or icy upgrade?
sec09-card-sec09-R07.expected_back: Climbing a snowy or icy hill, give the vehicle just enough power to keep moving without spinning the wheels.

sec09-card-sec09-R08.front: Is an icy road slicker right near freezing or when temperatures plunge far below zero?
sec09-card-sec09-R08.expected_back: A road is likely to be most slippery when the temperature is close to freezing, more so than when it is well below freezing.

sec09-card-sec09-R09.front: What happens physically when a car skids, and what driver error triggers it?
sec09-card-sec09-R09.expected_back: A skid happens when the tires can no longer grip the road, and driving too fast for conditions is what causes it.

sec09-card-sec09-R10.front: Why does Oregon's manual tell you to stay off the brake pedal during a skid?
sec09-card-sec09-R10.expected_back: In a skid, stay off the brakes, because they will not work well until the vehicle slows.

sec09-card-sec09-R11.front: Where do you steer in a skid, and why straighten promptly as the nose recovers?
sec09-card-sec09-R11.expected_back: In a skid, steer the way you want the vehicle to go, turn the wheel back as soon as it starts to straighten so it does not swing the other way, and keep correcting left and right until you are back in control.

sec09-card-sec09-R12.front: What two winter-equipment duties can posted Oregon highway signs require?
sec09-card-sec09-R12.expected_back: Signs may require you to carry or to use chains or traction tires.

sec09-card-sec09-R13.front: Beyond steel link chains, what else legally qualifies as chains in Oregon?
sec09-card-sec09-R13.expected_back: In Oregon, chains include link chains, cable chains and any other device fastened to the wheel, the vehicle or the outside of the tire that is built to add traction on snow and ice.

sec09-card-sec09-R14.front: Which three tire types qualify as legal traction tires in Oregon—and what sidewall symbol marks non-studded ones?
sec09-card-sec09-R14.expected_back: Traction tires are studded tires, retractable studded tires or tires that meet the tire industry definition for severe snow use, which carry a mountain and snowflake emblem on the sidewall.

sec09-card-sec09-R15.front: Between which calendar dates are studded tires generally permitted in Oregon, and why are alternatives urged?
sec09-card-sec09-R15.expected_back: Studded tires are generally allowed in Oregon only from November one through March thirty-one, and because studs damage roads, drivers are urged to use chains or other traction tires instead.

sec09-card-sec09-R16.front: Where do state transportation officials post live Oregon chain and traction-tire requirements?
sec09-card-sec09-R16.expected_back: Chain and traction tire requirements are published by ODOT on TripCheck.com.

sec10-card-sec10-F01.front: How do mental, emotional, and physical conditions like anger, worry, illness, or fatigue shape driving?
sec10-card-sec10-F01.expected_back: Your mental and emotional state and your physical health shape how you drive, and poor health, fatigue or feelings such as anger or worry can make you unsafe.

sec10-card-sec10-F02.front: What should you do immediately if you catch yourself driving on autopilot without tracking traffic?
sec10-card-sec10-F02.expected_back: If you notice you are just going through the motions without really tracking what is happening around you, stop to rest or end your driving for the day.

sec10-card-sec10-F03.front: What is Oregon's mobile-device law for drivers under eighteen—even with Bluetooth or speakerphone?
sec10-card-sec10-F03.expected_back: Drivers under eighteen years of age may not use a cell phone or any other mobile electronic device while driving, so turn it off or put it in the back seat.

sec10-card-sec10-F04.front: How may an Oregon driver age eighteen or older legally use a mobile electronic device?
sec10-card-sec10-F04.expected_back: Drivers eighteen or older may use a cell phone or other mobile electronic device only with a hands-free accessory that needs no more than minimal finger use to switch on or off.

sec10-card-sec10-R08.front: How does turning eighteen change Oregon's mobile-device restriction behind the wheel?
sec10-card-sec10-R08.expected_back: A driver under eighteen may not use a phone at all while driving, while a driver eighteen or older may use one only through a hands-free accessory.

sec10-card-sec10-F05.front: What does Oregon law say about mounting a television, tablet, or video screen in the cabin?
sec10-card-sec10-F05.expected_back: It is illegal to have a TV, tablet or other video display where the driver can see it.

sec10-card-sec10-F06.front: At what outside distance does booming car audio become illegal in Oregon—and why?
sec10-card-sec10-F06.expected_back: It is illegal to play a radio or other sound system loud enough to be heard fifty feet from your vehicle, since you need to hear horns, screeching tires and sirens.

sec10-card-sec10-F07.front: Why are eating, drinking, reading, grooming, or peeling off a jacket hazardous while rolling?
sec10-card-sec10-F07.expected_back: Anything that takes your eyes off the road while driving is dangerous, such as texting, reading, eating, drinking, putting on makeup or taking off clothing.

sec10-card-sec10-F08.front: May you drive with a small dog, child, or parcel resting in your lap or arms?
sec10-card-sec10-F08.expected_back: Never hold a person, a pet or a package in your lap or arms while driving.

sec10-card-sec10-F09.front: What must you do first when children, pets, or passengers in back need hands-on help?
sec10-card-sec10-F09.expected_back: Do not turn around to tend to passengers, children or pets; if they need attention, pull to the side of the road and park first.

sec10-card-sec10-F10.front: Which angry behaviors behind the wheel constitute road rage in Oregon's manual?
sec10-card-sec10-F10.expected_back: Road rage is angry or aggressive behavior by drivers, such as driving in an illegal, unsafe or threatening way, shouting or making rude gestures.

sec10-card-sec10-F11.front: How should you respond when an angry, aggressive motorist tailgates or crowds you?
sec10-card-sec10-F11.expected_back: If you meet an aggressive driver, stay out of the way and do not challenge them by speeding up or trying to out-drive them.

sec10-card-sec10-F12.front: Which five physical or lane-keeping red flags warn you are about to fall asleep driving?
sec10-card-sec10-F12.expected_back: Frequent yawning, head nodding, heavy eyelids, blurred vision and drifting out of your lane are signs you may be falling asleep at the wheel.

sec10-card-sec10-F13.front: Which two driving abilities drop when you are tired, and how do you prevent drowsy crashes?
sec10-card-sec10-F13.expected_back: A tired driver reacts more slowly and notices changing road and traffic conditions less, so be well rested before and during a trip and take breaks when you feel tired.

sec10-card-sec10-F14.front: Instead of pushing drowsy miles to finish a trip, what two stops restore safety?
sec10-card-sec10-F14.expected_back: Never keep driving drowsy just to reach your destination; pull over somewhere safe to rest, or get out for a brisk walk.

sec10-card-sec10-F15.front: Why does drinking water—paired with conversation and sharing wheel shifts—help fight trip fatigue?
sec10-card-sec10-F15.expected_back: To stay awake, drink water because dehydration causes fatigue, talk with your passenger, and take turns driving so each driver can rest.

sec10-card-sec10-F16.front: What common medication side effect must every driver watch out for before picking up keys?
sec10-card-sec10-F16.expected_back: Be wary of medicines that can make you drowsy.

sec10-card-sec10-F17.front: What honest self-check belongs before driving with an illness, especially ahead of a long drive?
sec10-card-sec10-F17.expected_back: If you are sick, think honestly about whether you are fit to drive, especially for a long trip.

sec10-card-sec10-F18.front: Because certain health conditions risk confusion, slow reactions, or blackouts, whom should you consult?
sec10-card-sec10-F18.expected_back: Some medical conditions can cause confusion, slower reaction time or a sudden loss of consciousness, so ask your doctor how your condition may affect your driving.

sec10-card-sec10-F19.front: Which four safety clues do your ears catch while driving?
sec10-card-sec10-F19.expected_back: Hearing matters while driving: tire noise changes with the road surface, engine noise can signal a problem, sound can reveal a vehicle in your blind spot, and you need to hear emergency vehicles.

sec10-card-sec10-F20.front: Why does Oregon's manual tell drivers not to wear ear-covering or sound-blocking headphones?
sec10-card-sec10-F20.expected_back: Do not wear headphones that could reduce your hearing while driving.

sec10-card-sec10-F21.front: What is the only safe plan after drinking alcohol or using impairing drugs?
sec10-card-sec10-F21.expected_back: Never drive after drinking alcohol or using other drugs, because they raise your chance of a collision that can cause serious injury or death; let someone else drive.

sec10-card-sec10-F22.front: Can police arrest you for impaired driving whenever alcohol or drugs noticeably affect your driving?
sec10-card-sec10-F22.expected_back: Driving while alcohol or drugs are affecting you can get you arrested for DUII.

sec10-card-sec10-F24.front: Which drug leads impaired crashes, what second substance adds major Oregon crashes, and what happens together?
sec10-card-sec10-F24.expected_back: Alcohol is the drug most often involved in impaired driving, marijuana impairment has also contributed to many Oregon collisions, and using the two together further reduces your ability to drive.

sec10-card-sec10-F25.front: How should you verify store-shelf or prescription medicines, and what if a new dose feels uncertain?
sec10-card-sec10-F25.expected_back: Over-the-counter and prescription medicines can also impair driving, so ask a doctor or pharmacist about side effects, and if you are unsure after starting a new medicine, use other transportation.

sec10-card-sec10-F26.front: Does Oregon's impaired-driving law apply solely to alcohol, or how broad is its reach?
sec10-card-sec10-F26.expected_back: Oregon's DUII law covers any substance that impairs your mental or physical ability to drive, not just alcohol.

sec10-card-sec10-F27.front: Which three chemical tests have you already agreed to take simply by driving on Oregon roads?
sec10-card-sec10-F27.expected_back: Under Oregon's Implied Consent law, driving a motor vehicle means you have agreed to take a breath, blood or urine test when a police officer asks.

sec10-card-sec10-F28.front: Which two penalties hit a driver who refuses an officer's implied-consent test?
sec10-card-sec10-F28.expected_back: Refusing an implied consent test can bring a fine, a suspension of your driving privileges, or both.

sec10-card-sec10-R11.front: Why doesn't refusing a breath, blood, or urine test dodge impaired-driving consequences?
sec10-card-sec10-R11.expected_back: Refusing the implied consent test is not a way out, since refusal itself can bring a fine and a suspension of driving privileges.

sec10-card-sec10-F29.front: What blood alcohol concentration fails the test for any Oregon driver under twenty-one?
sec10-card-sec10-F29.expected_back: Oregon has a zero tolerance law: a driver under twenty-one fails the test with a blood alcohol concentration of any amount.

sec10-card-sec10-F31.front: What does Oregon's Open Container law prohibit inside a vehicle on any road?
sec10-card-sec10-F31.expected_back: Oregon's Open Container law makes it illegal to have an open bottle or other container of alcohol in a vehicle on any road.

sec10-card-sec10-F32.front: When does a bottle count as open, and where must a previously opened bottle ride?
sec10-card-sec10-F32.expected_back: A container counts as open once its seal is broken, even if it has been closed again, and any open container belongs in the trunk.

sec10-card-sec10-R12.front: Does screwing the cap tightly back onto an unsealed liquor bottle make it legal inside the passenger cabin?
sec10-card-sec10-R12.expected_back: Open alcohol containers should ride in the trunk, and a bottle whose seal has been broken counts as open even after it is recapped.

sec10-card-sec10-F33.front: Who does Oregon's manual say should ride inside an open pickup bed or on a vehicle's exterior?
sec10-card-sec10-F33.expected_back: No one of any age should ride in a pickup bed or on any outside part of a vehicle.

sec10-card-sec10-F34.front: For passengers under eighteen, what does Oregon law strictly outlaw regarding pickup beds, hoods, or fenders?
sec10-card-sec10-F34.expected_back: Oregon law forbids anyone under eighteen from riding on a hood, fender, running board, pickup bed or other outside part of a vehicle.

sec10-card-sec10-F35.front: Under what condition may a dog legally ride in an open pickup bed in Oregon?
sec10-card-sec10-F35.expected_back: A dog may ride on an outside part of a vehicle, including a pickup bed, only if a framework, carrier or other device keeps it from falling off.

sec10-card-sec10-R13.front: Compare Oregon's pickup-bed rules across adults, riders under eighteen, and dogs?
sec10-card-sec10-R13.expected_back: Riding outside the cab is discouraged for everyone but outlawed for anyone under eighteen, while a dog may ride outside only when a carrier or framework keeps it from falling.

sec10-card-sec10-F36.front: What habit prevents most mechanical road failures, and what guide lists your car's service schedule?
sec10-card-sec10-F36.expected_back: Good maintenance prevents most equipment failures, an unmaintained vehicle can become unsafe, and your owner's manual lists the maintenance it needs.

sec10-card-sec10-F37.front: How does a front-tire blowout feel through the wheel compared with a rear-tire blowout?
sec10-card-sec10-F37.expected_back: A front tire blowout makes steering hard and can pull the vehicle strongly to one side, while a rear blowout makes the back of the vehicle weave or sway.

sec10-card-sec10-F38.front: What three calm steps bring a vehicle safely off the road after any tire blows out?
sec10-card-sec10-F38.expected_back: After a blowout, grip the steering wheel firmly, slow down gradually and pull off the road.

sec10-card-sec10-R14.front: Even though front blowouts pull and rear blowouts sway, does your recovery action change?
sec10-card-sec10-R14.expected_back: A front blowout shows up as hard steering and a pull to one side, while a rear blowout shows up as weaving or swaying of the back end; the response is the same: grip, slow gradually, pull off.

sec10-card-sec10-F39.front: What is the immediate first pedal action to try if your service brakes suddenly lose pressure?
sec10-card-sec10-F39.expected_back: If your brakes fail, pump the pedal, which may build enough pressure to get them working again.

sec10-card-sec10-F40.front: If pumping failed brakes isn't enough, how do your transmission and parking brake help scrub speed?
sec10-card-sec10-F40.expected_back: With failed brakes, shift to a lower gear so the engine helps slow the vehicle, and apply the parking brake slowly.

sec10-card-sec10-F41.front: With failed brakes, how do you alert surrounding traffic and where do you guide the car?
sec10-card-sec10-F41.expected_back: With failed brakes, warn other drivers with your horn or lights that you cannot control the vehicle, and once you have slowed, ease onto the shoulder.

sec10-card-sec10-R01.front: If your headlights suddenly cut out at night, which switches should you try immediately?
sec10-card-sec10-R01.expected_back: If your headlights go out, flip the headlight switch off and on, then try your high beams, driving lights or hazard lights, which may give enough light to steer off the road.

sec10-card-sec10-R02.front: Once backup flashers or beams give minimal sight after headlight failure, where do you go?
sec10-card-sec10-R02.expected_back: After a headlight failure, slow down and ease onto the shoulder.

sec10-card-sec10-R03.front: Does steering lock solid if power-steering assist fails—and how should you handle it?
sec10-card-sec10-R03.expected_back: If power steering fails, grip the wheel firmly because steering will be hard, then slow down and ease onto the shoulder.

sec10-card-sec10-R04.front: If the accelerator sticks down, how and with what hand technique should you shift?
sec10-card-sec10-R04.expected_back: If the accelerator sticks, look for an escape path and shift into neutral, using an open palm on the shifter so you do not push it into another gear.

sec10-card-sec10-R05.front: After shifting a runaway engine into neutral, how do you bring the vehicle off the highway?
sec10-card-sec10-R05.expected_back: With a stuck accelerator, steer smoothly while braking and leave the road once it is safe.

sec10-card-sec10-R15.front: Why do failed brakes want a lower gear whereas a stuck accelerator wants neutral?
sec10-card-sec10-R15.expected_back: Failed brakes call for pumping the pedal and downshifting, whereas a stuck accelerator calls for shifting to neutral and braking while steering smoothly.

sec10-card-sec10-R06.front: How do your speed choice, launches, and stops save gasoline on everyday drives?
sec10-card-sec10-R06.expected_back: To save fuel, drive at a steady pace without going over posted limits, and avoid jackrabbit starts and sudden stops.

sec10-card-sec10-R07.front: Beyond smooth pedal habits, what three planning and upkeep choices stretch fuel mileage?
sec10-card-sec10-R07.expected_back: Other fuel savers are cutting unneeded idling, combining errands into one trip and keeping the vehicle properly maintained.

sec11-card-sec11-F01.front: Which everyday vehicles—and up to what gross weight—does an Oregon non-commercial Class C license cover?
sec11-card-sec11-F01.expected_back: A Class C non-commercial driving privilege lets you drive a passenger car, moped, autocycle, van or pickup weighing no more than twenty-six thousand pounds that does not require a commercial driver license or a motorcycle endorsement.

sec11-card-sec11-F02.front: What is the minimum age to apply for an Oregon instruction permit?
sec11-card-sec11-F02.expected_back: You must be at least fifteen years old to apply for an instruction permit.

sec11-card-sec11-F03.front: What is the minimum age to apply for an Oregon driver license?
sec11-card-sec11-F03.expected_back: You must be at least sixteen years old to apply for a driver license.

sec11-card-sec11-R11.front: How do Oregon's minimum instruction-permit age and minimum driver-license age step up?
sec11-card-sec11-R11.expected_back: The instruction permit age is fifteen, while the driver license age is sixteen.

sec11-card-sec11-F04.front: Who must sign an electronic application for a minor under eighteen—and what if that adult cannot attend?
sec11-card-sec11-F04.expected_back: You apply with an electronic application, and an applicant under eighteen needs a parent or legal guardian to sign it, or to sign form seven hundred thirty-five-173DP if that adult cannot come to DMV.

sec11-card-sec11-F05.front: Which two legal statuses waive the parent-signature requirement for an applicant under eighteen?
sec11-card-sec11-F05.expected_back: An applicant who is emancipated or married shows proof of that status and then needs no parent or guardian signature.

sec11-card-sec11-F06.front: Which three core facts must every Oregon permit or license applicant prove?
sec11-card-sec11-F06.expected_back: Every applicant must present proof of identity, date of birth and residence address.

sec11-card-sec11-F07.front: How do you satisfy Oregon's Social Security Number rule if one has never been issued to you?
sec11-card-sec11-F07.expected_back: You must provide your Social Security Number or certify electronically that you do not have one.

sec11-card-sec11-F08.front: What school-status proof must a first-time Oregon applicant under eighteen provide?
sec11-card-sec11-F08.expected_back: A first-time applicant under eighteen needs a parent or guardian to certify school enrollment or attendance, or, if no longer in school, must show a high school diploma or GED certificate.

sec11-card-sec11-F09.front: Along with paying required fees, which three exams unlock an Oregon driving privilege?
sec11-card-sec11-F09.expected_back: To get the privilege you must pass the required knowledge, vision and drive tests and pay the applicable fees.

sec11-card-sec11-F10.front: Which four head, face, or eye items must come off before your Oregon license photo?
sec11-card-sec11-F10.expected_back: For the license photo, hats, glasses, face paint or other temporary substances on the face, and contact lenses that change how the eye looks, are not allowed.

sec11-card-sec11-F11.front: How do out-of-state suspensions and existing licenses or identification cards affect getting an Oregon license?
sec11-card-sec11-F11.expected_back: You cannot be under suspension, revocation or cancellation in Oregon or any other state, and you must surrender any other driving privilege or ID card.

sec11-card-sec11-F12.front: How long must a teen under eighteen hold an instruction permit—and does out-of-state permit time count?
sec11-card-sec11-F12.expected_back: An applicant under eighteen must have held an instruction permit for at least six months before getting a license, and time on an out-of-state permit counts.

sec11-card-sec11-F13.front: What are the two supervised-driving hour options for an Oregon license applicant under eighteen?
sec11-card-sec11-F13.expected_back: An applicant under eighteen needs one hundred hours of supervised driving, or fifty hours plus an ODOT-approved traffic safety education course whose completion proof DMV must receive.

sec11-card-sec11-F14.front: What minimum age and license tenure must your front-seat supervisor hold for teen practice hours to count?
sec11-card-sec11-F14.expected_back: Supervised practice counts only when the supervisor is at least twenty-one years old and has held valid driving privileges for at least three years.

sec11-card-sec11-R12.front: How does finishing an approved driver-education course change a teen's supervised-practice total?
sec11-card-sec11-R12.expected_back: A teen applicant reaches the practice requirement either with one hundred supervised hours alone, or with fifty supervised hours combined with an ODOT-approved traffic safety education course.

sec11-card-sec11-R13.front: Keep the two teen-practice time rules straight: permit holding months versus supervisor licensed years?
sec11-card-sec11-R13.expected_back: The teen permit must be held at least six months, while the practice supervisor must be at least twenty-one and licensed for at least three years.

sec11-card-sec11-F15.front: In what physical document format must identity and birth-date proofs be presented?
sec11-card-sec11-F15.expected_back: Documents used as proof of identity and date of birth must be originals or certified copies from the agency that issued them.

sec11-card-sec11-F16.front: Which birth certificate proves identity in Oregon—and which two keepsake records get rejected?
sec11-card-sec11-F16.expected_back: A U.S. government-issued birth certificate is accepted proof, but hospital-issued birth certificates and baptismal records are not.

sec11-card-sec11-F17.front: How long past its printed expiration date can a United States passport or passport card still prove identity?
sec11-card-sec11-F17.expected_back: A U.S. passport or passport card is accepted if it is valid or has been expired no more than five years.

sec11-card-sec11-F18.front: Which tribal identification cards and federal citizenship certificates prove identity in Oregon?
sec11-card-sec11-F18.expected_back: A DMV-approved tribal ID card from a federally recognized tribe located in Oregon is accepted, as is a Certificate of Naturalization or Certificate of Citizenship.

sec11-card-sec11-F19.front: Up to how many years past expiration are federal work, permanent-resident, re-entry, or foreign-passport documents accepted?
sec11-card-sec11-F19.expected_back: An Employment Authorization Card (I-seven hundred sixty-six), Permanent Resident Card (I-five hundred fifty-one), foreign passport, Re-entry Permit (I-three hundred twenty-seven) or Refugee Travel Document (I-five hundred seventy-one) is accepted if valid or expired no more than five years.

sec11-card-sec11-F20.front: How long past expiration does Oregon accept an official consulate card for identity?
sec11-card-sec11-F20.expected_back: A consulate card is accepted if it is valid or has been expired no more than five years.

sec11-card-sec11-F21.front: Up to how many years after expiring can an old Oregon license, permit, or identification card prove identity?
sec11-card-sec11-F21.expected_back: An Oregon driver license, permit or ID card is accepted as proof if valid or expired no more than thirteen years.

sec11-card-sec11-F22.front: How long past expiration is an out-of-state license, permit, or identification card accepted as Oregon identity proof?
sec11-card-sec11-F22.expected_back: An out-of-state driver license, permit or ID card is accepted as proof only if valid or expired no more than one year.

sec11-card-sec11-R14.front: Contrast Oregon's post-expiration identity window for an Oregon card versus an out-of-state card?
sec11-card-sec11-R14.expected_back: An expired Oregon license, permit or ID card can still prove identity for up to thirteen years after expiry, while an expired out-of-state card counts for only up to one year.

sec11-card-sec11-F23.front: What extra documentation is required when your current legal name differs from your birth or identity record?
sec11-card-sec11-F23.expected_back: If your current legal name differs from the name on your identity document, you must also prove the legal name change.

sec11-card-sec11-F24.front: How many qualifying documents are needed to prove your Oregon residence address on a standard application?
sec11-card-sec11-F24.expected_back: One document is enough to prove your residence address when you apply.

sec11-card-sec11-F25.front: If you have no bills in your own name yet, how can someone living with you verify your address?
sec11-card-sec11-F25.expected_back: Someone who lives at your address can certify it, but that person must come with you and show proof of the address, such as their own license or ID card.

sec11-card-sec11-F26.front: Which sender types qualify as address-proof mail—and which two everyday mail types get rejected?
sec11-card-sec11-F26.expected_back: Mail from a business, school or government agency showing your first and last name proves your address, but personal mail and forwarded mail do not.

sec11-card-sec11-F27.front: Which four school, utility, or homeownership records also prove your Oregon residence address?
sec11-card-sec11-F27.expected_back: A document from an educational provider, a utility hookup order or bill, a mortgage document or a property tax statement can also prove your address.

sec11-card-sec11-F29.front: What two card markings appear when you join Oregon's organ, eye, and tissue donor registry?
sec11-card-sec11-F29.expected_back: When you are issued a driving privilege you can join the organ, eye and tissue donor registry, and DMV adds a heart symbol to the front of the card and the words Anatomical Donor to the back.

sec11-card-sec11-F30.front: What military discharge paperwork and discharge character earn a veteran designation on an Oregon card?
sec11-card-sec11-F30.expected_back: A veteran may ask for a veteran designation by showing a DD214 or DD215 form that shows discharge under honorable conditions.

sec11-card-sec11-F31.front: What medical proof is needed for a deaf or hard-of-hearing card designation—and who sees it?
sec11-card-sec11-F31.expected_back: You may ask DMV to add a deaf or hard of hearing designation with no proof required, and it is also visible to law enforcement through your DMV record.

sec11-card-sec11-R17.front: How do documentation rules differ between adding a veteran designation and a deaf-or-hard-of-hearing designation?
sec11-card-sec11-R17.expected_back: A veteran designation requires a discharge document as proof, while a deaf or hard of hearing designation requires no proof at all.

sec11-card-sec11-F32.front: What are Oregon's minimum bodily-injury liability limits for one person versus two or more people per crash?
sec11-card-sec11-F32.expected_back: Oregon's minimum bodily injury coverage is twenty-five thousand dollars per collision for one person and fifty thousand dollars per collision for injury to or death of two or more people.

sec11-card-sec11-F33.front: What is Oregon's minimum per-crash liability coverage for damaging someone else's vehicle or property?
sec11-card-sec11-F33.expected_back: Oregon's minimum property damage coverage is twenty thousand dollars per collision for damage to other people's property.

sec11-card-sec11-R15.front: Put Oregon's three core liability numbers together: one injured person, multiple injured, and property damage?
sec11-card-sec11-R15.expected_back: The minimum liability limits are twenty-five thousand dollars for injury to one person and fifty thousand dollars for two or more people per collision, while the separate property damage minimum is twenty thousand dollars.

sec11-card-sec11-F34.front: At least how much Personal Injury Protection per person—and over what post-crash timespan—does Oregon require?
sec11-card-sec11-F34.expected_back: Personal Injury Protection must be at least fifteen thousand dollars per person for reasonable and necessary medical, dental and other expenses incurred within two years after the injury.

sec11-card-sec11-F35.front: What minimum per-person and per-crash bodily-injury amounts apply to Oregon Uninsured Motorist coverage?
sec11-card-sec11-F35.expected_back: Uninsured Motorist Coverage must be at least twenty-five thousand dollars per person and fifty thousand dollars per collision for bodily injury.

sec11-card-sec11-R16.front: How does Oregon's Personal Injury Protection dollar minimum differ from Uninsured Motorist bodily-injury minimums?
sec11-card-sec11-R16.expected_back: Personal Injury Protection is set at fifteen thousand dollars per person, while Uninsured Motorist Coverage is set at twenty-five thousand dollars per person and fifty thousand dollars per collision.

sec11-card-sec11-F36.front: Why does Oregon's manual reject calling a distracted, drowsy, or careless crash an accident?
sec11-card-sec11-F36.expected_back: The manual calls the word accident misleading: a collision caused by being distracted, tired or not driving defensively is a preventable collision.

sec11-card-sec11-F37.front: After an uninjured fender-bender where cars still drive safely, what must you do before trading details?
sec11-card-sec11-F37.expected_back: After a collision you must stop, and if no one is hurt and the vehicles can be moved safely, get them out of the travel lanes quickly and swap information away from the scene.

sec11-card-sec11-F38.front: What two duties govern helping someone hurt in a collision?
sec11-card-sec11-F38.expected_back: You must give reasonable help to anyone injured in a collision, and injured people should never be moved carelessly.

sec11-card-sec11-F39.front: Which five pieces of identification and coverage info must drivers exchange after a collision?
sec11-card-sec11-F39.expected_back: After a collision, give your name, address, driver license number, vehicle plate number and insurance details to the other driver, passengers or any injured pedestrian involved.

sec11-card-sec11-F40.front: Which two severe victim conditions require staying at a crash scene until law enforcement arrives?
sec11-card-sec11-F40.expected_back: If anyone is killed or unconscious after a collision, stay at the scene until police arrive.

sec11-card-sec11-R01.front: Within how many hours—and above what dollar damage to your car or non-vehicle property—must you report?
sec11-card-sec11-R01.expected_back: You must file a collision report on Form seven hundred thirty-five-thirty-two within seventy-two hours when damage to the vehicle you were driving is over two thousand five hundred dollars, or damage to property other than a vehicle is over two thousand five hundred dollars.

sec11-card-sec11-R02.front: How do vehicle damage and towing combine to trigger an Oregon seventy-two-hour collision report?
sec11-card-sec11-R02.expected_back: A collision report is also required within seventy-two hours when any vehicle has more than two thousand five hundred dollars of damage and any vehicle is towed from the scene because of collision damage.

sec11-card-sec11-R03.front: Regardless of bumper repair cost, what human outcome always triggers a mandatory Oregon collision report?
sec11-card-sec11-R03.expected_back: A collision report is also required whenever the collision causes injury or death.

sec11-card-sec11-R04.front: When does the registered vehicle owner—rather than the driver—have to file Oregon's collision report?
sec11-card-sec11-R04.expected_back: A vehicle owner must file the collision report when the owner's vehicle was in a reportable collision and the driver fails to report it.

sec11-card-sec11-R05.front: If a police officer writes an official crash report at the scene, are you excused from filing yours?
sec11-card-sec11-R05.expected_back: A police report does not replace your duty to file your own collision report with DMV.

sec11-card-sec11-R06.front: What must you do after bumping an unoccupied parked vehicle if you cannot locate its owner?
sec11-card-sec11-R06.expected_back: If you hit an unoccupied vehicle, try to find its owner, and if you cannot, leave a note with your name, address and a short account of what happened.

sec11-card-sec11-R07.front: What duty applies if your car knocks over a mailbox, fence, sign, or landscaping?
sec11-card-sec11-R07.expected_back: Damaging something that is not a motor vehicle carries the same duty: look for its owner or whoever is in charge of it and tell them about the damage.

sec11-card-sec11-R08.front: What ongoing performance standard determines whether you keep your Oregon driving privilege?
sec11-card-sec11-R08.expected_back: Keeping your driving privilege depends on keeping a good driving record.

sec11-card-sec11-R09.front: Which three major violations—involving impairment, crashes, or coverage—can strip your Oregon driving privilege?
sec11-card-sec11-R09.expected_back: You can lose your driving privilege for driving under the influence of alcohol, drugs or inhalants, for failing to report a collision, or for driving uninsured.

sec11-card-sec11-R10.front: How can stacked traffic tickets or ignored court fines affect your Oregon license?
sec11-card-sec11-R10.expected_back: Too many traffic convictions, handled through the Driver Improvement Program, and failing to comply with court fines can also cost you your privilege, and the manual says its list is not complete.

sec08-card-sec08-F01.front: What visual checks and right-of-way rule apply every time you pull out from a parked or stopped spot?
sec08-card-sec08-F01.expected_back: When you pull out from a parked or stopped position, check your mirrors and blind spots and yield to all other traffic.

sec08-card-sec08-R02.front: Before rolling away from a curb or stopped spot, who holds the right of way and where must you look?
sec08-card-sec08-R02.expected_back: Before pulling out from a parked or stopped spot, check mirrors and blind spots and yield to all other traffic.

sec08-card-sec08-F02.front: Which direction must your car face whenever you parallel park along a street?
sec08-card-sec08-F02.expected_back: When parallel parking, face the same direction that traffic moves in that lane.

sec08-card-sec08-F03.front: What is the maximum distance your tires may sit from a curb when parallel parked, or where do you park without a curb?
sec08-card-sec08-F03.expected_back: Park parallel to the curb and no more than twelve inches from it, or if there is no curb, as close as you can to the edge of the shoulder.

sec08-card-sec08-R01.front: How does Oregon's parallel parking distance rule change when a street has no curb?
sec08-card-sec08-R01.expected_back: With a curb you stay within twelve inches of it, but with no curb you simply get as close as you can to the shoulder edge, with no set number.

sec08-card-sec08-F04.front: Where must all of your tires rest when parking in a marked stall?
sec08-card-sec08-F04.expected_back: Where parking spaces are marked, your wheels must be inside the marked space.

sec08-card-sec08-F05.front: What three steering and backing steps does the Oregon manual list for parallel parking behind Car A?
sec08-card-sec08-F05.expected_back: The manual's parallel parking steps are to pull even with the car labeled Car A, back slowly into the space while turning the wheels sharply, and then straighten the wheels.

sec08-card-sec08-F06.front: In which three types of places do you most often encounter angle parking?
sec08-card-sec08-F06.expected_back: Angle parking is common in parking lots, at shopping centers and on wide streets.

sec08-card-sec08-F07.front: When must drivers of long or large vehicles skip an angle parking stall?
sec08-card-sec08-F07.expected_back: When driving a large vehicle, avoid angle spaces where your vehicle would stick out and block traffic on the road.

sec08-card-sec08-F08.front: What special entry rule may posted signs require at certain angle parking stalls?
sec08-card-sec08-F08.expected_back: Signs may show that an angle parking area is reverse angle or back-in only.

sec08-card-sec08-F09.front: What brake and transmission settings must you apply every time you park on a hill?
sec08-card-sec08-F09.expected_back: When parking on a hill, always set the parking brake, and leave a manual transmission in gear or an automatic transmission in park.

sec08-card-sec08-R05.front: When parking on a slope, what step stays identical and what step changes between manual and automatic cars?
sec08-card-sec08-R05.expected_back: On a hill the parking brake is always set, and the gear selection differs only by transmission: in gear for a manual, in park for an automatic.

sec08-card-sec08-F10.front: What safety purpose does turning your front wheels serve when parking on a hill?
sec08-card-sec08-F10.expected_back: On a hill, turn your front wheels so the vehicle would not roll downhill into traffic if the brake failed.

sec08-card-sec08-F11.front: Which way must you turn your front wheels when parked facing downhill beside a curb?
sec08-card-sec08-F11.expected_back: Parked downhill next to a curb, turn your front wheels toward the curb.

sec08-card-sec08-F12.front: Which way must you turn your front wheels when parked facing uphill beside a curb?
sec08-card-sec08-F12.expected_back: Parked uphill next to a curb, turn your front wheels toward the travel lane.

sec08-card-sec08-F13.front: Which way do your front wheels point when parking on a hill that has no curb?
sec08-card-sec08-F13.expected_back: Parked on a hill with no curb, turn your front wheels toward the edge of the road.

sec08-card-sec08-R03.front: At a curbed street, why do downhill and uphill wheel angles point in opposite directions?
