sec03-card-sec03-F39.question_text: What does red pavement paint reserve, and why can you not rely on red paint alone to spot transit lanes?
sec03-card-sec03-F39.teaching_text: Many bus or light-rail lanes use standard pavement with white regulatory signs and stencil legends rather than red coating.

sec03-card-sec03-F40.question_text: What legends may appear on a solid red transit lane, and what do striped red lines allow cars to do?
sec03-card-sec03-F40.teaching_text: Waiting until the red paint breaks into stripes keeps passenger cars out of bus and light-rail lanes until the turn zone.
sec03-card-sec03-F40.must_match_memory_hook: Solid blocks cars, stripes allow turns

visual_sync.text_span: Solid blocks cars, stripes allow turns

sec03-card-sec03-R11.question_text: How does permission to cross compare across wide solid, broken or dotted, and double solid white lines?
sec03-card-sec03-R11.teaching_text: Ranking white stripes from cautious freedom to discouraged to strictly illegal locks in three high-frequency exam items at once.

sec03-card-sec03-R12.question_text: How does a dotted white line before a freeway exit differ from a dotted white line at an on-ramp?
sec03-card-sec03-R12.teaching_text: Spotting exit dots early stops accidental off-ramp detours, while on-ramp dots signal your acceleration lane is about to end.

sec03-card-sec03-R14.question_text: How does a solid red lane differ from striped red markings for someone driving a passenger car?
sec03-card-sec03-R14.teaching_text: Entering on solid red before the striped transition earns a transit-lane violation even if you plan to turn ahead.
sec03-card-sec03-R14.must_match_memory_hook: Solid stays closed, stripes open turns

visual_sync.text_span: Solid stays closed, stripes open turns

sec03-card-sec03-F41.question_text: What sides make up your space cushion, and how does driving faster change hazard time and stopping distance?
sec03-card-sec03-F41.teaching_text: Higher speed burns through open pavement before your foot even reaches the brake pedal and stretches braking distance.

sec03-card-sec03-F42.question_text: What is a safe following gap in seconds, and what does Oregon recommend above thirty miles per hour?
sec03-card-sec03-F42.teaching_text: Once speeds pass thirty miles per hour, two seconds leaves too little pavement to stop if traffic ahead locks up.
sec03-card-sec03-F42.must_match_memory_hook: Two to four, four plus faster

visual_sync.text_span: Two to four, four plus faster

sec03-card-sec03-F43.question_text: How do you measure your following distance in seconds, and what if your count finishes under two seconds?
sec03-card-sec03-F43.teaching_text: Using shadows, signs, or overpass posts adjusts automatically to your speed, unlike guessing car lengths.

sec03-card-sec03-F44.question_text: What visual check tells you that you stopped far enough behind the vehicle ahead?
sec03-card-sec03-F44.teaching_text: Leaving tire-to-pavement room keeps you from getting pushed into the car ahead if rear-ended and lets you steer around stalls.

sec03-card-sec03-F45.question_text: Which weather, visibility, vehicle, and passing conditions call for extra following distance?
sec03-card-sec03-F45.teaching_text: Wet tires skid farther, heavy rigs stop slower, motorcycles stop quicker, and tight gaps trap passing cars.
sec03-card-sec03-F45.must_match_memory_hook: Add seconds for rain, size, loads

visual_sync.text_span: Add seconds for rain, size, loads

sec03-card-sec03-F46.question_text: What three additional situations involving hills, driver experience, and road crews call for extra following room?
sec03-card-sec03-F46.teaching_text: Manual-shift or heavy vehicles can roll backward on steep grades, and work zones bring sudden flagger stops.

sec03-card-sec03-F53.question_text: Which four factors shape stopping distance, and how does speed affect it even on dry clear days?
sec03-card-sec03-F53.teaching_text: Even brand-new brakes on dry asphalt cannot beat physics when extra speed multiplies braking distance.

sec03-card-sec03-F54.question_text: Traveling sixty miles per hour, how does total hazard-to-stop distance compare against a football field?
sec03-card-sec03-F54.teaching_text: Over three hundred feet vanishes between seeing brake lights, moving your foot, and scrubbing off highway speed.

sec03-card-sec03-R15.question_text: How does Oregon's general following-distance range shift once your speed climbs above thirty miles per hour?
sec03-card-sec03-R15.teaching_text: Test questions pinpoint thirty miles per hour as the exact threshold where four seconds becomes the minimum safe cushion.

sec03-card-sec03-R16.question_text: Why and how do you increase your following gap when a driver behind you wants to pass?
sec03-card-sec03-R16.teaching_text: If you tailgate the car ahead, an overtaking driver gets stranded in the oncoming lane with nowhere to tuck back in.

sec03-card-sec03-F47.question_text: How should you position your vehicle on multilane and two-way streets to protect your side space?
sec03-card-sec03-F47.teaching_text: Lingering next to another car erases your escape lane if a pothole, sudden swerve, or oncoming drift happens.

sec03-card-sec03-F48.question_text: How can you help merging freeway traffic or a driver signaling to change lanes?
sec03-card-sec03-F48.teaching_text: A tiny lift off the accelerator or early lane shift prevents risky pinch points at ramp merges.

sec03-card-sec03-F49.question_text: Why should you leave extra room inside your lane when passing a line of parked cars?
sec03-card-sec03-F49.teaching_text: A distracted occupant can fling a car door open or step from between bumpers with zero warning.

sec03-card-sec03-F50.question_text: How do you keep a following driver back, and what is your first move if tailgated on a multi-lane road?
sec03-card-sec03-F50.teaching_text: Flashing brake lights early warns distracted followers before hard braking starts, and moving right clears aggressive drivers safely.
sec03-card-sec03-F50.must_match_memory_hook: Steady speed, tap brakes, move right

visual_sync.text_span: Steady speed, tap brakes, move right

sec03-card-sec03-F51.question_text: If a tailgater stays glued to your bumper and no right lane exists, what should you do and never do?
sec03-card-sec03-F51.teaching_text: Brake-checking a close follower leaves them zero reaction time and puts their front bumper into your trunk.

sec03-card-sec03-F52.question_text: Because mirrors miss blind zones, how should you position your body and scan while backing up?
sec03-card-sec03-F52.teaching_text: Twisting to look directly through the rear window plus side glances catches low obstacles and walking kids that mirrors hide.

sec03-card-sec03-R17.question_text: Which response to a tailgater is recommended, and which response is never acceptable?
sec03-card-sec03-R17.teaching_text: DMV exams contrast calm gradual speed drops that invite a pass against retaliatory hard braking that causes rear-end wrecks.
sec03-card-sec03-R17.must_match_memory_hook: Gradual slowdown yes, hard brake never

visual_sync.text_span: Gradual slowdown yes, hard brake never

sec03-card-sec03-R18.question_text: Why are mirrors alone not enough when backing up, and what must you do instead?
sec03-card-sec03-R18.teaching_text: Relying only on mirrors or cameras during a drive test fails the observation check if you never turn to look back.

sec04-card-sec04-F01.question_text: How far ahead should you scan for trouble spots, and what driving benefit does that give you?
sec04-card-sec04-F01.teaching_text: Looking all the way down your sightline turns sudden panic swerves into calm, early speed or lane adjustments.

sec04-card-sec04-F02.question_text: What areas does proper scanning cover, and what four kinds of roadway clues does it help you catch?
sec04-card-sec04-F02.teaching_text: Tunnel vision down the hood misses pedestrians at curbs, driveway pull-outs, roadside hazards, and route signs.

sec04-card-sec04-F03.question_text: What three visual clues warn that a driver ahead may be about to slow down or stop?
sec04-card-sec04-F03.teaching_text: Easing off the gas as soon as you see a walker ahead or blinking signals prevents hard braking seconds later.

sec04-card-sec04-F04.question_text: When should you slow down for a curve, and what posted clue helps guide your speed?
sec04-card-sec04-F04.teaching_text: Braking hard after your front tires are already loaded inside a sharp corner can break traction and start a skid.

sec04-card-sec04-F05.question_text: Where should your eyes and vehicle stay inside a curve, and what hidden users must you anticipate?
sec04-card-sec04-F05.teaching_text: Blind bends often hide slow farm rigs, cyclists, or walkers just around the apex while oncoming cars drift near center.

sec04-card-sec04-F06.question_text: How should you adjust your speed as your vehicle straightens out leaving a curve?
sec04-card-sec04-F06.teaching_text: Smooth throttle as the steering wheel unwinds keeps weight balanced instead of jerking the tires loose.

sec04-card-sec04-R01.question_text: What is the proper order for slowing down and speeding up when driving through a curve?
sec04-card-sec04-R01.teaching_text: Reversing that sequence by charging in fast and braking mid-corner is one of the top rural run-off-road crash causes.

sec04-card-sec04-F07.question_text: What is a vehicle blind spot, and how should you drive around other vehicles' blind spots?
sec04-card-sec04-F07.teaching_text: Hovering off another driver's rear quarter panel leaves you invisible right where they might merge.

sec04-card-sec04-F08.question_text: What three steps must you complete before moving into an adjacent lane?
sec04-card-sec04-F08.teaching_text: Skipping the quick shoulder look toward your target lane is an automatic deduction on drive tests and causes sideswipes.

sec04-card-sec04-R02.question_text: Why are mirrors alone insufficient before changing lanes, and which shoulder must you check?
sec04-card-sec04-R02.teaching_text: Glancing over the shoulder on the side you plan to enter directly clears the pocket that glass cannot cover.
sec04-card-sec04-R02.must_match_memory_hook: Mirrors miss blind spots, check target

visual_sync.text_span: Mirrors miss blind spots, check target

sec04-card-sec04-F09.question_text: Before overtaking on a two-lane road, why must you avoid tailgating, especially behind trucks, and what must you know about your car?
sec04-card-sec04-F09.teaching_text: Hugging a tall trailer blocks your view of oncoming traffic and robs your space to build passing momentum.

sec04-card-sec04-F10.question_text: What crash risk comes from cutting back too early versus returning too late after passing, and what if you have doubts?
sec04-card-sec04-F10.teaching_text: Even a couple seconds of misjudged gap can trap you between clipping a fender on the right and meeting headlights ahead.

sec04-card-sec04-R03.question_text: How does the collision hazard of cutting in too soon after a pass differ from staying out too long?
sec04-card-sec04-R03.teaching_text: Exam questions contrast those two timing errors to reinforce why waiting for a long, unmistakable gap matters.
sec04-card-sec04-R03.must_match_memory_hook: Early clips side, late hits oncoming

visual_sync.text_span: Early clips side, late hits oncoming

sec04-card-sec04-F11.question_text: On a two-lane road, which side do you pass on, and where must your pass start and finish?
sec04-card-sec04-F11.teaching_text: Pulling out early before the dashed stripe begins or drifting past the solid stripe puts you in a blind zone.

sec04-card-sec04-R04.question_text: How do passing-zone and no-passing-zone markings restrict both the start and the end of a pass?
sec04-card-sec04-R04.teaching_text: Drivers often think starting inside a legal zone excuses finishing across solid yellow, which is flatly illegal.

sec04-card-sec04-F12.question_text: Are you allowed to exceed the posted speed limit briefly to pass a slower vehicle?
sec04-card-sec04-F12.teaching_text: One of the biggest permit-test myths is a temporary passing speed cushion, when Oregon law caps your speed at all times.

sec04-card-sec04-F13.question_text: Walk through the steps of a safe pass from checking ahead to pulling back into your lane?
sec04-card-sec04-F13.teaching_text: Waiting until the overtaken vehicle appears in your inside rearview mirror guarantees safe bumper clearance before moving right.

sec04-card-sec04-R05.question_text: What mirror visual confirms you have enough room to signal and return to the right lane after passing?
sec04-card-sec04-R05.teaching_text: Relying only on your right side mirror misjudges nose clearance and risks clipping the front corner of the passed car.

sec04-card-sec04-F14.question_text: What roadway guides tell you where passing is allowed, and what visibility rule overrides everything?
sec04-card-sec04-F14.teaching_text: Fog, rain spray, glare, or dips can erase sight distance even where dashed center paint would normally allow passing.

sec04-card-sec04-F15.question_text: What two passing actions are illegal in or approaching a no-passing zone?
sec04-card-sec04-F15.teaching_text: Starting a late pass near the end of dashed yellow leaves you facing oncoming traffic right where sightlines vanish.
sec04-card-sec04-F15.must_match_memory_hook: Never cross inside or run over

visual_sync.text_span: Never cross inside or run over

sec04-card-sec04-F16.question_text: When do hills or curves make passing illegal?
sec04-card-sec04-F16.teaching_text: An approaching car hidden behind a crest or bend closes the gap at combined highway speeds with nowhere to escape.

sec04-card-sec04-F17.question_text: At or approaching which two types of crossings is passing strictly forbidden?
sec04-card-sec04-F17.teaching_text: Vehicles turning from cross streets or stopping for trains create sudden conflicts where an overtaking car is invisible.

sec04-card-sec04-F18.question_text: What is the rule if a vehicle ahead stops at a crosswalk for a pedestrian?
sec04-card-sec04-F18.teaching_text: The stopped vehicle hides the walking pedestrian from your view until you swing around directly into their path.

sec04-card-sec04-R07.question_text: Which three crossing situations all share a strict ban on passing?
sec04-card-sec04-R07.teaching_text: Grouping crosswalk stops with intersections and railroad tracks locks in all three conflict-point passing bans together.

sec04-card-sec04-F19.question_text: What two situations allow crossing the center line inside a no-passing zone?
sec04-card-sec04-F19.teaching_text: No-passing paint forbids overtaking moving traffic, not steering carefully around a stalled car or turning into a driveway.

sec04-card-sec04-R06.question_text: Inside a no-passing zone, which center-line crossings remain legal and which crossing is never legal?
sec04-card-sec04-R06.teaching_text: Permit questions test whether you know solid yellow still lets you turn left or clear an obstruction safely.
sec04-card-sec04-R06.must_match_memory_hook: Left turns or blocks, never passing

visual_sync.text_span: Left turns or blocks, never passing

sec04-card-sec04-F20.question_text: Under what conditions may you pass on the right of a vehicle that is turning or signaling left?
sec04-card-sec04-F20.teaching_text: Dipping onto a gravel shoulder or into a bicycle lane to squeeze around a left turner is unlawful and dangerous.
sec04-card-sec04-F20.must_match_memory_hook: Clear pavement only, skip bike lane

visual_sync.text_span: Clear pavement only, skip bike lane

sec04-card-sec04-F21.question_text: When may you pass on the right on a roadway with two or more lanes moving in your direction?
sec04-card-sec04-F21.teaching_text: Open same-direction right lanes allow passing slower left-lane traffic legally as long as you stay within the speed limit.

sec04-card-sec04-R08.question_text: How do Oregon's two legal situations for passing on the right differ?
sec04-card-sec04-R08.teaching_text: Knowing both right-pass rules prevents shoulder or bike-lane violations on single-lane streets while clarifying multi-lane flow.

sec04-card-sec04-F22.question_text: Why does passing on the right demand extra caution, and what speed rule still applies?
sec04-card-sec04-F22.teaching_text: Passenger-side blind spots are wider and drivers expect overtakes on their left, so sudden right drifts catch people off guard.

sec04-card-sec04-F23.question_text: What three things should you do when another driver is passing your vehicle?
sec04-card-sec04-F23.teaching_text: Speeding up to block an overtaking car traps both of you in a high-speed head-on emergency if oncoming traffic appears.

sec04-card-sec04-F24.question_text: Why must you never wave or flash vehicle lights to tell a following driver when to pass?
sec04-card-sec04-F24.teaching_text: Oregon law flatly forbids flashing signals as a pass cue, and misjudging oncoming traffic makes a friendly wave deadly.

sec04-card-sec04-R09.question_text: When being passed, how may you cooperate legally, and what signal action is forbidden?
sec04-card-sec04-R09.teaching_text: Each driver must judge passing sightlines independently, so you assist with lane position and speed rather than hand or light cues.

sec04-card-sec04-F25.question_text: Which design features allow traffic on multi-lane freeways to move faster and smoother?
sec04-card-sec04-F25.teaching_text: Eliminating cross streets, stoplights, train tracks, and tight bends removes the stop-and-go conflict points of surface roads.
sec04-card-sec04-F25.must_match_memory_hook: Controlled access, zero lights or rails

visual_sync.text_span: Controlled access, zero lights or rails

sec04-card-sec04-F26.question_text: Why is holding a steady freeway speed smarter than weaving from lane to lane?
sec04-card-sec04-F26.teaching_text: Aggressive lane-hopping multiplies blind-spot conflicts at highway speed while shaving almost zero minutes off arrival.
sec04-card-sec04-F26.must_match_memory_hook: Steady cuts risk, weaving wastes effort

visual_sync.text_span: Steady cuts risk, weaving wastes effort

sec04-card-sec04-F27.question_text: How should you balance freeway traffic flow with the speed limit, and which lane belongs to slower vehicles?
sec04-card-sec04-F27.teaching_text: Everyone speeding around you never legalizes breaking the posted limit, and camping slowly in left lanes triggers road rage and right-passes.
sec04-card-sec04-F27.must_match_memory_hook: Keep pace under limit, slow right

visual_sync.text_span: Keep pace under limit, slow right

sec04-card-sec04-R12.question_text: Does keeping pace with fast freeway traffic ever make driving over the posted speed limit legal?
sec04-card-sec04-R12.teaching_text: Going with the flow is a classic ticket excuse that fails in court and on the Oregon knowledge exam.

sec04-card-sec04-F28.question_text: How should mainline freeway drivers respond when vehicles are entering from an on-ramp?
sec04-card-sec04-F28.teaching_text: Spotting ramp cars early lets you open a clean merge pocket instead of boxing them onto the shoulder.

sec04-card-sec04-F29.question_text: How do you warn drivers behind you when you spot freeway traffic slowing up ahead?
sec04-card-sec04-F29.teaching_text: Flashing your brake lights early wakes up following drivers before high-speed traffic compresses into a chain-reaction crash.
sec04-card-sec04-F29.must_match_memory_hook: Tap brake pedal lightly several times

visual_sync.text_span: Tap brake pedal lightly several times

sec04-card-sec04-R11.question_text: What specific brake-pedal technique signals a freeway slowdown to trailing drivers?
sec04-card-sec04-R11.teaching_text: Waiting until the last second for one hard brake press leaves fast highway followers far less reaction distance.

sec04-card-sec04-F30.question_text: How does entering a freeway on an on-ramp differ from pulling onto most busy surface streets?
sec04-card-sec04-F30.teaching_text: Crawling onto a freeway at city speed forces sixty-mile-per-hour traffic to slam brakes or swerve around you.

sec04-card-sec04-R10.question_text: Instead of slowing or stopping like at surface intersections, what do you do on a freeway on-ramp?
sec04-card-sec04-R10.teaching_text: Hesitating or stopping needlessly near the end of an acceleration lane leaves zero runway to reach freeway pace.

sec04-card-sec04-F31.question_text: Who yields during a freeway merge, what checks must you make, and why must you keep moving?
sec04-card-sec04-F31.teaching_text: Drivers behind you on the ramp are looking over their left shoulders to merge and will rear-end you if you stop unexpectedly.
sec04-card-sec04-F31.must_match_memory_hook: Yield, check, match speed, keep moving

visual_sync.text_span: Yield, check, match speed, keep moving

sec04-card-sec04-F32.question_text: What immediate steps must you take if DO NOT ENTER or WRONG WAY signs tell you that you entered a ramp backward?
sec04-card-sec04-F32.teaching_text: Stopping immediately on the ramp edge with flashers keeps a wrong-way mistake off the high-speed mainline.

sec04-card-sec04-F33.question_text: How do ramp meters operate on single-lane and multi-lane freeway entrances when switched on?
sec04-card-sec04-F33.teaching_text: Spacing incoming cars one per green cycle breaks up platoons so mainline freeway traffic never jams at the merge.

sec04-card-sec04-F34.question_text: What should you do when you approach a freeway ramp meter that is completely dark?
sec04-card-sec04-F34.teaching_text: Unlike a blacked-out intersection traffic light, a dark ramp meter simply means metering is turned off for current traffic.

sec04-card-sec04-R13.question_text: How does your action at a green ramp meter compare with a dark ramp meter?
sec04-card-sec04-R13.teaching_text: Stopping at an inactive dark ramp meter surprises trailing drivers who know off-peak ramps run free-flow.
sec04-card-sec04-R13.must_match_memory_hook: Green releases one, dark skips stop

visual_sync.text_span: Green releases one, dark skips stop

sec04-card-sec04-F35.question_text: When leaving a freeway, when do you signal and where do you begin slowing down?
sec04-card-sec04-F35.teaching_text: Braking early in high-speed travel lanes catches behind traffic off guard before you reach the deceleration ramp.

sec04-card-sec04-R14.question_text: Why must you hold speed until leaving freeway travel lanes rather than braking before the exit ramp?
sec04-card-sec04-R14.teaching_text: Exit ramps post advisory speeds specifically so you shed speed safely out of the path of through traffic.

sec04-card-sec04-F36.question_text: What must you do if you miss your freeway exit, and why is using the shoulder or reversing banned?
sec04-card-sec04-F36.teaching_text: Stopping or backing on a freeway shoulder to salvage a missed turn triggers catastrophic high-speed collisions.
sec04-card-sec04-F36.must_match_memory_hook: Take next exit, never back up

visual_sync.text_span: Take next exit, never back up

sec04-card-sec04-R15.question_text: After passing your intended freeway exit, which choice is lawful and which two moves are strictly forbidden?
sec04-card-sec04-R15.teaching_text: Numbered exits make looping back at the next interchange simple, whereas reversing on a freeway is deadly and illegal.
sec04-card-sec04-R15.must_match_memory_hook: Continue ahead, never stop or reverse

visual_sync.text_span: Continue ahead, never stop or reverse

sec04-card-sec04-F37.question_text: If your vehicle breaks down on a freeway, where should you pull over, what lights go on, and where should you wait?
sec04-card-sec04-F37.teaching_text: Walking along high-speed freeway lanes exposes pedestrians to deadly drift crashes, so stay inside or away from traffic.
sec04-card-sec04-F37.must_match_memory_hook: Right shoulder, hazards, away from traffic

visual_sync.text_span: Right shoulder, hazards, away from traffic

sec04-card-sec04-F38.question_text: How do large vehicles and towed trailers differ from ordinary cars in size, acceleration, braking, and turning?
sec04-card-sec04-F38.teaching_text: Extra mass and wheelbase demand longer merge gaps, earlier braking, and wider cornering arcs around curbs.
sec04-card-sec04-F38.must_match_memory_hook: Bigger dimensions, slower stops, wide turns

visual_sync.text_span: Bigger dimensions, slower stops, wide turns

sec04-card-sec04-F39.question_text: What lane and turnout habits apply when driving a camper, motor home, or trailer that slows following traffic?
sec04-card-sec04-F39.teaching_text: Watching mirrors and pulling into turnouts clears stacked cars before frustrated drivers gamble on blind mountain passes.
sec04-card-sec04-F39.must_match_memory_hook: Keep right, use first safe turnout

visual_sync.text_span: Keep right, use first safe turnout

sec04-card-sec04-F40.question_text: Is riding inside a towed trailer legal in Oregon, and what three trailer types are exceptions?
sec04-card-sec04-F40.teaching_text: Ordinary utility or boat trailers lack crash protection and emergency exits, making passenger riding unlawful outside those three designs.

sec04-card-sec04-F41.question_text: What three safety features must a fifth-wheel trailer have before passengers may ride inside it?
sec04-card-sec04-F41.teaching_text: Shatter-resistant glass, two-way cab communication, and a latch opening from both sides prevent riders from getting trapped.
sec04-card-sec04-F41.must_match_memory_hook: Safety glazing, driver signal, two-way exit

visual_sync.text_span: Safety glazing, driver signal, two-way exit

sec04-card-sec04-R16.question_text: How does Oregon's passenger rule for an equipped fifth-wheel trailer differ from an ordinary bumper-pull trailer?
sec04-card-sec04-R16.teaching_text: DMV questions test both the general trailer passenger ban and the three-item equipment checklist that unlocks fifth-wheel riders.

sec04-card-sec04-F42.question_text: How many boats, utility trailers, or vehicles may a passenger or recreational vehicle tow at once in Oregon?
sec04-card-sec04-F42.teaching_text: Hitching a boat behind a travel trailer, often called recreational double towing, is illegal for passenger and RV drivers in Oregon.

sec04-card-sec04-R17.question_text: May a passenger car or recreational vehicle add a second towed unit behind its first trailer in Oregon?
sec04-card-sec04-R17.teaching_text: Visitors from states allowing triple-unit RV setups often get cited in Oregon where one towed unit is the hard ceiling.

sec05-card-sec05-F01.question_text: Which four maneuvers require a signal, and which directions must you check first?
sec05-card-sec05-F01.teaching_text: Leaving a curb or exiting a roundabout catches nearby drivers off guard just as fast as a sudden lane shift.

sec05-card-sec05-F02.question_text: How far ahead must your turn signal click on when you are already moving in traffic?
sec05-card-sec05-F02.teaching_text: Flipping the stalk mid-turn gives trailing drivers zero warning to ease off the gas before your brake lights flare.

sec05-card-sec05-F03.question_text: How long should you run your turn signal before pulling out from a curb into traffic?
sec05-card-sec05-F03.teaching_text: A parked car looks stationary until a steady blinker gives oncoming lanes time to read your move.

sec05-card-sec05-R02.question_text: How does signaling while moving in traffic differ from signaling when pulling away from a curb?
sec05-card-sec05-R02.teaching_text: Exam questions contrast rolling lane moves that cover ground against stationary curb starts where feet cannot measure warning time.

sec05-card-sec05-F04.question_text: Under what visibility conditions are hand-and-arm signals legal, and what must you use after dark?
sec05-card-sec05-F04.teaching_text: An extended arm vanishes in dusk, rain, or fog long before trailing headlights reach stopping range.

sec05-card-sec05-F05.question_text: In what kind of vehicle must you avoid using hand-and-arm signals?
sec05-card-sec05-F05.teaching_text: Extended bodywork or cargo boxes block drivers behind you from spotting a hand out the cab window.

sec05-card-sec05-F06.question_text: Which three driver actions have official hand-and-arm signals in the Oregon manual?
sec05-card-sec05-F06.teaching_text: Knowing all three arm positions helps you read cyclists and vintage cars as well as pass sign-recognition questions.

sec05-card-sec05-R01.question_text: How does the legal window for electric signal lights compare with hand-and-arm signals?
sec05-card-sec05-R01.teaching_text: Test writers pair foggy daytime roads with nighttime driving because both conditions ban arm gestures completely.

sec05-card-sec05-F07.question_text: Why is trusting another vehicle's flashing turn signal by itself a dangerous mistake?
sec05-card-sec05-F07.teaching_text: Drivers forget cancelled stalks or change their minds mid-block, turning a premature pull-out into a T-bone collision.

sec05-card-sec05-F08.question_text: Do Oregon's turning rules stop at street intersections, or where else do they apply?
sec05-card-sec05-F08.teaching_text: Sidewalk crossings at shopping plazas and narrow back alleys carry the exact same legal duties as major cross streets.

sec05-card-sec05-F09.question_text: When should you scan behind and beside your car for a turn, and how should you steer through it?
sec05-card-sec05-F09.teaching_text: Braking hard mid-corner upsets tire grip while early mirror checks let you slow down predictably beforehand.

sec05-card-sec05-F22.question_text: Which lane do you start a turn from, which lane do you finish in, and what two habits must you avoid?
sec05-card-sec05-F22.teaching_text: Drifting outward mid-arc clips parallel turners or sideswipes oncoming cars waiting at the cross street.

sec05-card-sec05-F23.question_text: Which two specific lane mistakes does the manual illustrate as improper turns?
sec05-card-sec05-F23.teaching_text: Cutting across from an interior lane or drifting wide on exit causes most multi-lane corner collisions.

sec05-card-sec05-F10.question_text: How must you handle a painted bicycle lane when preparing for and making a turn?
sec05-card-sec05-F10.teaching_text: Oregon forbids using bike lanes as right-turn queues, keeping cyclists safe from cars drifting into their space early.

sec05-card-sec05-R03.question_text: Which action in a bike lane is legal during a turn, and which pre-turn move is illegal?
sec05-card-sec05-R03.teaching_text: Drivers trained in other states often fail this Oregon test question because pre-turn merging into bike stripes is outlawed here.

sec05-card-sec05-F11.question_text: Why must you check both mirrors and glance over your shoulder before turning?
sec05-card-sec05-F11.teaching_text: Fast cyclists rolling alongside your rear fender stay invisible in side glass until a quick head turn spots them.

sec05-card-sec05-F12.question_text: Which cyclists and pedestrians take priority over your turning vehicle?
sec05-card-sec05-F12.teaching_text: Turning across someone rolling along a sidewalk or stepping off a curb puts steel directly across an unprotected path.

sec05-card-sec05-F13.question_text: What is the right move when you reach an intersection in the wrong lane for your intended turn?
sec05-card-sec05-F13.teaching_text: Diving across lanes at the stop bar causes panic braking and broadside hits over a two-minute detour.

sec05-card-sec05-F14.question_text: Where do you position your car for a right turn, and what four-step visual scan comes right before entering?
sec05-card-sec05-F14.teaching_text: Traffic from your left crosses your bumper first, making that final leftward glance your best shield against red-light runners.

sec05-card-sec05-F15.question_text: Which lane do you use to turn left from a two-way street, and who gets the right of way?
sec05-card-sec05-F15.teaching_text: Misjudging an oncoming car's closing speed across opposing lanes creates the most severe head-on angle crashes.

sec05-card-sec05-R04.question_text: How does your starting position on a two-way street change between a right turn and a left turn?
sec05-card-sec05-R04.teaching_text: Starting from the proper edge keeps trailing traffic flowing smoothly without guessing which way your wheels will cut.

sec05-card-sec05-R05.question_text: What exact four-part head check applies right before both right turns and left turns?
sec05-card-sec05-R05.teaching_text: Keeping one consistent four-beat rhythm builds muscle memory whether you are hugging a curb or waiting by yellow paint.

sec05-card-sec05-F16.question_text: Relative to the center point and the new street's center line, where do you turn and finish a left turn?
sec05-card-sec05-F16.teaching_text: Cutting the corner too early clips the opposing left-turn lane, while swinging past center tangles with oncoming turners.

sec05-card-sec05-F17.question_text: Is turning left on red onto a two-way road ever legal, and what rule governs dedicated left-turn lanes?
sec05-card-sec05-F17.teaching_text: Turning left onto a two-way street against red crosses two live opposing streams, and skipping a turn bay sideswipes properly queued cars.

sec05-card-sec05-F21.question_text: When can two or more lanes turn the same direction together, and how must drivers steer through?
sec05-card-sec05-F21.teaching_text: Drifting across dashed guide lines mid-turn puts your quarter panel straight into the car turning beside you.

sec05-card-sec05-F18.question_text: Which lanes do you use to turn left from one one-way street onto another, and what is the red-light rule?
sec05-card-sec05-F18.teaching_text: Because neither street carries opposing traffic, hugging the left curb crosses zero oncoming lanes after a full stop.

sec05-card-sec05-F19.question_text: How do you position and handle a red light when turning from a two-way street onto a one-way street?
sec05-card-sec05-F19.teaching_text: Oregon uniquely permits left-on-red from a two-way street onto a one-way street once you stop and yield completely.

sec05-card-sec05-F20.question_text: Going left off a one-way street onto a two-way street, which lanes apply and is red legal?
sec05-card-sec05-F20.teaching_text: Entering a two-way cross street on red forces you across cross-traffic lanes from both directions without signal protection.

sec05-card-sec05-R06.question_text: Leaving a one-way street to turn left, what determines whether you can go on a red light?
sec05-card-sec05-R06.teaching_text: On the Oregon exam, look at the street you are entering rather than the street you are leaving.

sec05-card-sec05-R07.question_text: Why does turning from a two-way street onto a one-way street have the opposite red-light rule from turning left onto a two-way street?
sec05-card-sec05-R07.teaching_text: Many applicants miss Oregon's two-way-to-one-way left on red because most other states outlaw that move.

sec05-card-sec05-R08.question_text: When turning left off a one-way street, what stays identical and what changes based on the cross street?
sec05-card-sec05-R08.teaching_text: Every one-way left starts against the left curb so nobody can undercut your inside fender.

sec05-card-sec05-F24.question_text: When is a U-turn legal at an intersection controlled by a traffic light in Oregon?
sec05-card-sec05-F24.teaching_text: Unlike states where green arrows imply U-turns, Oregon flips the default and requires an explicit permissive sign at traffic lights.

sec05-card-sec05-F25.question_text: Are U-turns allowed between intersections on city streets?
sec05-card-sec05-F25.teaching_text: Swinging across urban lanes mid-block surprises parked cars pulling out and drivers exiting driveways.

sec05-card-sec05-R10.question_text: Which urban U-turn ban can be lifted by a posted sign, and which one has no sign exception?
sec05-card-sec05-R10.teaching_text: Test questions pit signalized corners against mid-block stretches to see if you know where permissive signs exist.

sec05-card-sec05-F26.question_text: Inside city limits, how far away must approaching drivers from both directions be able to see your car for a U-turn?
sec05-card-sec05-F26.teaching_text: Crests, curves, and leafy corners hide a slow three-point swing until urban traffic is right on your doors.

sec05-card-sec05-F27.question_text: Outside city limits, what clear sight distance in both directions is required to make a U-turn?
sec05-card-sec05-F27.teaching_text: Highway speeds eat up pavement twice as fast, demanding double the clear sightline before turning broadside across lanes.

sec05-card-sec05-R09.question_text: How does the required sight distance for a U-turn change once you drive past city limits?
sec05-card-sec05-R09.teaching_text: Higher rural closing speeds double the distance oncoming traffic needs to spot a car swinging across the road.

sec05-card-sec05-F28.question_text: Which two other locations strictly outlaw U-turns regardless of sight distance?
sec05-card-sec05-F28.teaching_text: Stalling mid-turn across steel rails or ignoring local no-turn postings puts your cabin directly in high-speed conflict zones.

sec05-card-sec05-F29.question_text: What dangerous assumption does a defensive driver refuse to make about stop signs and red lights?
sec05-card-sec05-F29.teaching_text: Paint and red bulbs cannot apply brakes for a distracted driver, so verifying cross traffic saves your fenders.

sec05-card-sec05-F30.question_text: Where must your front bumper stop at a stop sign, steady red light, or flashing red signal?
sec05-card-sec05-F30.teaching_text: Rolling onto marked or unmarked crossing paths forces walkers out into live cross traffic.

sec05-card-sec05-F31.question_text: Even when your signal or sign allows a turn, which two groups still hold priority over you?
sec05-card-sec05-F31.teaching_text: A green ball or legal turn-on-red grants permission to move only after walkers, cyclists, and clearing cars pass safely.

sec05-card-sec05-F32.question_text: What should you do after stopping properly if hedges, buildings, or parked cars still block your side view?
sec05-card-sec05-F32.teaching_text: Completing your legal stop first keeps crosswalks safe before you inch forward far enough to peek past obstructions.

sec05-card-sec05-F33.question_text: What space check must pass before you roll into an intersection on a green light?
sec05-card-sec05-F33.teaching_text: Getting trapped mid-box when traffic stalls ahead locks cross streets solid the instant the signal cycles.

sec05-card-sec05-R13.question_text: Why does a green signal alone fail to guarantee you should enter an intersection?
sec05-card-sec05-R13.teaching_text: Exam questions trap drivers who equate green bulbs with an automatic clear path when bumper-to-bumper queues block the exit.

sec05-card-sec05-F34.question_text: How do drivers decide order at a four-way stop, and what breaks a tie when arrival order is unclear?
sec05-card-sec05-F34.teaching_text: Eye contact and yielding to your right prevent two bumpers from lunging into the middle together.

sec05-card-sec05-F35.question_text: When two opposite approaches have stop signs and cross traffic does not, who yields between straight and left-turning cars?
sec05-card-sec05-F35.teaching_text: Cutting across an oncoming driver's straight path invites a collision even if you touched your stop bar slightly earlier.

sec05-card-sec05-R11.question_text: How does priority shift between a four-way stop and an intersection where only facing approaches have stop signs?
sec05-card-sec05-R11.teaching_text: Applying four-way first-in rules at a two-way stop causes left turners to pull straight across oncoming traffic.

sec05-card-sec05-F36.question_text: At an intersection with zero signs or signals, which way do you look first and who gets the right of way?
sec05-card-sec05-F36.teaching_text: Cross traffic from the left reaches your driver's door first, while vehicles from the right hold legal priority.

sec05-card-sec05-F37.question_text: Who holds the right of way when your street ends at an uncontrolled T-intersection?
sec05-card-sec05-F37.teaching_text: Drivers cruising along the continuous top bar expect uninterrupted flow while your terminating street forces a turn.

sec05-card-sec05-R12.question_text: How does the uncontrolled right-of-way rule change when one road ends at a T instead of crossing straight through?
sec05-card-sec05-R12.teaching_text: Do not expect a through-street driver on your left to yield at an unsigned T-intersection.

sec05-card-sec05-F38.question_text: What defines roundabouts, rotaries, and traffic circles, and which direction does traffic travel around the island?
sec05-card-sec05-F38.teaching_text: Every entry curves right so circulating vehicles always approach from your left around the raised center.

sec05-card-sec05-F39.question_text: What does a yellow warning sign displaying arrows arranged in a circle mean?
sec05-card-sec05-F39.teaching_text: Spotting the advance symbol lets you ease off the throttle and scan lane signs before reaching the yield line.

sec05-card-sec05-F40.question_text: Which four actions prepare you safely as you roll toward a roundabout entry?
sec05-card-sec05-F40.teaching_text: Cyclists choosing between the travel lane and sidewalk ramp share the entry zone with pedestrians on the splitter crosswalk.

sec05-card-sec05-F41.question_text: Who must you yield to when entering a roundabout, and how should you merge in?
sec05-card-sec05-F41.teaching_text: Jumping in ahead of circulating or exiting cars cuts across curved lanes where drivers have little room to swerve.

sec05-card-sec05-F42.question_text: How must you drive behind a bicyclist who has merged into the roundabout lane?
sec05-card-sec05-F42.teaching_text: Tight curved aprons leave zero side clearance, so squeezing past a rider inside the ring risks clipping handlebars.

sec05-card-sec05-R15.question_text: What two path choices do bicyclists have at a roundabout, and what protection applies if they join traffic?
sec05-card-sec05-R15.teaching_text: Expect riders either rolling onto pedestrian crossings or claiming the center of the curved lane ahead of your hood.

sec05-card-sec05-F43.question_text: Which signal and hazard check are required every time you exit a roundabout?
sec05-card-sec05-F43.teaching_text: Your right blinker tells waiting drivers at the next entry they can merge while alerting walkers at the splitter island.

sec05-card-sec05-R14.question_text: How do your responsibilities at a roundabout entry compare with your responsibilities at the exit?
sec05-card-sec05-R14.teaching_text: Skipping the yield causes entry collisions, while skipping the right blinker stalls waiting traffic and surprises crossing pedestrians.

sec05-card-sec05-F44.question_text: When do you select your lane for a multi-lane roundabout, and what must you avoid once inside?
sec05-card-sec05-F44.teaching_text: Spiraling lane lines guide each ring to specific exits, so weaving mid-circle cuts straight across adjacent cars.

sec05-card-sec05-R17.question_text: Why is changing lanes inside a multi-lane roundabout the wrong way to reach your exit?
sec05-card-sec05-R17.teaching_text: Short curved sightlines hide cars tucked beside your rear quarter panel, making pre-entry sign reading essential.

sec05-card-sec05-F45.question_text: What lane space can large trucks use in a roundabout, and what is illegal around them?
sec05-card-sec05-F45.teaching_text: Long trailers track tightly toward the center apron and sweep across both rings, crushing any car squeezing alongside.

sec05-card-sec05-F46.question_text: What must you do if an emergency vehicle approaches before you have entered a roundabout?
sec05-card-sec05-F46.teaching_text: Keeping the narrow curved apron empty lets circulating cars clear out quickly so fire trucks never get boxed in.

sec05-card-sec05-F47.question_text: What is the rule if sirens approach while you are already driving inside a roundabout?
sec05-card-sec05-F47.teaching_text: Stopping against the curved island corks the narrow ring and blocks a wide fire engine from getting past you.

sec05-card-sec05-R16.question_text: How does yielding to an emergency vehicle change once your car is already inside a roundabout?
sec05-card-sec05-R16.teaching_text: Both rules serve one goal by keeping the tight circular roadway completely clear of parked metal.

sec06-card-sec06-F01.question_text: Which people on public ways, crosswalks, or highway shoulders count as vulnerable road users in Oregon?
sec06-card-sec06-F01.teaching_text: Oregon law groups everyone outside a protective steel cabin under stronger legal safeguards whenever crashes occur.

sec06-card-sec06-F02.question_text: What two real-world factors make vulnerable road users especially at risk around cars?
sec06-card-sec06-F02.teaching_text: Narrow profiles disappear behind windshield pillars and even a low-speed bumper tap transfers full impact straight to a human body.

sec06-card-sec06-F03.question_text: Beyond people on foot, who else counts as a pedestrian under the Oregon manual?
sec06-card-sec06-F03.teaching_text: Treat someone rolling across an intersection on a skateboard, scooter, or wheelchair with every legal crosswalk protection.

sec06-card-sec06-F04.question_text: Does a crosswalk need painted stripes before you are required to stop for a pedestrian?
sec06-card-sec06-F04.teaching_text: Missing paint never erases a walker's right of way at residential corners where stripes were never laid down.

sec06-card-sec06-F05.question_text: What exact movement triggers a pedestrian's legal crossing right of way in Oregon?
sec06-card-sec06-F05.teaching_text: Once a cane tip, front wheel, or shoe extends past the curb, Oregon law says the crossing is already underway.

sec06-card-sec06-F06.question_text: When a pedestrian is in a crosswalk, which specific lanes require you to stop and remain stopped?
sec06-card-sec06-F06.teaching_text: Counting an adjacent bike stripe as a neighboring lane keeps drivers from brushing past walkers just steps away.

sec06-card-sec06-F09.question_text: Why is passing another car stopped at a crosswalk illegal?
sec06-card-sec06-F09.teaching_text: The halted SUV beside you blocks your sightline right as a pedestrian steps past its front fender into your lane.

sec06-card-sec06-F10.question_text: Do you have to stop for a pedestrian crossing on the far side of a raised safety island?
sec06-card-sec06-F10.teaching_text: A physical refuge island divides wide boulevards into separate crossings until the walker reaches your side.

sec06-card-sec06-R21.question_text: How does your duty to stop compare between a pedestrian in the adjacent lane and one beyond a safety island?
sec06-card-sec06-R21.teaching_text: Test questions check whether you recognize a raised refuge island as a legal break versus open adjacent pavement.

sec06-card-sec06-F07.question_text: At an intersection with a traffic light, how much clearance past your target lane must a pedestrian have before you turn?
sec06-card-sec06-F07.teaching_text: Rolling slowly toward a walker's heels crowds their stride and leaves zero margin if someone trips.

sec06-card-sec06-F08.question_text: When turning at an intersection with no traffic signal, how far must a pedestrian clear before you start turning?
sec06-card-sec06-F08.teaching_text: Unsigned corners lack walk phases, so Oregon requires a full extra lane of cushion beyond your turn path.

sec06-card-sec06-R20.question_text: How does pedestrian clearance for a turn change when an intersection has no traffic signal?
sec06-card-sec06-R20.teaching_text: Oregon's permit test loves contrasting the measured buffer at traffic lights against the wider lane rule at unsigned corners.

sec06-card-sec06-F11.question_text: Where do unmarked crosswalks exist, and how do you picture their boundaries?
sec06-card-sec06-F11.teaching_text: Extending the sidewalk or shoulder straight across the street reveals legal crossing zones at every neighborhood corner.

sec06-card-sec06-F12.question_text: What is the minimum width of an unmarked crosswalk, and does a street need sidewalks to have one?
sec06-card-sec06-F12.teaching_text: Rural and older suburban intersections without concrete walkways still carry legal crossing corridors at every corner.

sec06-card-sec06-F13.question_text: What does a flashing yellow beacon at a mid-block crosswalk alert drivers to expect?
sec06-card-sec06-F13.teaching_text: Pedestrians activate rapid-flashing beacons between intersections where drivers are cruising without expecting corner stops.

sec06-card-sec06-F14.question_text: Why must your front and rear bumpers stay completely off a crosswalk when stopped?
sec06-card-sec06-F14.teaching_text: Parking across painted bars pushes parents with strollers and wheelchair users out into live moving lanes.

sec06-card-sec06-F15.question_text: Where must you stop and who gets priority when crossing a sidewalk at an alley, driveway, or lot?
sec06-card-sec06-F15.teaching_text: Pulling straight to the curb noses across joggers and cyclists before you ever look down the walkway.

sec06-card-sec06-F17.question_text: What does a yellow five-sided road sign tell you is ahead?
sec06-card-sec06-F17.teaching_text: The roof-shaped pentagon appears exclusively near schools and crossings where unpredictable young walkers gather.

sec06-card-sec06-F18.question_text: What reduced speed limit applies in an Oregon school speed zone, and what marks its start and end?
sec06-card-sec06-F18.teaching_text: Accelerating before passing the end sign or next speed limit post earns steep school-zone citations.

sec06-card-sec06-F19.question_text: What does a flashing yellow light mounted on a school speed sign tell you?
sec06-card-sec06-F19.teaching_text: Active beacons remove all guesswork about bell schedules and demand an immediate drop in speed.

sec06-card-sec06-F20.question_text: Which hours and days trigger a school-hours speed sign, and what if you cannot tell whether school is open?
sec06-card-sec06-F20.teaching_text: Defaulting to the lower pace whenever holiday schedules are unclear protects kids at campus activities and avoids tickets.

sec06-card-sec06-F21.question_text: On which days and hours does a when-children-are-present school speed sign take effect?
sec06-card-sec06-F21.teaching_text: Weekend soccer games or evening school events still trigger this sign whenever students use the crossing.

sec06-card-sec06-F22.question_text: Which three specific crosswalk scenes legally count as children being present in Oregon?
sec06-card-sec06-F22.teaching_text: Kids chatting on a distant playground lawn differ legally from students waiting at the curb or guided by a patrol.

sec06-card-sec06-R22.question_text: How does a school-hours speed sign differ from a children-present speed sign?
sec06-card-sec06-R22.teaching_text: Reading the bottom plaque carefully tells you whether the clock or crosswalk activity controls your speedometer.

sec06-card-sec06-F23.question_text: How long must you remain stopped for a pedestrian with a white cane or guide dog, even if your light turns green?
sec06-card-sec06-F23.teaching_text: Engine noise or horn honks disorient someone navigating by sound, so Oregon requires total curb-to-curb clearance.

sec06-card-sec06-F24.question_text: What two precautions protect children near parks, parked cars, and residential driveways?
sec06-card-sec06-F24.teaching_text: Small children sit below trunk height and dart out from between curbside bumpers with zero warning.

sec06-card-sec06-F25.question_text: When children enter a crosswalk or a school crossing guard signals, when can you move again?
sec06-card-sec06-F25.teaching_text: Rolling forward while the last student is still near the far curb risks hitting a child who drops a backpack.

sec06-card-sec06-F26.question_text: Why are bicyclists easier to overlook than full-size motor vehicles?
sec06-card-sec06-F26.teaching_text: A thin frame slips entirely inside rear-pillar blind zones where only a direct shoulder glance spots it.

sec06-card-sec06-F27.question_text: What street-surface hazards can force a bicyclist to brake or swerve toward your lane?
sec06-card-sec06-F27.teaching_text: Skinny bike tires catch in drain slots, rail grooves, broken glass, or swinging car doors that sedans barely feel.

sec06-card-sec06-F28.question_text: Are driving or parking in a bike lane ever allowed, and when may your tires cross one?
sec06-card-sec06-F28.teaching_text: Keeping motor vehicles out of painted bike corridors except when turning into streets or driveways prevents rear-end strikes.

sec06-card-sec06-F29.question_text: How do right-of-way rules treat bicyclists in bike lanes, on sidewalks, and at intersections?
sec06-card-sec06-F29.teaching_text: Cutting across a rider's straight line at a corner violates the exact same priority law as cutting off a sedan.

sec06-card-sec06-F30.question_text: Above thirty-five miles per hour, how much lateral room must you leave to pass a bicyclist in your lane?
sec06-card-sec06-F30.teaching_text: Oregon measures high-speed passing clearance by asking whether a sudden tip-over would still miss your fenders completely.

sec06-card-sec06-F31.question_text: What should you do when traffic or sightlines prevent you from passing a bicyclist safely?
sec06-card-sec06-F31.teaching_text: Squeezing between an oncoming truck and a cyclist over ten seconds of impatience risks a fatal sideswipe.

sec06-card-sec06-F32.question_text: Which assistive or electric devices legally share bike lanes and paths, and how do you yield to them?
sec06-card-sec06-F32.teaching_text: Expect motorized wheelchairs and scooters rolling along painted bike lanes whenever you turn across a curb cut.

sec06-card-sec06-F33.question_text: What does a green bike box at a signalized intersection look like, and where must cars stop?
sec06-card-sec06-F33.teaching_text: Giving cyclists the front queue space makes riders visible to every windshield before the light turns green.

sec06-card-sec06-F34.question_text: How does a bike box change right-on-red rules and right turns on green?
sec06-card-sec06-F34.teaching_text: Creeping right on red would roll straight over the green waiting zone, and green turns still yield to riders beside you.

sec06-card-sec06-F35.question_text: What road marking pairs two chevrons over a bicycle icon, and what does it mean?
sec06-card-sec06-F35.teaching_text: Where streets are too narrow for dedicated bike lanes, sharrows remind drivers that cyclists legally occupy the travel lane.

sec06-card-sec06-F36.question_text: Why do drivers misread approaching motorcycles and mopeds at intersections?
sec06-card-sec06-F36.teaching_text: A single headlight looks farther away and slower than twin car beams, tempting left turners to pull out too late.

sec06-card-sec06-F37.question_text: How should you handle an oncoming motorcyclist when waiting to turn across traffic?
sec06-card-sec06-F37.teaching_text: Waiting three extra heartbeats eliminates misjudged closing speeds that cause devastating left-turn motorcycle crashes.

sec06-card-sec06-F38.question_text: How should your following distance behind a motorcycle compare with following a passenger car?
sec06-card-sec06-F38.teaching_text: Light two-wheelers shed speed rapidly using engine braking alone before a brake lamp even illuminates.

sec06-card-sec06-F39.question_text: Why must you verify a motorcycle is genuinely slowing before turning across its flashing signal?
sec06-card-sec06-F39.teaching_text: Many handlebars lack self-cancelling switches, so a rider cruising straight may not realize an old turn lamp is still blinking.

sec06-card-sec06-F40.question_text: Is lane sharing alongside a motorcycle or moped legal, and how much space do you give when passing?
sec06-card-sec06-F40.teaching_text: Riders use the entire lane width to dodge potholes and crosswinds, making side-by-side squeezing illegal.

sec06-card-sec06-F41.question_text: What wind and pavement conditions force motorcyclists to adjust speed or lane position suddenly?
sec06-card-sec06-F41.teaching_text: Grooved concrete, metal covers, loose gravel, and crosswinds tug at two tires, so extra trailing space prevents rear-ending.

sec06-card-sec06-R23.question_text: Which two space rules protect motorcyclists when you follow behind them and when you overtake them?
sec06-card-sec06-R23.teaching_text: Extra room fore and aft plus full lateral lane width keeps riders safe from sudden stops and side gusts.

sec06-card-sec06-F42.question_text: How do large trucks, buses, RVs, and towed trailers compare with small cars in acceleration and stopping distance?
sec06-card-sec06-F42.teaching_text: Cutting tightly ahead of a loaded semi steals the massive runway its air brakes need at highway speed.

sec06-card-sec06-F43.question_text: How can you tell whether the driver of a large truck or bus can see your car beside it?
sec06-card-sec06-F43.teaching_text: Hovering alongside trailer wheels where cab glass shows no face leaves you invisible if the rig merges.

sec06-card-sec06-F44.question_text: What two hazards make stopping close behind a large truck or bus dangerous?
sec06-card-sec06-F44.teaching_text: Tucked against trailer doors, you vanish from cab mirrors and sit directly under heavy bumpers if clutch engagement rolls backward.

sec06-card-sec06-R24.question_text: How do you recognize when your car sits inside a large vehicle's rear or side blind spots?
sec06-card-sec06-R24.teaching_text: Staying far enough back or ahead to keep cab mirrors in view prevents accidental squeeze plays.

sec06-card-sec06-F45.question_text: How should you pace a pass beside a large vehicle, and when is it safe to merge back over?
sec06-card-sec06-F45.teaching_text: Waiting until both headlights fill your center mirror leaves essential braking cushion ahead of sixty thousand pounds.

sec06-card-sec06-F46.question_text: How do you maintain visibility around tire spray thrown up by a large vehicle on wet pavement?
sec06-card-sec06-F46.teaching_text: Eighteen spinning tires whip road film onto your windshield faster than wipers clear it if you crowd closely.

sec06-card-sec06-F47.question_text: Why must you keep out of the curbside gap beside a turning bus or big truck?
sec06-card-sec06-F47.teaching_text: Long wheelbases swing left first just to clear rear trailer axles around tight corners, trapping cars that sneak right.

sec06-card-sec06-R01.question_text: What rule applies whenever a large truck is preparing to back up or reversing into a dock?
sec06-card-sec06-R01.teaching_text: Trying to zip behind a reversing trailer puts your car inside a massive blind zone while forty feet swings across lanes.

sec06-card-sec06-R02.question_text: What do smoking wheels or high downhill speed on a large truck warn of, and how should you react?
sec06-card-sec06-R02.teaching_text: Overheated drum brakes lose stopping power fast on Oregon mountain passes, so hanging well back without passing keeps you clear.

sec06-card-sec06-R03.question_text: What is the role of a specially marked pilot vehicle on Oregon highways?
sec06-card-sec06-R03.teaching_text: Spotting an escort car with warning banners tells you a wide house beam or turbine blade is right behind or ahead.

sec06-card-sec06-R04.question_text: How should you adjust position and speed when meeting, following, or passing a pilot vehicle?
sec06-card-sec06-R04.teaching_text: Wide cargo overhangs the centerline on curves, making slow right-edge positioning inside your lane vital.

sec06-card-sec06-R05.question_text: Where are warning lamps mounted on a school bus, and what swings out when red lights flash?
sec06-card-sec06-R05.teaching_text: Roof-high lamps shine over intervening SUVs so trailing drivers spot student stops well down the block.

sec06-card-sec06-R06.question_text: What do flashing amber lights at the top of a school bus warn drivers to prepare for?
sec06-card-sec06-R06.teaching_text: Speeding up to beat amber lamps puts your bumper beside the bus right as red lights lock traffic down.

sec06-card-sec06-R07.question_text: What is your exact legal duty when a school bus switches on flashing red lights?
sec06-card-sec06-R07.teaching_text: Students cross from both curbs unpredictably, so rolling before the overhead reds go dark carries heavy penalties.

sec06-card-sec06-R08.question_text: When does oncoming traffic not have to stop for a school bus flashing red lights?
sec06-card-sec06-R08.teaching_text: Only an unpaved strip or physical wall splits a highway into two separate roadways where kids do not cross.

sec06-card-sec06-R09.question_text: Does a painted median or center turn lane excuse oncoming drivers from stopping for a school bus?
sec06-card-sec06-R09.teaching_text: Oregon's top bus-law exam trap tests five-lane streets with center turn lanes where every single lane must halt.

sec06-card-sec06-R10.question_text: Which other buses may flash amber and red warning lights, and how must you respond?
sec06-card-sec06-R10.teaching_text: Oregon extends identical stop-and-hold protections to farmworker and congregation buses displaying overhead warning flashers.

sec06-card-sec06-R11.question_text: When are drivers behind a public transit bus legally required to yield and let it back into the lane?
sec06-card-sec06-R11.teaching_text: Letting city buses merge smoothly when their rear yield sign flashes keeps whole transit corridors moving on schedule.

sec06-card-sec06-R12.question_text: What colors make up a slow-moving vehicle emblem, and what vehicles display it on highways?
sec06-card-sec06-R12.teaching_text: Closing at highway pace on farm tractors happens shockingly fast, so brake early the instant that triangle appears.

sec06-card-sec06-R13.question_text: At what rear overhang length must cargo carry a red warning flag, and how big must that flag be?
sec06-card-sec06-R13.teaching_text: Unmarked lumber or pipe jutting past a tailgate blends into asphalt until a trailing hood spears straight into it.

sec06-card-sec06-R14.question_text: What replaces the red cloth flag on a long rear load at night or in poor visibility?
sec06-card-sec06-R14.teaching_text: Cloth flags vanish after sunset, so a bright lamp visible from rear and sides keeps trailing cars off protruding cargo.

sec06-card-sec06-R15.question_text: How far may cargo extend beyond the left fenders, right fenders, and front bumper of a passenger car?
sec06-card-sec06-R15.teaching_text: Zero left overhang protects oncoming mirrors while tight right and front caps keep curbside pedestrians safe.

sec06-card-sec06-R16.question_text: How do intersection rules apply to vehicles inside a funeral procession versus outside traffic?
sec06-card-sec06-R16.teaching_text: Keeping the escort line intact prevents split convoys, so cross traffic waits even when green lights cycle.

sec06-card-sec06-R17.question_text: Is an outside driver allowed to join or cut between cars in a funeral procession?
sec06-card-sec06-R17.teaching_text: Weaving between closely spaced procession cars breaks line visibility and breaks Oregon traffic law.

sec06-card-sec06-R18.question_text: On a multi-lane road, what are your two options when approaching any stopped vehicle with flashing lights?
sec06-card-sec06-R18.teaching_text: Oregon protects every flashing roadside vehicle—not just police cruisers—from high-speed mirror strikes.

sec06-card-sec06-R19.question_text: How should you drive near an emergency scene, and when can your tires cross a fire hose?
sec06-card-sec06-R19.teaching_text: Crushing a charged canvas hose cuts water pressure to firefighters inside a burning structure.

sec09-card-sec09-F01.question_text: What two continuous awareness habits form the foundation of safe, responsible driving in Oregon?
sec09-card-sec09-F01.teaching_text: Catching subtle lane drifts or brake lights early stops everyday situations from turning into emergencies.

sec09-card-sec09-F02.question_text: Which six vehicle, road, environment, and personal factors must a defensive driver continually adjust for?
sec09-card-sec09-F02.teaching_text: Even familiar streets turn hazardous when mechanical wear, rain, glare, or your own stress stack together.
sec09-card-sec09-F02.must_match_memory_hook: Car, road, weather, traffic, light, self

visual_sync.text_span: Car, road, weather, traffic, light, self

sec09-card-sec09-F03.question_text: Which directions must remain clear from the driver's seat, and what everyday items can shrink that view?
sec09-card-sec09-F03.teaching_text: Piled cargo, mirror charms, or windshield decals create self-inflicted blind zones large enough to hide pedestrians.

sec09-card-sec09-F04.question_text: Alongside tracking nearby traffic, what backup option does a defensive driver keep ready at all times?
sec09-card-sec09-F04.teaching_text: Pre-spotting an open shoulder or adjacent lane lets you steer clear without panicking when brakes lock ahead.

sec09-card-sec09-F05.question_text: Who must buckle up under Oregon's safety-belt law?
sec09-card-sec09-F05.teaching_text: Backseat adults hold zero exemption in Oregon—unbelted riders become lethal projectiles inside a rolling cabin.

sec09-card-sec09-F06.question_text: How tight should a safety belt sit, and where must the shoulder strap never be tucked?
sec09-card-sec09-F06.teaching_text: Tucking the strap under an arm or behind your back crushes ribs or lets your torso slam forward.

sec09-card-sec09-F07.question_text: Until what age or height—plus fit check—must a child use an approved safety seat or booster?
sec09-card-sec09-F07.teaching_text: Adult belts ride dangerously across a small child's soft abdomen until height reaches four feet nine inches.

sec09-card-sec09-F08.question_text: Until what birthday must infants ride in a rear-facing child seat in Oregon?
sec09-card-sec09-F08.teaching_text: Rear-facing shells cradle fragile infant necks and spines evenly during sudden frontal impacts.

sec09-card-sec09-F09.question_text: What two everyday breakdowns between drivers account for a huge share of collisions?
sec09-card-sec09-F09.teaching_text: Active scanning fixes missed vehicles while early signaling eliminates surprise lane shifts.

sec09-card-sec09-F10.question_text: Which five built-in lights or sounds broadcast your intentions and warnings to surrounding drivers?
sec09-card-sec09-F10.teaching_text: Using turn signals, clean brake lamps, headlamps, polite horn taps, and flashers keeps neighbors informed.

sec09-card-sec09-F11.question_text: What three emergency maneuvers can avoid an imminent crash or soften its impact?
sec09-card-sec09-F11.teaching_text: Freezing purely on the brake pedal overlooks two faster escapes—steering clear or accelerating away.

sec09-card-sec09-F12.question_text: What road space makes emergency braking work, and where do you learn your car's specific brake type?
sec09-card-sec09-F12.teaching_text: Checking your manual ahead of time tells you whether anti-lock pulsing or threshold braking applies.

sec09-card-sec09-F13.question_text: When stopping distance runs out ahead, why is steering toward a pre-spotted escape route your best play?
sec09-card-sec09-F13.teaching_text: At highway speed a car needs hundreds of feet to halt yet shifts one lane width in yards.

sec09-card-sec09-F14.question_text: In what crash-angle scenario can pressing the gas pedal save you?
sec09-card-sec09-F14.teaching_text: Punching ahead into clear asphalt pulls your doors clear of a side-impact runner or skidding tailgater.

sec09-card-sec09-R20.question_text: How do you choose between steering away and speeding up during a split-second emergency?
sec09-card-sec09-R20.teaching_text: Match your escape to threat direction—swerve around blocked lanes ahead, accelerate away from closing bumpers behind.

sec09-card-sec09-F15.question_text: If your right tires drop off the pavement edge, what two reactions must you avoid while slowing?
sec09-card-sec09-F15.teaching_text: Slamming brakes with two tires on gravel and two on asphalt spins the car sideways instantly.

sec09-card-sec09-F16.question_text: How should your hands hold and aim the vehicle immediately after wheels drop onto a shoulder?
sec09-card-sec09-F16.teaching_text: Soft dirt and pavement lips tug hard on front tires—two firm hands keep the nose straight.

sec09-card-sec09-F17.question_text: Why must you use only minimal steering angle when climbing back over a pavement edge?
sec09-card-sec09-F17.teaching_text: Cranking hard against a drop-off lip flings the car across your lane straight into oncoming traffic.

sec09-card-sec09-F18.question_text: What three immediate steps respond to an oncoming car drifting across the centerline into your lane?
sec09-card-sec09-F18.teaching_text: Hugging the right edge buys survival space while horn blasts and headlight flashes wake drowsy drifters.

sec09-card-sec09-F19.question_text: Why must you never swerve left into the opposing lane to dodge an oncoming drifter?
sec09-card-sec09-F19.teaching_text: Waking drivers instinctively yank back into their own lane—a glancing bush or ditch beats head-on impact.

sec09-card-sec09-F20.question_text: How should you respond to yellow animal-crossing signs or wildlife standing near the shoulder?
sec09-card-sec09-F20.teaching_text: Deer and elk bolt unpredictably across asphalt and often travel in small herds.

sec09-card-sec09-F21.question_text: What three legal duties trigger if your vehicle strikes and injures a domestic animal in Oregon?
sec09-card-sec09-F21.teaching_text: Driving off breaks Oregon law—notify the owner right away or call local police if unfound.

sec09-card-sec09-F22.question_text: What does a horseback rider's raised hand mean, and what must you do unless stopping causes a crash?
sec09-card-sec09-F22.teaching_text: A panicked thousand-pound horse can buck into windshields—halting quietly lets the handler regain control.

sec09-card-sec09-F23.question_text: What cabin or exhaust noises must you avoid while passing horses or livestock along a road?
sec09-card-sec09-F23.teaching_text: Even a polite horn tap or revving engine spooks calm horses into bolting sideways into traffic.

sec09-card-sec09-R21.question_text: How does your horn rule flip completely between an oncoming drifting car and a frightened horse?
sec09-card-sec09-R21.teaching_text: Loud warnings snap distracted human drivers awake, whereas silence prevents panicking livestock.

sec09-card-sec09-F24.question_text: Which two fundamental changes belong whenever visibility drops or roads turn wet, snowy, or icy?
sec09-card-sec09-F24.teaching_text: Slowing down while stretching space ahead compensates for both delayed sight and weaker tire grip.

sec09-card-sec09-F25.question_text: During what daily clock span does Oregon law require headlights to burn?
sec09-card-sec09-F25.teaching_text: Unlike states that wait thirty minutes after sunset, Oregon turns headlights on right at sunset.

sec09-card-sec09-F26.question_text: During daytime weather, below what forward visibility footage must Oregon drivers switch headlights on?
sec09-card-sec09-F26.teaching_text: Oregon's one-thousand-foot threshold is wider than many states—light up early in mist, smoke, or rain.

sec09-card-sec09-F27.question_text: Within how many feet of an oncoming vehicle must you switch high beams down to low?
sec09-card-sec09-F27.teaching_text: Blinding an approaching driver on a two-lane road invites them to drift across your centerline.

sec09-card-sec09-F28.question_text: Within how many feet behind another vehicle must Oregon drivers dim high beams?
sec09-card-sec09-F28.teaching_text: Watch that Oregon-specific test number—three hundred fifty feet prevents mirror glare from blinding leaders.

sec09-card-sec09-R17.question_text: Compare Oregon's oncoming high-beam dimming distance against its following dimming distance?
sec09-card-sec09-R17.teaching_text: Direct windshield glare reaches eyes farther away than reflected mirror glare, explaining the two distances.

sec09-card-sec09-R18.question_text: How do one thousand feet, five hundred feet, and three hundred fifty feet split Oregon's headlight laws?
sec09-card-sec09-R18.teaching_text: Keeping those three footage benchmarks crisp prevents mixing up lights-on visibility with high-beam dimming.

sec09-card-sec09-F29.question_text: What must happen to auxiliary lights like fog lamps whenever law requires dimming your high beams?
sec09-card-sec09-F29.teaching_text: Bright aftermarket or fog lamps throw extra glare into oncoming eyes unless switched off when dimming.

sec09-card-sec09-F30.question_text: Is cruising at night or in bad weather using parking lights alone legal in Oregon?
sec09-card-sec09-F30.teaching_text: Dim amber marker bulbs project zero road beam and trick cross-street drivers into thinking you are parked.

sec09-card-sec09-F31.question_text: When do parking lights perform their actual legal job on a roadway or shoulder?
sec09-card-sec09-F31.teaching_text: Illuminated parking lamps outline a stationary shoulder vehicle so moving traffic steers clear in fog or dark.

sec09-card-sec09-F32.question_text: Why is your reaction margin naturally tighter after dark than in daylight?
sec09-card-sec09-F32.teaching_text: Unlit obstacles beyond your low-beam cone stay invisible until you roll right up to them.

sec09-card-sec09-F33.question_text: Where should you aim your eyes to avoid getting blinded by oncoming headlights at night?
sec09-card-sec09-F33.teaching_text: Tracking the white right-edge stripe guides lane position cleanly while sparing your dark-adapted pupils.

sec09-card-sec09-F34.question_text: What two maintenance checks keep your exterior lighting effective year-round?
sec09-card-sec09-F34.teaching_text: Road-grime film across plastic lenses can cut headlight output in half before you notice.

sec09-card-sec09-F35.question_text: What hidden danger makes two-lane passing at dawn or dusk extra risky?
sec09-card-sec09-F35.teaching_text: Gray cars running without headlights disappear against twilight asphalt until they are dangerously close.

sec09-card-sec09-F36.question_text: Which two vulnerable road-user groups demand extra nighttime alertness because dark clothing hides them?
sec09-card-sec09-F36.teaching_text: Walkers in dark hoodies and unlit bicycles blend into roadside shadows at intersections and driveways.

sec09-card-sec09-F37.question_text: Which headlight setting belongs in fog, dust, or smoke—and why does the brighter setting fail?
sec09-card-sec09-F37.teaching_text: High beams aim upward into airborne droplets, bouncing a blinding white wall right back at you.

sec09-card-sec09-R19.question_text: Why do high beams worsen visibility in thick fog despite producing stronger light?
sec09-card-sec09-R19.teaching_text: Aiming low beams downward lights pavement beneath the mist instead of illuminating the fog bank itself.

sec09-card-sec09-F38.question_text: When thick fog or storms force you off the road, where do you park and what lights go on?
sec09-card-sec09-F38.teaching_text: Getting completely off travel lanes with four-way hazard flashers stops trailing drivers from homing into taillights.

sec09-card-sec09-F39.question_text: How should rain change both the timing and foot pressure of your braking?
sec09-card-sec09-F39.teaching_text: Starting gentle deceleration sooner avoids locking slick tires while giving trailing drivers extra warning.

sec09-card-sec09-F40.question_text: Why can a light summer rain shower make dry asphalt unexpectedly slick?
sec09-card-sec09-F40.teaching_text: Weeks of dripped crankcase oil float upward on fresh raindrops into a greasy film.

sec09-card-sec09-F41.question_text: What three settings—for headlights, cruise control, and interior glass—belong whenever wipers run in rain?
sec09-card-sec09-F41.teaching_text: Active cruise control can spin wet tires on puddles, while clear defrosted glass and headlamps maintain sight.

sec09-card-sec09-F42.question_text: What happens to your tires and vehicle controls during hydroplaning?
sec09-card-sec09-F42.teaching_text: Once water lifts tread off pavement, slowing down beforehand is your best defense against losing control.

sec09-card-sec09-F43.question_text: How do you restore stopping bite right after splashing through deep water soaks your brakes?
sec09-card-sec09-F43.teaching_text: Light brake-pad friction warms wet rotors and squeezes water off before you need a real stop.

sec09-card-sec09-F44.question_text: What two serious failures make driving through flooded roadways too dangerous to risk?
sec09-card-sec09-F44.teaching_text: Moving floodwater sweeps cars sideways while ingested water hydro-locks engines right in the current.

sec09-card-sec09-F45.question_text: What speed, gap, window, and cruise-control rules govern driving on snow and ice?
sec09-card-sec09-F45.teaching_text: Scraping every window clean and keeping cruise control off prevents sudden wheelspin on icy grades.

sec09-card-sec09-R01.question_text: When should you skip driving altogether during severe winter weather?
sec09-card-sec09-R01.teaching_text: Heeding police or highway storm advisories keeps your car out of multi-vehicle mountain pileups.

sec09-card-sec09-R02.question_text: Why must you press the accelerator gently when pulling out on snow or ice?
sec09-card-sec09-R02.teaching_text: Delicate throttle pressure lets cold rubber bite packed snow instead of polishing ice beneath spinning wheels.

sec09-card-sec09-R03.question_text: How should you work the brake pedal on snowy or icy pavement to avoid skidding?
sec09-card-sec09-R03.teaching_text: Stomping hard on ice locks tires instantly and turns your car into an unsteerable sled.

sec09-card-sec09-R04.question_text: How can you safely gauge road slickness right after starting out on snow or ice?
sec09-card-sec09-R04.teaching_text: Sampling brake bite softly on an empty side street reveals black ice before fast intersections.

sec09-card-sec09-R05.question_text: How should you carry speed through turns when snow or ice coats the pavement?
sec09-card-sec09-R05.teaching_text: Slowing beforehand and holding smooth even pace keeps lateral cornering forces inside icy grip limits.

sec09-card-sec09-R06.question_text: Which two roadway locations freeze into ice patches while open sunlit stretches remain wet?
sec09-card-sec09-R06.teaching_text: Cold air chills bridge decks from both above and below while tree shade blocks warming sun.

sec09-card-sec09-R07.question_text: How much throttle belongs while climbing a snow-covered or icy upgrade?
sec09-card-sec09-R07.teaching_text: Spinning drive wheels halfway up a hill kills forward momentum and slides you backward.

sec09-card-sec09-R08.question_text: Is an icy road slicker right near freezing or when temperatures plunge far below zero?
sec09-card-sec09-R08.teaching_text: Ice near thirty-two degrees carries a microscopic film of meltwater that slashes friction worse than cold dry ice.

sec09-card-sec09-R09.question_text: What happens physically when a car skids, and what driver error triggers it?
sec09-card-sec09-R09.teaching_text: Even twenty miles per hour below a dry sign limit counts as too fast on glare ice.

sec09-card-sec09-R10.question_text: Why does Oregon's manual tell you to stay off the brake pedal during a skid?
sec09-card-sec09-R10.teaching_text: Brakes cannot grip effectively on sliding tires until speed drops and rolling contact returns.

sec09-card-sec09-R11.question_text: Where do you steer in a skid, and why straighten promptly as the nose recovers?
sec09-card-sec09-R11.teaching_text: Catching the wheel back as the car straightens stops violent fishtail swings in the opposite direction.
