sec09-card-sec09-R12.question_text: What two winter-equipment duties can posted Oregon highway signs require?
sec09-card-sec09-R12.teaching_text: Mountain passes shift quickly from carry-chains alerts to mandatory chain-up zones with steep fines.

sec09-card-sec09-R13.question_text: Beyond steel link chains, what else legally qualifies as chains in Oregon?
sec09-card-sec09-R13.teaching_text: Approved tire socks or external wheel-mounted traction spiders count alongside link and cable sets.

sec09-card-sec09-R14.question_text: Which three tire types qualify as legal traction tires in Oregon—and what sidewall symbol marks non-studded ones?
sec09-card-sec09-R14.teaching_text: Ordinary mud-and-snow all-season tires lack that official three-peak severe-snow sidewall certification for mountain passes.

sec09-card-sec09-R15.question_text: Between which calendar dates are studded tires generally permitted in Oregon, and why are alternatives urged?
sec09-card-sec09-R15.teaching_text: Metal studs grind costly ruts into bare asphalt, so Oregon encourages chains or mountain-snowflake tires instead.

sec09-card-sec09-R16.question_text: Where do state transportation officials post live Oregon chain and traction-tire requirements?
sec09-card-sec09-R16.teaching_text: Checking TripCheck dot com before mountain travel prevents getting turned back unequipped at snowy pass checkpoints.

sec10-card-sec10-F01.question_text: How do mental, emotional, and physical conditions like anger, worry, illness, or fatigue shape driving?
sec10-card-sec10-F01.teaching_text: Heavy worry or anger narrows tunnel vision and slows hazard reactions just like physical illness.

sec10-card-sec10-F02.question_text: What should you do immediately if you catch yourself driving on autopilot without tracking traffic?
sec10-card-sec10-F02.teaching_text: Going through mechanical motions without mental awareness means microsleep or highway hypnosis has set in.

sec10-card-sec10-F03.question_text: What is Oregon's mobile-device law for drivers under eighteen—even with Bluetooth or speakerphone?
sec10-card-sec10-F03.teaching_text: Minors cannot even use hands-free mode while driving—power the phone off or stash it backseat.

sec10-card-sec10-F04.question_text: How may an Oregon driver age eighteen or older legally use a mobile electronic device?
sec10-card-sec10-F04.teaching_text: Adult legality stops at single-tap activation through a mount or headset—holding or typing stays illegal.

sec10-card-sec10-R08.question_text: How does turning eighteen change Oregon's mobile-device restriction behind the wheel?
sec10-card-sec10-R08.teaching_text: Test questions love pairing a seventeen-year-old on Bluetooth—under eighteen means zero phone use period.

sec10-card-sec10-F05.question_text: What does Oregon law say about mounting a television, tablet, or video screen in the cabin?
sec10-card-sec10-F05.teaching_text: Moving video pulls peripheral gaze involuntarily off traffic, so entertainment screens belong strictly out of sight.

sec10-card-sec10-F06.question_text: At what outside distance does booming car audio become illegal in Oregon—and why?
sec10-card-sec10-F06.teaching_text: Blasting music audible fifty feet away drowns out emergency sirens, horn warnings, and screeching tires.

sec10-card-sec10-F07.question_text: Why are eating, drinking, reading, grooming, or peeling off a jacket hazardous while rolling?
sec10-card-sec10-F07.teaching_text: Even two seconds glanced down at spilled coffee or a jacket zipper covers half a football field blind.

sec10-card-sec10-F08.question_text: May you drive with a small dog, child, or parcel resting in your lap or arms?
sec10-card-sec10-F08.teaching_text: Anything wedged between your chest and steering wheel blocks emergency turns and turns lethal with airbags.

sec10-card-sec10-F09.question_text: What must you do first when children, pets, or passengers in back need hands-on help?
sec10-card-sec10-F09.teaching_text: Twisting around toward the backseat yanks your shoulders and steering wheel straight off the lane.

sec10-card-sec10-F10.question_text: Which angry behaviors behind the wheel constitute road rage in Oregon's manual?
sec10-card-sec10-F10.teaching_text: Aggressive tailgating, cut-offs, yelling, and hostile hand signs escalate minor traffic errors into violence.

sec10-card-sec10-F11.question_text: How should you respond when an angry, aggressive motorist tailgates or crowds you?
sec10-card-sec10-F11.teaching_text: Speeding up to hold your lane turns one reckless stranger into a two-car high-speed duel.

sec10-card-sec10-F12.question_text: Which five physical or lane-keeping red flags warn you are about to fall asleep driving?
sec10-card-sec10-F12.teaching_text: By the time your head nods or tires touch rumble strips, microsleep is seconds away.

sec10-card-sec10-F13.question_text: Which two driving abilities drop when you are tired, and how do you prevent drowsy crashes?
sec10-card-sec10-F13.teaching_text: Starting trips rested and scheduling regular stretch stops keeps reaction timing sharp on long highways.

sec10-card-sec10-F14.question_text: Instead of pushing drowsy miles to finish a trip, what two stops restore safety?
sec10-card-sec10-F14.teaching_text: Ten minutes from home is where exhausted commuters talk themselves into fatal run-off-road crashes.

sec10-card-sec10-F15.question_text: Why does drinking water—paired with conversation and sharing wheel shifts—help fight trip fatigue?
sec10-card-sec10-F15.teaching_text: Mild dehydration triggers sluggish fatigue quickly, while rotating drivers lets each person sleep properly.

sec10-card-sec10-F16.question_text: What common medication side effect must every driver watch out for before picking up keys?
sec10-card-sec10-F16.teaching_text: Allergy, pain, and cold remedies slow brain processing just like alcohol despite coming from a pharmacy.

sec10-card-sec10-F17.question_text: What honest self-check belongs before driving with an illness, especially ahead of a long drive?
sec10-card-sec10-F17.teaching_text: Fever, dizziness, and coughing fits drain concentration fast once an hour-long highway drive begins.

sec10-card-sec10-F18.question_text: Because certain health conditions risk confusion, slow reactions, or blackouts, whom should you consult?
sec10-card-sec10-F18.teaching_text: A physician can adjust treatment or timing before a sudden blackout happens at highway speed.

sec10-card-sec10-F19.question_text: Which four safety clues do your ears catch while driving?
sec10-card-sec10-F19.teaching_text: Changing tire hum warns of ice, mechanical clunks flag trouble, and sirens announce approaching responders.

sec10-card-sec10-F20.question_text: Why does Oregon's manual tell drivers not to wear ear-covering or sound-blocking headphones?
sec10-card-sec10-F20.teaching_text: Sealing both ears cuts off horns, sirens, and blind-spot engine roar right beside your door.

sec10-card-sec10-F21.question_text: What is the only safe plan after drinking alcohol or using impairing drugs?
sec10-card-sec10-F21.teaching_text: Alcohol and drugs multiply fatal crash risk—line up a sober driver or transit ride instead.

sec10-card-sec10-F22.question_text: Can police arrest you for impaired driving whenever alcohol or drugs noticeably affect your driving?
sec10-card-sec10-F22.teaching_text: You need not hit a specific number—driving while noticeably affected by intoxicants justifies arrest.

sec10-card-sec10-F24.question_text: Which drug leads impaired crashes, what second substance adds major Oregon crashes, and what happens together?
sec10-card-sec10-F24.teaching_text: Mixing alcohol with cannabis multiplies reaction delays and lane weaving far worse than either alone.

sec10-card-sec10-F25.question_text: How should you verify store-shelf or prescription medicines, and what if a new dose feels uncertain?
sec10-card-sec10-F25.teaching_text: Never test a brand-new prescription's drowsiness behind a steering wheel—arrange another ride first.

sec10-card-sec10-F26.question_text: Does Oregon's impaired-driving law apply solely to alcohol, or how broad is its reach?
sec10-card-sec10-F26.teaching_text: Cannabis, prescription sedatives, inhalants, and illegal drugs carry the exact same criminal charge as alcohol.

sec10-card-sec10-F27.question_text: Which three chemical tests have you already agreed to take simply by driving on Oregon roads?
sec10-card-sec10-F27.teaching_text: Operating a motor vehicle in Oregon automatically grants legal consent when an officer requests testing.

sec10-card-sec10-F28.question_text: Which two penalties hit a driver who refuses an officer's implied-consent test?
sec10-card-sec10-F28.teaching_text: Saying no at the roadside triggers harsh administrative license suspension plus steep monetary fines.

sec10-card-sec10-R11.question_text: Why doesn't refusing a breath, blood, or urine test dodge impaired-driving consequences?
sec10-card-sec10-R11.teaching_text: Refusal carries standalone penalties regardless of how a later court case turns out.

sec10-card-sec10-F29.question_text: What blood alcohol concentration fails the test for any Oregon driver under twenty-one?
sec10-card-sec10-F29.teaching_text: Oregon enforces strict zero tolerance—even a trace alcohol reading above zero fails minors.

sec10-card-sec10-F31.question_text: What does Oregon's Open Container law prohibit inside a vehicle on any road?
sec10-card-sec10-F31.teaching_text: Even a sober driver gets cited if a passenger holds an unsealed drink inside the cabin.

sec10-card-sec10-F32.question_text: When does a bottle count as open, and where must a previously opened bottle ride?
sec10-card-sec10-F32.teaching_text: Twisting a cap back onto half a wine bottle still counts as open unless locked in the trunk.

sec10-card-sec10-R12.question_text: Does screwing the cap tightly back onto an unsealed liquor bottle make it legal inside the passenger cabin?
sec10-card-sec10-R12.teaching_text: Once the original seal snaps, only the trunk keeps you compliant with open-container law.

sec10-card-sec10-F33.question_text: Who does Oregon's manual say should ride inside an open pickup bed or on a vehicle's exterior?
sec10-card-sec10-F33.teaching_text: Steel cargo beds lack seats and belts, ejecting riders onto pavement during minor swerves.

sec10-card-sec10-F34.question_text: For passengers under eighteen, what does Oregon law strictly outlaw regarding pickup beds, hoods, or fenders?
sec10-card-sec10-F34.teaching_text: Allowing a teen or child in an open truck bed or on running boards is flatly illegal.

sec10-card-sec10-F35.question_text: Under what condition may a dog legally ride in an open pickup bed in Oregon?
sec10-card-sec10-F35.teaching_text: Unsecured dogs slide or leap out at highway speed—Oregon mandates a crate, rack, or restraint.

sec10-card-sec10-R13.question_text: Compare Oregon's pickup-bed rules across adults, riders under eighteen, and dogs?
sec10-card-sec10-R13.teaching_text: Keep those three tiers straight—minors never ride outside, while dogs require fall-preventing hardware.

sec10-card-sec10-F36.question_text: What habit prevents most mechanical road failures, and what guide lists your car's service schedule?
sec10-card-sec10-F36.teaching_text: Following scheduled tire, brake, and fluid checks in your owner's manual stops highway breakdowns early.

sec10-card-sec10-F37.question_text: How does a front-tire blowout feel through the wheel compared with a rear-tire blowout?
sec10-card-sec10-F37.teaching_text: Front blowouts yank steering toward the flat side while rear blowouts make the tail fishtail.

sec10-card-sec10-F38.question_text: What three calm steps bring a vehicle safely off the road after any tire blows out?
sec10-card-sec10-F38.teaching_text: Stomping brakes on a shredded tire spins the rim—let momentum bleed gently before leaving lanes.

sec10-card-sec10-R14.question_text: Even though front blowouts pull and rear blowouts sway, does your recovery action change?
sec10-card-sec10-R14.teaching_text: Front or back, two firm hands, gradual coast-down, and a smooth shoulder exit always win.

sec10-card-sec10-F39.question_text: What is the immediate first pedal action to try if your service brakes suddenly lose pressure?
sec10-card-sec10-F39.teaching_text: Rapid pumping can rebuild enough hydraulic line pressure in dual-circuit brakes for one stop.

sec10-card-sec10-F40.question_text: If pumping failed brakes isn't enough, how do your transmission and parking brake help scrub speed?
sec10-card-sec10-F40.teaching_text: Engine compression slows wheels smoothly while gradual parking-brake tension avoids locking the rear axle.

sec10-card-sec10-F41.question_text: With failed brakes, how do you alert surrounding traffic and where do you guide the car?
sec10-card-sec10-F41.teaching_text: Horn blasts and flashing lights clear a path ahead until engine drag slows you onto the shoulder.

sec10-card-sec10-R01.question_text: If your headlights suddenly cut out at night, which switches should you try immediately?
sec10-card-sec10-R01.teaching_text: Toggling the main switch or hitting high beams, fogs, or four-way flashers often restores enough glow.

sec10-card-sec10-R02.question_text: Once backup flashers or beams give minimal sight after headlight failure, where do you go?
sec10-card-sec10-R02.teaching_text: Never keep cruising dark—get completely onto the right shoulder before battery or bulb power dies.

sec10-card-sec10-R03.question_text: Does steering lock solid if power-steering assist fails—and how should you handle it?
sec10-card-sec10-R03.teaching_text: Mechanical linkage still turns front tires—expect heavy effort as you slow onto the shoulder.

sec10-card-sec10-R04.question_text: If the accelerator sticks down, how and with what hand technique should you shift?
sec10-card-sec10-R04.teaching_text: Pushing forward with an open palm lands cleanly in neutral without accidentally overshooting into reverse.

sec10-card-sec10-R05.question_text: After shifting a runaway engine into neutral, how do you bring the vehicle off the highway?
sec10-card-sec10-R05.teaching_text: Keep the engine running in neutral so power steering and vacuum brake boost stay alive until parked.

sec10-card-sec10-R15.question_text: Why do failed brakes want a lower gear whereas a stuck accelerator wants neutral?
sec10-card-sec10-R15.teaching_text: Failed brakes borrow engine drag to slow down, while a racing throttle must disconnect from wheels.

sec10-card-sec10-R06.question_text: How do your speed choice, launches, and stops save gasoline on everyday drives?
sec10-card-sec10-R06.teaching_text: Jackrabbit launches and late hard stops burn extra fuel as wasted heat in brakes.

sec10-card-sec10-R07.question_text: Beyond smooth pedal habits, what three planning and upkeep choices stretch fuel mileage?
sec10-card-sec10-R07.teaching_text: Warm engines handle chained errands efficiently while proper tire pressure and tune-ups cut rolling drag.

sec11-card-sec11-F01.question_text: Which everyday vehicles—and up to what gross weight—does an Oregon non-commercial Class C license cover?
sec11-card-sec11-F01.teaching_text: Mopeds and autocycles fit under standard Class C too, while full motorcycles and heavy rigs need endorsements.

sec11-card-sec11-F02.question_text: What is the minimum age to apply for an Oregon instruction permit?
sec11-card-sec11-F02.teaching_text: Turning fifteen opens supervised learner practice so teens build six-plus months of experience.

sec11-card-sec11-F03.question_text: What is the minimum age to apply for an Oregon driver license?
sec11-card-sec11-F03.teaching_text: Applicants under eighteen must also hold their permit six months and finish supervised practice hours.

sec11-card-sec11-R11.question_text: How do Oregon's minimum instruction-permit age and minimum driver-license age step up?
sec11-card-sec11-R11.teaching_text: That one-year age step pairs naturally with Oregon's six-month minimum teen permit holding period.

sec11-card-sec11-F04.question_text: Who must sign an electronic application for a minor under eighteen—and what if that adult cannot attend?
sec11-card-sec11-F04.teaching_text: Bringing the signed parental-consent form lets a minor complete office processing when a guardian works.

sec11-card-sec11-F05.question_text: Which two legal statuses waive the parent-signature requirement for an applicant under eighteen?
sec11-card-sec11-F05.teaching_text: Presenting official marriage or court-emancipation proof lets an independent minor sign on their own.

sec11-card-sec11-F06.question_text: Which three core facts must every Oregon permit or license applicant prove?
sec11-card-sec11-F06.teaching_text: Arriving without valid proof of any one of those three items halts your application at the counter.

sec11-card-sec11-F07.question_text: How do you satisfy Oregon's Social Security Number rule if one has never been issued to you?
sec11-card-sec11-F07.teaching_text: Applicants ineligible for a Social Security Number simply complete an electronic non-issuance certification.

sec11-card-sec11-F08.question_text: What school-status proof must a first-time Oregon applicant under eighteen provide?
sec11-card-sec11-F08.teaching_text: Minors who have already finished school present a high school diploma or equivalency certificate instead.

sec11-card-sec11-F09.question_text: Along with paying required fees, which three exams unlock an Oregon driving privilege?
sec11-card-sec11-F09.teaching_text: Written rules, clear eyesight, and behind-the-wheel control must all pass before plastic is issued.

sec11-card-sec11-F10.question_text: Which four head, face, or eye items must come off before your Oregon license photo?
sec11-card-sec11-F10.teaching_text: Facial-recognition accuracy requires unobstructed eyebrows, bare skin, and natural iris appearance without glasses glare.

sec11-card-sec11-F11.question_text: How do out-of-state suspensions and existing licenses or identification cards affect getting an Oregon license?
sec11-card-sec11-F11.teaching_text: National driver registries block new Oregon privileges until any other state's suspension is cleared.

sec11-card-sec11-F12.question_text: How long must a teen under eighteen hold an instruction permit—and does out-of-state permit time count?
sec11-card-sec11-F12.teaching_text: Moving teens don't restart at zero—verified months held on another state's learner permit carry over.

sec11-card-sec11-F13.question_text: What are the two supervised-driving hour options for an Oregon license applicant under eighteen?
sec11-card-sec11-F13.teaching_text: Completing a state-approved traffic-safety education course cuts required logged practice hours cleanly in half.

sec11-card-sec11-F14.question_text: What minimum age and license tenure must your front-seat supervisor hold for teen practice hours to count?
sec11-card-sec11-F14.teaching_text: Driving beside an eighteen-year-old sibling doesn't count—your coach needs age twenty-one plus three licensed years.

sec11-card-sec11-R12.question_text: How does finishing an approved driver-education course change a teen's supervised-practice total?
sec11-card-sec11-R12.teaching_text: Make sure course completion proof reaches the licensing office before scheduling your road test.

sec11-card-sec11-R13.question_text: Keep the two teen-practice time rules straight: permit holding months versus supervisor licensed years?
sec11-card-sec11-R13.teaching_text: Both clock requirements must be satisfied before any applicant under eighteen earns a license.

sec11-card-sec11-F15.question_text: In what physical document format must identity and birth-date proofs be presented?
sec11-card-sec11-F15.teaching_text: Phone photos, scans, or uncertified home photocopies get rejected at the licensing counter.

sec11-card-sec11-F16.question_text: Which birth certificate proves identity in Oregon—and which two keepsake records get rejected?
sec11-card-sec11-F16.teaching_text: Decorative footprints from a hospital or church baptismal certificates lack official vital-statistics certification.

sec11-card-sec11-F17.question_text: How long past its printed expiration date can a United States passport or passport card still prove identity?
sec11-card-sec11-F17.teaching_text: Oregon grants a generous five-year post-expiration window on United States passports for identity verification.

sec11-card-sec11-F18.question_text: Which tribal identification cards and federal citizenship certificates prove identity in Oregon?
sec11-card-sec11-F18.teaching_text: Approved cards from federally recognized tribes inside Oregon work alongside Naturalization or Citizenship certificates.

sec11-card-sec11-F19.question_text: Up to how many years past expiration are federal work, permanent-resident, re-entry, or foreign-passport documents accepted?
sec11-card-sec11-F19.teaching_text: Matching the passport rule, those listed federal immigration and travel cards remain usable five years post-expiry.

sec11-card-sec11-F20.question_text: How long past expiration does Oregon accept an official consulate card for identity?
sec11-card-sec11-F20.teaching_text: Consulate cards share that exact same five-year grace window as passports and immigration cards.

sec11-card-sec11-F21.question_text: Up to how many years after expiring can an old Oregon license, permit, or identification card prove identity?
sec11-card-sec11-F21.teaching_text: Because state licensing databases already hold your prior record, home-state cards count for thirteen years.

sec11-card-sec11-F22.question_text: How long past expiration is an out-of-state license, permit, or identification card accepted as Oregon identity proof?
sec11-card-sec11-F22.teaching_text: New arrivals should transfer promptly—once an out-of-state card passes one year expired, bring a passport or birth record.

sec11-card-sec11-R14.question_text: Contrast Oregon's post-expiration identity window for an Oregon card versus an out-of-state card?
sec11-card-sec11-R14.teaching_text: That thirteen-to-one gap is a classic Oregon knowledge-exam favorite—keep home and away separate.

sec11-card-sec11-F23.question_text: What extra documentation is required when your current legal name differs from your birth or identity record?
sec11-card-sec11-F23.teaching_text: Certified marriage certificates, divorce decrees, or court orders bridge every name link cleanly.

sec11-card-sec11-F24.question_text: How many qualifying documents are needed to prove your Oregon residence address on a standard application?
sec11-card-sec11-F24.teaching_text: Standard Oregon privileges need only a single valid address proof showing your name and street.

sec11-card-sec11-F25.question_text: If you have no bills in your own name yet, how can someone living with you verify your address?
sec11-card-sec11-F25.teaching_text: A parent or roommate appearing in person with their own matching license certifies teen residency easily.

sec11-card-sec11-F26.question_text: Which sender types qualify as address-proof mail—and which two everyday mail types get rejected?
sec11-card-sec11-F26.teaching_text: Handwritten birthday cards or yellow postal-forwarding stickers never verify where you currently live.

sec11-card-sec11-F27.question_text: Which four school, utility, or homeownership records also prove your Oregon residence address?
sec11-card-sec11-F27.teaching_text: High school transcripts or utility hookup orders work cleanly when regular billing hasn't started.

sec11-card-sec11-F29.question_text: What two card markings appear when you join Oregon's organ, eye, and tissue donor registry?
sec11-card-sec11-F29.teaching_text: Printing donor status on both sides gives hospital transplant teams instant, unmistakable confirmation.

sec11-card-sec11-F30.question_text: What military discharge paperwork and discharge character earn a veteran designation on an Oregon card?
sec11-card-sec11-F30.teaching_text: Presenting military separation form two-fourteen or two-fifteen showing honorable conditions adds the veteran mark.

sec11-card-sec11-F31.question_text: What medical proof is needed for a deaf or hard-of-hearing card designation—and who sees it?
sec11-card-sec11-F31.teaching_text: Officers running your plate see the hearing alert beforehand so roadside communication starts smoothly.

sec11-card-sec11-R17.question_text: How do documentation rules differ between adding a veteran designation and a deaf-or-hard-of-hearing designation?
sec11-card-sec11-R17.teaching_text: Military status verifies discharge records, whereas communication-safety alerts carry zero paperwork barrier.

sec11-card-sec11-F32.question_text: What are Oregon's minimum bodily-injury liability limits for one person versus two or more people per crash?
sec11-card-sec11-F32.teaching_text: Liability insurance pays medical and death claims for people you injure in another vehicle.

sec11-card-sec11-F33.question_text: What is Oregon's minimum per-crash liability coverage for damaging someone else's vehicle or property?
sec11-card-sec11-F33.teaching_text: Twenty thousand dollars covers repairs to other cars, fences, or poles you strike.

sec11-card-sec11-R15.question_text: Put Oregon's three core liability numbers together: one injured person, multiple injured, and property damage?
sec11-card-sec11-R15.teaching_text: Insurance policies write that exact trio as twenty-five slash fifty slash twenty.

sec11-card-sec11-F34.question_text: At least how much Personal Injury Protection per person—and over what post-crash timespan—does Oregon require?
sec11-card-sec11-F34.teaching_text: Personal Injury Protection covers your own medical and dental bills within two years regardless of fault.

sec11-card-sec11-F35.question_text: What minimum per-person and per-crash bodily-injury amounts apply to Oregon Uninsured Motorist coverage?
sec11-card-sec11-F35.teaching_text: Uninsured Motorist coverage mirrors your bodily-injury liability numbers to protect you from hit-and-runs.

sec11-card-sec11-R16.question_text: How does Oregon's Personal Injury Protection dollar minimum differ from Uninsured Motorist bodily-injury minimums?
sec11-card-sec11-R16.teaching_text: Keep fifteen thousand for immediate medical-expense protection separate from twenty-five-and-fifty uninsured limits.

sec11-card-sec11-F36.question_text: Why does Oregon's manual reject calling a distracted, drowsy, or careless crash an accident?
sec11-card-sec11-F36.teaching_text: Calling preventable errors mere bad luck excuses poor choices—alert defensive habits stop most crashes.

sec11-card-sec11-F37.question_text: After an uninjured fender-bender where cars still drive safely, what must you do before trading details?
sec11-card-sec11-F37.teaching_text: Standing between bumpers in live freeway lanes causes deadly secondary crashes—move off first.

sec11-card-sec11-F38.question_text: What two duties govern helping someone hurt in a collision?
sec11-card-sec11-F38.teaching_text: Calling emergency medics helps immediately, whereas dragging an injured neck victim worsens spinal trauma.

sec11-card-sec11-F39.question_text: Which five pieces of identification and coverage info must drivers exchange after a collision?
sec11-card-sec11-F39.teaching_text: Having a photo of your insurance card and registration ready keeps roadside info-swapping calm and complete.

sec11-card-sec11-F40.question_text: Which two severe victim conditions require staying at a crash scene until law enforcement arrives?
sec11-card-sec11-F40.teaching_text: Fatalities or unconscious victims turn the crash into an active police investigation scene.

sec11-card-sec11-R01.question_text: Within how many hours—and above what dollar damage to your car or non-vehicle property—must you report?
sec11-card-sec11-R01.teaching_text: Missing that three-day window when damage tops two thousand five hundred dollars risks license suspension.

sec11-card-sec11-R02.question_text: How do vehicle damage and towing combine to trigger an Oregon seventy-two-hour collision report?
sec11-card-sec11-R02.teaching_text: Even if your own bumper barely scratched, another car exceeding twenty-five hundred or getting towed triggers reporting.

sec11-card-sec11-R03.question_text: Regardless of bumper repair cost, what human outcome always triggers a mandatory Oregon collision report?
sec11-card-sec11-R03.teaching_text: Even a zero-dollar bumper tap that injures a pedestrian or rider requires filing within seventy-two hours.

sec11-card-sec11-R04.question_text: When does the registered vehicle owner—rather than the driver—have to file Oregon's collision report?
sec11-card-sec11-R04.teaching_text: If a hospitalized or negligent borrower skips filing, legal responsibility falls onto the vehicle's owner.

sec11-card-sec11-R05.question_text: If a police officer writes an official crash report at the scene, are you excused from filing yours?
sec11-card-sec11-R05.teaching_text: That classic misconception suspends thousands of licenses—police reports never satisfy your personal filing duty.

sec11-card-sec11-R06.question_text: What must you do after bumping an unoccupied parked vehicle if you cannot locate its owner?
sec11-card-sec11-R06.teaching_text: Secure a clear note with your name, address, and brief explanation where the returning owner will spot it.

sec11-card-sec11-R07.question_text: What duty applies if your car knocks over a mailbox, fence, sign, or landscaping?
sec11-card-sec11-R07.teaching_text: Non-vehicle property carries hit-and-run duties too—locate the owner or person in charge and inform them.

sec11-card-sec11-R08.question_text: What ongoing performance standard determines whether you keep your Oregon driving privilege?
sec11-card-sec11-R08.teaching_text: Safe, lawful choices protect your record from suspensions and steep insurance surcharges.

sec11-card-sec11-R09.question_text: Which three major violations—involving impairment, crashes, or coverage—can strip your Oregon driving privilege?
sec11-card-sec11-R09.teaching_text: Inhalants count alongside alcohol and drugs, and skipping insurance or crash reports suspends privileges too.

sec11-card-sec11-R10.question_text: How can stacked traffic tickets or ignored court fines affect your Oregon license?
sec11-card-sec11-R10.teaching_text: Repeated convictions trigger Oregon's Driver Improvement Program, and unpaid court fines suspend licenses too.

sec08-card-sec08-F01.question_text: What visual checks and right-of-way rule apply every time you pull out from a parked or stopped spot?
sec08-card-sec08-F01.teaching_text: Moving lanes already own the roadway, so creeping out without a shoulder check invites an immediate sideswipe.

sec08-card-sec08-R02.question_text: Before rolling away from a curb or stopped spot, who holds the right of way and where must you look?
sec08-card-sec08-R02.teaching_text: Bicyclists and approaching cars never have to brake for a parked vehicle nosing back into live flow.

sec08-card-sec08-F02.question_text: Which direction must your car face whenever you parallel park along a street?
sec08-card-sec08-F02.teaching_text: Crossing oncoming lanes to park nose-first against the curb creates head-on conflict going in and pulling out.

sec08-card-sec08-F03.question_text: What is the maximum distance your tires may sit from a curb when parallel parked, or where do you park without a curb?
sec08-card-sec08-F03.teaching_text: Leaving wide gaps pushes your driver's door and mirror straight out into cyclists and passing fenders.

sec08-card-sec08-R01.question_text: How does Oregon's parallel parking distance rule change when a street has no curb?
sec08-card-sec08-R01.teaching_text: Exam questions test whether you invent a fake inch number on rural shoulders where hugging the edge is the actual rule.

sec08-card-sec08-F04.question_text: Where must all of your tires rest when parking in a marked stall?
sec08-card-sec08-F04.teaching_text: Straddling a white stall stripe steals door clearance from neighboring cars and earns parking citations.

sec08-card-sec08-F05.question_text: What three steering and backing steps does the Oregon manual list for parallel parking behind Car A?
sec08-card-sec08-F05.teaching_text: Starting side-by-side with the front car sets your pivot angle cleanly so you never clip its rear bumper.

sec08-card-sec08-F06.question_text: In which three types of places do you most often encounter angle parking?
sec08-card-sec08-F06.teaching_text: Diagonal stalls fit more vehicles along broad retail avenues where backing out requires extra patience.

sec08-card-sec08-F07.question_text: When must drivers of long or large vehicles skip an angle parking stall?
sec08-card-sec08-F07.teaching_text: A crew-cab pickup or camper jutting out into the travel lane forces passing cars across the centerline.

sec08-card-sec08-F08.question_text: What special entry rule may posted signs require at certain angle parking stalls?
sec08-card-sec08-F08.teaching_text: Backing into reverse-angle stalls points your windshield straight toward traffic so leaving later has clear visibility.

sec08-card-sec08-F09.question_text: What brake and transmission settings must you apply every time you park on a hill?
sec08-card-sec08-F09.teaching_text: Combining mechanical cable hold with transmission lock keeps gravity from creeping a heavy car down a slope.

sec08-card-sec08-R05.question_text: When parking on a slope, what step stays identical and what step changes between manual and automatic cars?
sec08-card-sec08-R05.teaching_text: Leaving a manual stick in neutral relies solely on a cable that can stretch or snap on steep grades.

sec08-card-sec08-F10.question_text: What safety purpose does turning your front wheels serve when parking on a hill?
sec08-card-sec08-F10.teaching_text: Properly angled front tires use the concrete curb or shoulder edge as a physical chock if brakes let go.

sec08-card-sec08-F11.question_text: Which way must you turn your front wheels when parked facing downhill beside a curb?
sec08-card-sec08-F11.teaching_text: Gravity pulls nose-first, so angling right wedges the front tire straight against the concrete curb face.

sec08-card-sec08-F12.question_text: Which way must you turn your front wheels when parked facing uphill beside a curb?
sec08-card-sec08-F12.teaching_text: If the car rolls backward, left-turned front tires swing the rear of the front wheel cleanly against the curb.

sec08-card-sec08-F13.question_text: Which way do your front wheels point when parking on a hill that has no curb?
sec08-card-sec08-F13.teaching_text: Without raised concrete to catch a tire, steering toward the shoulder sends a rolling car off the road instead of into traffic.

sec08-card-sec08-R03.question_text: At a curbed street, why do downhill and uphill wheel angles point in opposite directions?
sec08-card-sec08-R03.teaching_text: Uphill beside a curb is the single case where wheels point toward the street so backward roll hooks the curb.

sec08-card-sec08-R04.question_text: When there is no curb on a hill, does your wheel direction change between uphill and downhill?
sec08-card-sec08-R04.teaching_text: Whether rolling forward or backward on an open shoulder, angling right steers the car away from oncoming lanes.

sec08-card-sec08-F14.question_text: Which two categories of applicants can receive disabled parking permits from Oregon?
sec08-card-sec08-F14.teaching_text: Care facilities and shuttle programs transporting passengers with mobility needs qualify alongside individual placard holders.

sec08-card-sec08-F15.question_text: Where do symbols appear to mark a reserved disabled parking space?
sec08-card-sec08-F15.teaching_text: Checking upright post signs matters on rainy or snowy days when wet glare hides blue pavement paint.

sec08-card-sec08-F16.question_text: What is required to park legally in any stall marked for people with disabilities?
sec08-card-sec08-F16.teaching_text: Accessible stalls give wheelchair ramps essential side clearance that unauthorized cars block immediately.

sec08-card-sec08-F17.question_text: What fine range applies in Oregon for parking in a disabled space without a permit, even briefly?
sec08-card-sec08-F17.teaching_text: Idling two minutes to grab takeout triggers the exact same steep citation bracket as leaving a car all afternoon.

sec08-card-sec08-F18.question_text: Does staying seated inside your car exempt you from Oregon's stopping and parking bans?
sec08-card-sec08-F18.teaching_text: Sitting behind the wheel scrolling your phone in a no-parking zone blocks sightlines identically to a locked empty car.

sec08-card-sec08-F19.question_text: Under what narrow circumstances are Oregon's no-stopping and no-parking zones excused?
sec08-card-sec08-F19.teaching_text: Lawmakers carve out an exception only when dead machinery or missing shoulders leave you physically unable to clear traffic.

sec08-card-sec08-R06.question_text: Why doesn't flashing your hazards for a thirty-second package drop waive a no-stopping rule?
sec08-card-sec08-R06.teaching_text: Hazard lamps are never a park-anywhere pass when your engine runs fine and only convenience stops you.

sec08-card-sec08-F20.question_text: Is stopping or parking allowed inside a street's travel lane or within an intersection?
sec08-card-sec08-F20.teaching_text: Halting in active flow forces trailing drivers into blind emergency swerves across neighboring lanes.

sec08-card-sec08-F21.question_text: What does double parking mean, and how does Oregon law treat it?
sec08-card-sec08-F21.teaching_text: Blocking the lane next to curbside cars traps parked drivers inside and chokes city traffic down to one lane.

sec08-card-sec08-F22.question_text: Which four non-car travel paths strictly forbid stopping or parking?
sec08-card-sec08-F22.teaching_text: Blocking any of these corridors forces walkers or cyclists into live lanes or halts rail transit dead.

sec08-card-sec08-F23.question_text: Which elevated, enclosed, and divided highway areas ban stopping and parking?
sec08-card-sec08-F23.teaching_text: Zero shoulder escape room on spans and tunnels turns any parked vehicle into a high-speed collision wall.

sec08-card-sec08-F24.question_text: When is stopping or parking prohibited near road work or construction?
sec08-card-sec08-F24.teaching_text: Narrowed work chutes already run tight tolerances without a parked car choking flow around orange cones.

sec08-card-sec08-F25.question_text: How does Oregon regulate stopping in front of driveways and painted diagonal road stripes?
sec08-card-sec08-F25.teaching_text: Diagonal zebra gore stripes preserve sightlines and access ramps just like posted no-parking signs.

sec08-card-sec08-F26.question_text: How many feet of clear curb must you leave on either side of a fire hydrant in Oregon?
sec08-card-sec08-F26.teaching_text: Oregon sets a ten-foot hydrant buffer—shorter than states using fifteen—making exact state numbers crucial on test day.

sec08-card-sec08-R07.question_text: Can you briefly stop without parking inside Oregon's restricted zones like the ten-foot hydrant buffer?
sec08-card-sec08-R07.teaching_text: Idling beside a hydrant blocks engine-company supply hoses until you pull away, so Oregon bans stopping outright.

sec08-card-sec08-F27.question_text: What no-parking distances apply on the same side versus the opposite side of a fire station driveway?
sec08-card-sec08-F27.teaching_text: Long ladder trucks need a wide seventy-five-foot swing arc across the street to pull out of bay doors fast.

sec08-card-sec08-R08.question_text: Which side of the street requires the much larger clearance from a fire station driveway, and what are the numbers?
sec08-card-sec08-R08.teaching_text: Many test-takers guess the firehouse curb has the bigger number, forgetting the wide turning radius needed across the road.

sec08-card-sec08-F28.question_text: How far back from an intersection crosswalk—marked or unmarked—must you park?
sec08-card-sec08-F28.teaching_text: Parking right up to the corner hides children stepping off the curb until oncoming drivers have zero braking room.

sec08-card-sec08-F29.question_text: What distance and visibility condition make parking ahead of a traffic sign or signal illegal?
sec08-card-sec08-F29.teaching_text: A tall van or SUV parked close ahead of a stop sign masks the octagon from approaching drivers.

sec08-card-sec08-F30.question_text: What minimum distance from the nearest rail applies when parking near a railroad or light rail crossing?
sec08-card-sec08-F30.teaching_text: Parked cars crowding crossing gates block approaching drivers from spotting warning flashers and oncoming trains.

sec08-card-sec08-R10.question_text: How does the fifty-foot no-parking rule at traffic signs differ from the fifty-foot rule at railroad crossings?
sec08-card-sec08-R10.teaching_text: A low coupe that leaves a tall sign visible can park closer, whereas rail crossings enforce fifty feet unconditionally.

sec08-card-sec08-F32.question_text: When a breakdown leaves zero alternatives, what conditions allow a brief stop in a banned spot and what lights go on?
sec08-card-sec08-F32.teaching_text: Switching four-way emergency flashers on immediately warns approaching traffic that your car is disabled rather than moving.

sec08-card-sec08-F33.question_text: What clearance check determines whether you may park on a highway shoulder when needed?
sec08-card-sec08-F33.teaching_text: If a narrow gravel edge leaves your left wheels overhanging the fog line, highway traffic loses safe clearance.

sec08-card-sec08-F34.question_text: When must you place flares, flags, or warning signals around a stopped vehicle, and at what distance?
sec08-card-sec08-F34.teaching_text: Drivers rounding a blind hill crest at highway speed need early advance markers in both directions before spotting your bumper.

sec08-card-sec08-R11.question_text: How do hazard flashers and roadside warning devices pair up during a breakdown?
sec08-card-sec08-R11.teaching_text: Four-way flashers handle visible straightaways, while hills, curves, or fog within two hundred feet require deployed roadside markers.

sec08-card-sec08-F35.question_text: Which four actions must you complete before leaving a roadside vehicle unattended?
sec08-card-sec08-F35.teaching_text: Pulling the key and setting the brake prevents rollaways or theft while hazard lamps keep your dark shell visible.

sec08-card-sec08-F36.question_text: When can an officer order a parked vehicle towed, and who covers the towing and storage bill?
sec08-card-sec08-F36.teaching_text: Leaving a car in a prohibited or dangerous spot turns a quick stop into a costly impound lot pickup.

sec08-card-sec08-R12.question_text: If police tow your car from a banned or hazardous location, whose wallet pays towing and storage?
sec08-card-sec08-R12.teaching_text: Daily storage fees stack on top of hookup charges until the registered owner settles the bill.

sec07-card-sec07-F01.question_text: Which emergency vehicles require you to yield, and from which directions does that rule apply?
sec07-card-sec07-F01.teaching_text: Whether an ambulance closes from behind, oncoming, or a side street, clearing its path saves critical response seconds.

sec07-card-sec07-F02.question_text: Where must you steer and stop when an emergency warning sounds, and where must you never stop?
sec07-card-sec07-F02.teaching_text: Halting mid-box blocks wide fire ladders from turning onto cross streets even when your lane looks open.

sec07-card-sec07-F03.question_text: How long must you stay stopped after pulling over for an emergency vehicle?
sec07-card-sec07-F03.teaching_text: Pulling back out early risks cutting off a second trailing patrol car or fire chief unit running behind the first.

sec07-card-sec07-F04.question_text: Once an emergency vehicle passes your car, what minimum following distance must you maintain behind it?
sec07-card-sec07-F04.teaching_text: Fire trucks brake hard without warning at scene hydrants, and riding their draft endangers crews stepping off tailboards.

sec07-card-sec07-F05.question_text: How does a patrol officer signal that you are being pulled over?
sec07-card-sec07-F05.teaching_text: Checking your rearview mirror routinely lets you spot overhead strobes early before an officer needs the siren.

sec07-card-sec07-F06.question_text: Where do you pull over for a police stop, what do you do with the engine, and which two spots are off-limits?
sec07-card-sec07-F06.teaching_text: Stopping on a freeway center median traps the officer beside fast left-lane traffic, and shutting off the motor proves you will not bolt.

sec07-card-sec07-F07.question_text: Where should driver and passenger hands stay during a police stop, and how should everyone behave?
sec07-card-sec07-F07.teaching_text: Rummaging into a glovebox or under a seat looks threatening through tinted rear glass as an officer approaches.

sec07-card-sec07-F08.question_text: When do you reach for your license or registration at a stop, and when may you step out?
sec07-card-sec07-F08.teaching_text: Popping your door open unannounced puts you into moving traffic and raises immediate roadside safety tension.

sec07-card-sec07-F09.question_text: What extra interior step should you take right after stopping for police after dark?
sec07-card-sec07-F09.teaching_text: Illuminating the cabin before the officer walks up lets them see calm hands clearly instead of peering into pitch darkness.

sec07-card-sec07-F10.question_text: Why does the manual warn against arguing with an officer on the roadside?
sec07-card-sec07-F10.teaching_text: Roadside shoulders are noisy, hazardous places where tickets never get dismissed, whereas courtrooms exist specifically to hear challenges.

sec07-card-sec07-R07.question_text: What extra steps apply when police pull you over compared with yielding to a passing ambulance?
sec07-card-sec07-R07.teaching_text: A passing ambulance only needs a clear lane, whereas a traffic stop requires securing your ignition and cabin posture.

sec07-card-sec07-R08.question_text: Besides intersections, what additional highway area is off-limits when pulling over for police?
sec07-card-sec07-R08.teaching_text: Left-side highway medians force both you and the patrol cruiser to merge back out into the fastest lane afterward.

sec07-card-sec07-F11.question_text: Which color marks work-zone traffic controls, and what hazards operate right beside travel lanes?
sec07-card-sec07-F11.teaching_text: Bright orange warns instantly that road crews and heavy loaders are working feet from moving mirrors.

sec07-card-sec07-F12.question_text: How do penalties change inside an Oregon work zone, and who gets right-of-way priority?
sec07-card-sec07-F12.teaching_text: Higher financial stakes back up a simple human truth that highway workers have only safety vests between them and traffic.

sec07-card-sec07-F13.question_text: Which four tools guide traffic through a work zone, and what distinct jobs do orange signs and cones perform?
sec07-card-sec07-F13.teaching_text: Reading advance diamond warnings early keeps you from clipping channelizing barrels when lanes shift.

sec07-card-sec07-F14.question_text: Does a temporary work-zone speed limit turn off when crews go home for the night?
sec07-card-sec07-F14.teaching_text: Narrowed shoulders, drop-offs, and concrete barriers stay hazardous at midnight even when every crew truck has left.

sec07-card-sec07-F15.question_text: Which two roadside postings legally end a reduced work-zone speed limit?
sec07-card-sec07-F15.teaching_text: Guessing the zone is over just because orange barrels thin out triggers doubled speeding fines.

sec07-card-sec07-F16.question_text: What commonly stops traffic in two-lane work zones, and how do human flaggers communicate?
sec07-card-sec07-F16.teaching_text: Single-lane alternating closures rely on clear paddle and hand commands so opposing queues never meet head-on.

sec07-card-sec07-F17.question_text: What equipment makes up an automated flagger assistance device?
sec07-card-sec07-F17.teaching_text: Remote-controlled flagger trailers keep human crew members out of live rural traffic while controlling one-lane zones.

sec07-card-sec07-F18.question_text: Which light-and-arm combination means stop at an automated flagger, and which combination tells you to proceed?
sec07-card-sec07-F18.teaching_text: Proceeding cautiously on flashing yellow with the gate raised reminds you the lane ahead is still an active construction zone.

sec07-card-sec07-F19.question_text: How do lanes typically change inside a freeway work zone?
sec07-card-sec07-F19.teaching_text: Merging smoothly when advance arrows appear prevents last-second bottlenecks at the cone taper.

sec07-card-sec07-F20.question_text: Why must you drop speed and stay laser-focused inside freeway work zones?
sec07-card-sec07-F20.teaching_text: One glance at a dashboard screen in a narrowed concrete chute drifts tires straight into cones or workers.

sec07-card-sec07-F21.question_text: Why must you avoid tailing construction trucks inside a work zone?
sec07-card-sec07-F21.teaching_text: Following a dump truck turns you straight behind the cones into an active paving trench, and heavy haulers merge out slowly.

sec07-card-sec07-R09.question_text: Why does an empty-looking work zone still enforce its temporary speed limit?
sec07-card-sec07-R09.teaching_text: Permit tests love asking whether Sunday morning drivers can ignore orange speed signs when nobody is holding a shovel.

sec07-card-sec07-R10.question_text: Why shouldn't you wait for a green light at an automated flagger trailer?
sec07-card-sec07-R10.teaching_text: Waiting for a green lens that does not exist stalls the queue when the arm lifts and yellow flashes.

sec07-card-sec07-R11.question_text: How does traffic control in a two-lane work zone contrast with a freeway work zone?
sec07-card-sec07-R11.teaching_text: Two-lane highways must alternate directions past one open lane, whereas divided freeways squeeze traffic through narrow shifted chutes.

sec07-card-sec07-F22.question_text: What three actions should every railroad crossing sign or signal trigger immediately?
sec07-card-sec07-F22.teaching_text: Rolling down music volume and easing off the throttle ensures you can halt cleanly if a horn sounds.

sec07-card-sec07-F23.question_text: What is the job of a railroad advance warning sign?
sec07-card-sec07-F23.teaching_text: Curves and trees often hide rails until the last second, making early advance signs critical.

sec07-card-sec07-F24.question_text: Which regulatory sign pairs with a white railroad crossbuck, and what extra plaque appears at multi-track crossings?
sec07-card-sec07-F24.teaching_text: Reading the numbered plaque underneath tells you right away that one passing train could mask another rail.

sec07-card-sec07-F25.question_text: What warning hardware makes up an active railroad crossing signal system?
sec07-card-sec07-F25.teaching_text: Not every lighted crossing has drop arms, so alternating red lamps alone still command an immediate stop.

sec07-card-sec07-F26.question_text: What letters and shape are painted directly onto the lane ahead of a railroad crossing?
sec07-card-sec07-F26.teaching_text: Pavement markings catch low-beam headlights right where your eyes already track the asphalt.

sec07-card-sec07-F27.question_text: What space requirement on the far side must be met before your tires touch railroad tracks?
sec07-card-sec07-F27.teaching_text: Creeping onto rails behind stopped traffic traps your rear bumper across the path of an unstoppable locomotive.

sec07-card-sec07-F28.question_text: Which two risky choices at a railroad crossing must you never attempt?
sec07-card-sec07-F28.teaching_text: Locomotives weigh thousands of tons and win every tie against drivers gambling across the rails.

sec07-card-sec07-F29.question_text: Why do drivers misjudge approaching trains, and why can't engineers bail out a mistake?
sec07-card-sec07-F29.teaching_text: A massive locomotive appears to crawl down straight rails while closing highway speeds with a mile-long braking distance.

sec07-card-sec07-F30.question_text: Which three types of vehicles must stop at every railroad crossing even when no train is coming?
sec07-card-sec07-F30.teaching_text: Tailgating a yellow bus or fuel tanker toward silent tracks invites a rear-end crash when its brake lights flare.

sec07-card-sec07-F31.question_text: Why is charging across multi-track rails the instant the last caboose clears a classic trap?
sec07-card-sec07-F31.teaching_text: Boxcars form a solid moving wall that blocks sight and sound of a fast opposite-direction train on the next track.

sec07-card-sec07-R12.question_text: How does the legal meaning of a round railroad advance sign differ from the crossbuck assembly at the rails?
sec07-card-sec07-R12.teaching_text: The advance disk prepares your foot to brake, while the crossbuck post carries the enforceable yield or stop sign.

sec07-card-sec07-F32.question_text: Where do you stop for a railroad crossing with a painted stop line versus one without a line?
sec07-card-sec07-F32.teaching_text: Locomotives overhang wider than steel rails on both sides, so stopping closer than fifteen feet risks losing your front bumper.

sec07-card-sec07-F33.question_text: Which signal and train-sight conditions require a mandatory stop before the tracks?
sec07-card-sec07-F33.teaching_text: Even if electric flashers malfunction during a storm, seeing a locomotive closing in still commands an immediate halt.

sec07-card-sec07-F34.question_text: When must you come to a full stop at railroad tracks even if no train is anywhere in sight?
sec07-card-sec07-F34.teaching_text: Treating a red octagon at silent tracks like a yield sign earns the exact same violation as running an intersection stop.

sec07-card-sec07-F35.question_text: Is weaving around or ducking under a lowering or rising crossing gate ever legal?
sec07-card-sec07-F35.teaching_text: A rising arm can drop right back down if a second train triggers the track circuit seconds later.

sec07-card-sec07-F36.question_text: What must you confirm before rolling across tracks after a stop, especially where multiple tracks cross?
sec07-card-sec07-F36.teaching_text: Looking both ways across every set of rails prevents pulling straight into a second train hidden behind the first.

sec07-card-sec07-F37.question_text: What are your immediate first two priorities if a car stalls or gets stuck on railroad tracks?
sec07-card-sec07-F37.teaching_text: Trying to crank a dead starter wastes life-saving seconds because a silent train can round a curve before you hear it.

sec07-card-sec07-F38.question_text: Once everyone is clear of a blocked crossing, how do you alert the railroad to stop approaching trains?
sec07-card-sec07-F38.teaching_text: The Emergency Notification System plaque lists the exact crossing ID so dispatchers can halt locomotives miles upstream.

sec07-card-sec07-F39.question_text: Which exact direction and angle do you run if a train is bearing down on your stalled car?
sec07-card-sec07-F39.teaching_text: Impact hurls shattered car parts forward and outward along the train's travel direction like shrapnel.

sec07-card-sec07-R13.question_text: Between stop signs, red flashers, close trains, and flaggers, which one demands a stop on empty-looking tracks?
sec07-card-sec07-R13.teaching_text: Active lights, flaggers, and visible trains react to rail traffic, whereas a posted octagon commands every driver all day.

sec07-card-sec07-R14.question_text: When stalled on railroad tracks, how do escaping the car and calling the ENS number rank in order?
sec07-card-sec07-R14.teaching_text: Never sit inside a trapped cabin dialing your phone when getting bodies clear of steel rails comes first.

sec07-card-sec07-F40.question_text: How do streetcars and light rail trains operate on city streets?
sec07-card-sec07-F40.teaching_text: Unlike fenced freight corridors, urban rail glides quietly down shared asphalt lanes and halts frequently for riders.

sec07-card-sec07-F41.question_text: Who goes first between your car and a streetcar or light rail train, and when may you pass?
sec07-card-sec07-F41.teaching_text: Steel wheels on steel rails cannot swerve around your fender and take far longer to stop than rubber tires.

sec07-card-sec07-F42.question_text: What must you do behind a streetcar or train that has stopped to load or unload passengers?
sec07-card-sec07-F42.teaching_text: Commuters step directly off streetcar doors onto the travel lane expecting cars behind to wait.

sec07-card-sec07-R15.question_text: May you swing past a stopped streetcar just because it is halted to board riders?
sec07-card-sec07-R15.teaching_text: Swinging around a stationary streetcar puts your bumper straight through disembarking passengers.

sec07-card-sec07-F43.question_text: Where must you wait when approaching streetcar or light rail tracks at an intersection?
sec07-card-sec07-F43.teaching_text: Creeping past the white bar leaves your hood inside the sweeping overhang arc of turning rail cars.

sec07-card-sec07-F44.question_text: Where must your parked car sit on a street with streetcar tracks, with or without a white track line?
sec07-card-sec07-F44.teaching_text: A single mirror or tire overhanging the white clearance stripe halts an entire city transit line because trains cannot steer around you.

sec07-card-sec07-F45.question_text: What two checks must you make when parking and opening a car door near streetcar tracks?
sec07-card-sec07-F45.teaching_text: Quiet electric streetcars glide up silently and will shear an open driver's door clean off its hinges.

sec07-card-sec07-R01.question_text: May you turn across the path of a streetcar in the adjacent lane going your direction if it is currently stopped?
sec07-card-sec07-R01.teaching_text: A stopped transit operator watching boarding doors may accelerate smoothly on a white transit signal right as you cut left.

sec07-card-sec07-R02.question_text: What precautions apply before turning ahead of a train or crossing tracks at an intersection?
sec07-card-sec07-R02.teaching_text: Light rail vehicles run quietly in both directions, so slowing and checking left and right prevents broadside hits.

sec07-card-sec07-R04.question_text: What pedestrian behavior should you anticipate near streetcar and light rail stations?
sec07-card-sec07-R04.teaching_text: Late commuters fixate on closing train doors and sprint across lanes without glancing at oncoming bumpers.

sec07-card-sec07-R05.question_text: Why must you check behind for streetcars before changing lanes and avoid abrupt braking around them?
sec07-card-sec07-R05.teaching_text: Steel wheels glide silently into blind spots and need long braking distances when cars cut in and slam brakes.

sec07-card-sec07-R06.question_text: What should you do if your vehicle makes contact with a streetcar or train?
sec07-card-sec07-R06.teaching_text: Overhead power wires and coupled transit cars create electrical and mechanical hazards that trained personnel must assess first.

sec01-card-sec01-F01.question_text: On which two types of places in Oregon must you hold a valid driving privilege to operate a motor vehicle?
sec01-card-sec01-F01.teaching_text: Shopping-center lots and public parking garages require a valid privilege just like open state highways.

sec01-card-sec01-F02.question_text: Which specific class and type of driving privilege does the Oregon Driver Manual cover?
sec01-card-sec01-F02.teaching_text: Everyday passenger-car applicants study Class C rules without wading through heavy-rig endorsements.

sec01-card-sec01-R16.question_text: Can you rely on the Oregon Driver Manual to prepare for a commercial driver license?
sec01-card-sec01-R16.teaching_text: Commercial truck and bus operators need separate CDL handbooks because this guide sticks strictly to Class C.

sec01-card-sec01-F03.question_text: Which three areas does Oregon DMV evaluate when you apply for an original driving privilege?
sec01-card-sec01-F03.teaching_text: Checking eyesight, traffic-law recall, and behind-the-wheel control ensures new drivers handle streets safely.

sec01-card-sec01-F04.question_text: What payment and three personal proofs are required before starting each DMV test?
sec01-card-sec01-F04.teaching_text: Arriving without current home-address paperwork stops check-in before you ever reach a testing screen.

sec01-card-sec01-F05.question_text: How is your DMV test fee billed relative to other charges, and where are tests usually offered?
sec01-card-sec01-F05.teaching_text: Budgeting test fees separately from card issuance charges avoids payment surprises at the counter.

sec01-card-sec01-F36.question_text: How long must an applicant under eighteen hold an instruction permit before applying for an Oregon driver license?
sec01-card-sec01-F36.teaching_text: Six full months of supervised practice builds real-road instincts before teens ever drive solo.

sec01-card-sec01-R15.question_text: Who must complete the six-month permit-holding period before licensing, and who is exempt?
sec01-card-sec01-R15.teaching_text: Test distractors apply the six-month wait to everyone, whereas adult license applicants face no permit timer.

sec01-card-sec01-F06.question_text: What restriction appears on your driving privilege if you use glasses or contacts to pass the vision check?
sec01-card-sec01-F06.teaching_text: Passing the eye chart with lenses means driving without them later breaks your license restriction.

sec01-card-sec01-R08.question_text: How does wearing contact lenses or eyeglasses during DMV's eye screening change your privilege card?
sec01-card-sec01-R08.teaching_text: Keep spare glasses in the glovebox if you wear contacts, since your card mandates corrected sight.

sec01-card-sec01-F07.question_text: How much does Oregon's DMV vision screening cost, and what happens if you do not pass it?
sec01-card-sec01-F07.teaching_text: Instead of charging a fee or rejecting you forever, DMV refers you to an eye doctor.

sec01-card-sec01-R09.question_text: How does the vision screening differ from knowledge and drive tests in both price and failure result?
sec01-card-sec01-R09.teaching_text: Vision screening is free and routes failed results to an eye specialist rather than outright denial.

sec01-card-sec01-F08.question_text: Which subjects appear on the Class C knowledge test, and what single study source covers them all?
sec01-card-sec01-F08.teaching_text: Every single multiple-choice item pulls directly from the Oregon Driver Manual, making outside rumors unnecessary.

sec01-card-sec01-F09.question_text: How many multiple-choice questions are on the Class C knowledge test, and how many right answers pass?
sec01-card-sec01-F09.teaching_text: Hitting twenty-eight out of thirty-five means you can miss at most seven questions and still pass.

sec01-card-sec01-F10.question_text: What online and in-office options does Oregon give you for taking the Class C knowledge test?
sec01-card-sec01-F10.teaching_text: Testing twenty-four-seven on DMV2U saves an office trip, while offices handle appointments and standby walk-ins.

sec01-card-sec01-F11.question_text: Who are the only two groups permitted inside a DMV office knowledge-testing area?
sec01-card-sec01-F11.teaching_text: Friends, parents, and children wait outside the testing zone so every screen stays quiet and fair.

sec01-card-sec01-R04.question_text: How does Oregon's rule on authorized translators change between the office knowledge test and the road drive test?
sec01-card-sec01-R04.teaching_text: Translators can assist inside the office knowledge area, yet road tests allow only you and the examiner.

sec01-card-sec01-F12.question_text: How is an in-office knowledge test delivered, and what audio or headphone choices do you get?
sec01-card-sec01-F12.teaching_text: Bringing personal wired earbuds lets you listen to spoken questions comfortably on the touch-screen station.

sec01-card-sec01-F13.question_text: Which study materials or electronics are banned during the knowledge test, and what single paper aid may be approved?
sec01-card-sec01-F13.teaching_text: Pulling out notes, manuals, or smartphones ends your session, while staff can approve a plain paper dictionary.

sec01-card-sec01-R05.question_text: Which single reference item can enter an office knowledge test only with staff permission, unlike banned notes or devices?
sec01-card-sec01-R05.teaching_text: Always show a paper translation dictionary to staff beforehand instead of opening unapproved books mid-test.

sec01-card-sec01-F14.question_text: Which four actions during a knowledge test are treated as cheating by Oregon DMV?
sec01-card-sec01-F14.teaching_text: Even jotting quick scratch notes or glancing at a silenced phone triggers the full cheating penalty.

sec01-card-sec01-F17.question_text: Whom should an applicant contact to arrange a special accommodation on the knowledge test?
sec01-card-sec01-F17.teaching_text: Reaching out to your local branch ahead of time lets staff set up the right support smoothly.

sec01-card-sec01-F15.question_text: What happens to your test score and retest wait time if you are caught cheating on the knowledge test?
sec01-card-sec01-F15.teaching_text: Getting caught with a phone or notes locks you out of retesting anywhere for three full months.

sec01-card-sec01-F16.question_text: If you miss passing an office knowledge test honestly, when might you be able to try again?
sec01-card-sec01-F16.teaching_text: Busy branches may run out of open stations, while quieter offices can often seat a same-day retry.

sec01-card-sec01-R01.question_text: How does the wait after an honest office knowledge-test failure compare with the wait after cheating?
sec01-card-sec01-R01.teaching_text: Missing eight questions honestly may allow another try that afternoon, whereas cheating freezes testing ninety days.

sec01-card-sec01-F18.question_text: Which computer setup is required for Oregon's online knowledge test, and which mobile devices are blocked?
sec01-card-sec01-F18.teaching_text: Smartphones, iPads, and touchscreen tablets cannot run the proctored DMV2U knowledge session.

sec01-card-sec01-R06.question_text: Why does a touchscreen work for the knowledge test inside a DMV office yet fail for online testing at home?
sec01-card-sec01-R06.teaching_text: DMV booths run dedicated touch monitors, whereas home DMV2U requires a mouse, keyboard, and webcam.

sec01-card-sec01-F19.question_text: When does your webcam snap photos during an online knowledge test, and why?

sec01-card-sec01-R02.question_text: How do online knowledge retest limits compare with retesting inside a DMV office?

sec01-card-sec01-F22.question_text: Which core driving maneuvers does the drive test evaluate, and what role does the front-seat examiner play?

sec01-card-sec01-F23.question_text: When can Oregon DMV waive the behind-the-wheel drive test for someone moving in from another state?

sec01-card-sec01-R10.question_text: What two conditions on a new resident's out-of-state license qualify it for an Oregon drive-test waiver?

sec01-card-sec01-R11.question_text: What two requirements must a driver-education completion meet to waive Oregon's DMV drive test?

sec01-card-sec01-F25.question_text: Can you walk in for a drive test, and what happens if your car lacks current registration or insurance proof?

sec01-card-sec01-F26.question_text: Who may sit inside the vehicle during an Oregon DMV drive test?

sec01-card-sec01-F27.question_text: Which items must be removed, turned off, or cleared inside the cabin before your drive test starts?

sec01-card-sec01-F28.question_text: If you do not pass the behind-the-wheel drive test, what is the earliest you can take it again?

sec01-card-sec01-R03.question_text: Is a same-day retake ever permitted after failing an Oregon behind-the-wheel drive test?

sec01-card-sec01-F34.question_text: How do you schedule a DMV drive test, and how far ahead does DMV recommend booking?

sec01-card-sec01-F35.question_text: What scheduling perks can a certified Third Party drive tester offer, and what is the main tradeoff?
sec01-card-sec01-F35.teaching_text: Private certified testers often run weekend or evening road slots while charging their own higher fees.

sec01-card-sec01-R14.question_text: How does scheduling a drive test with a certified Third Party Tester compare with testing at a DMV office?
sec01-card-sec01-R14.teaching_text: You trade standard state pricing for faster availability or off-hour testing windows.

sec01-card-sec01-F29.question_text: What happens before you pull out for a drive test if your car fails the examiner's equipment check?

sec01-card-sec01-R12.question_text: Which two pre-drive problems force your drive test to be rescheduled before you steer a single foot?
sec01-card-sec01-R12.teaching_text: Both expired insurance paperwork and broken safety hardware cancel the road test right in the lot.

sec01-card-sec01-F30.question_text: Which six core mechanical and safety items must work on every test vehicle regardless of weather?

sec01-card-sec01-F31.question_text: What must be true of the passenger door, the passenger seat, and the vehicle's muffler for a drive test?
sec01-card-sec01-F31.teaching_text: Examiners will not climb across consoles, sit on loose seats, or ride over leaking exhaust fumes.

sec01-card-sec01-F32.question_text: What registration display, mirrors, and window sightlines must your test vehicle provide?
sec01-card-sec01-F32.teaching_text: Cracked windshields or cargo blocking rear glass keep the examiner from monitoring surrounding traffic.

sec01-card-sec01-F33.question_text: Which five additional items must work on your test vehicle whenever weather or light conditions demand them?
